title: fix(responses): include cache write tokens in usage details
body:
## Overview:

Responses API payloads were missing `usage.input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens`.
This PR includes the field in both non-streaming responses and streamed response events.

## Details:

- Added a small Responses serialization compatibility shim for `cache_write_tokens`.
- Defaults the field to `0` while preserving an existing value when one is available.
- Applies the same behavior to non-streaming and streaming Responses payloads.
- Keeps the optimized streaming serializer intact by processing only the small usage object when usage is present.
- Added focused regression coverage for both response modes.
- Updated the unary and streaming response snapshots.

## Where should the reviewer start?

- `lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/responses/mod.rs` - Shared usage compatibility helper and non-streaming serialization path.
- `lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/responses/stream_converter.rs` - Streaming usage serialization through `ResponseUsageForSpec`.
- `lib/llm/tests/responses_http_replay.rs`- Full HTTP regression coverage for non-streaming and streaming responses.

## Related Issues
- Related to ai-dynamo/frontend-crates#206
- Closes DIS-2925

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Responses usage data now consistently includes zero values for missing cache token details.
  * Fixed consistency between standard and streaming response usage payloads.

* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for unary and streaming responses to verify complete usage details.

title: fix(frontend): enable DeepSeek V4.1 images with aligned tool results
body:
## Overview

### Summary

DeepSeek V4.1 requests containing `image_url` blocks fail in Dynamo's pinned text-only renderer. This combines the published image-input renderer fix with media collection ordering: when assistant calls A then B but results arrive B then A, images and UUID cache references must follow the rendered A-then-B placeholders.

## Details

- Include Ace Eldeib's original commit `95f5434` from #15097, preserving its author and commit identity. It aligns tool-result media collection with the renderer, including model-name fallback and interleaved user images.
- Upgrade `dynamo-renderer` from 5.3.1 to 5.3.2 and its required shared `dynamo-protocols` dependency from 6.0.1 to 6.1.0.
- Regenerate the workspace, Python binding, and KVBM binding lockfiles with Cargo.
- Extend the existing DeepSeek V4.1 integration tests to cover interleaved text/images, URL and data-URL inputs, reasoning enabled/disabled, and UUID-only cached images in user/tool messages. Check that rendering preserves the original message content.

### Validation

- Combined head `262d772`: `cargo test --locked -p dynamo-llm --no-default-features --lib deepseek_v41` passed all 14 selected tests on macOS, including actual media collection and renderer-order parity.
- The following renderer-only and CI results were collected before integrating Ace's commit; they are not fresh CI results for the combined head.
- `cargo test --locked -p dynamo-llm --no-default-features --test deepseek_v41_renderer`: 3 passed on macOS.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo metadata --locked --no-deps --format-version 1`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Checked CODEOWNERS coverage for every changed file.
- GitHub CI on `ff54cabba7f1675b3972a226cea7a321751d93cc`: Rust tests and Clippy across the workspace/bindings/examples, pre-commit, DCO, CODEOWNERS, and the aggregate pre-merge check all passed.
- The deployment operator confirms that the container build has already been tested in production on NVIDIA H200. That validation predates this rebase; the exact combined head has not been rerun on H200 here.

The build emits an existing macOS unused-variable warning for `join_reuseport` in `lib/runtime/src/pipeline/network/quic_response.rs`.

### Integration and authorship

This branch now matches #15097 at `262d772`, with two commits: Ace Eldeib's ordering fix (`95f5434`) and thuanpham582002's renderer upgrade (`262d772`, cherry-picked by Ace). No author was rewritten and the renderer change is not duplicated. Maintainers can land the combined change through #15097; this PR can then be closed as superseded.

## Where should the reviewer start?

`lib/llm/src/preprocessor/deepseek_v41.rs`, its integration in `lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs`, then `Cargo.toml` and `lib/llm/tests/deepseek_v41_renderer.rs`.

## Related Issues

Closes #15168.

Related PRs: ai-dynamo/frontend-crates#254, #15030, #15097, #15152.

### Reviewer context

cc @rmccorm4 @alexeldeib for the published renderer integration and coordination with the tool-result media ordering fix.

title: docs(fern): lead nightly chips with the engine version
body: ## Overview: The nightly chip in both install selectors read the opposite way round from the stable chip. Stable shows the engine version on top with the Dynamo version beneath; nightly led with the Dynamo dev version and put `latest nightly` underneath, so the same row changed meaning depending on which channel you were on. Both selectors now lead with the engine version on every channel. ## Details: **Before → after** (SGLang, nightly): | | Row label | Chip | |---|---|---| | Before | `DYNAMO NIGHTLY` | **1.4.0.dev20260803** · latest nightly | | After | `SGLANG VERSION` | **0.5.18** · Dynamo 1.4.0.dev20260803 | Stable is unchanged and was already **0.5.16** · `Dynamo 1.4.1`. The row label loses its nightly special case for the same reason: it read "Dynamo nightly" while the chip below it now leads with an SGLang or vLLM version. Applied to `InstallSelector` (CLI quickstart) and `KubernetesContainerSelector` (Kubernetes quickstart), which carried the display logic verbatim — the point of the change is that the two agree. Entries with no Dynamo version keep their existing subtitle. The TensorRT-LLM nightly publishes no pinned wheel, so it still reads **1.3.0rc24** · `latest nightly`, and source builds still read `from main`. ## Where should the reviewer start? `docs/fern/components/InstallSelector.tsx` — the `displayVersion` / `displayMeta` pair. `KubernetesContainerSelector.tsx` gets the identical edit. ### Presentation only — two data problems are NOT fixed here Both are with the ops team; flagging so the diff isn't mistaken for a fix. **The engine version is the same across all three nightlies.** It comes from the single `MAIN_TOT` tip-of-main pin per backend (`sglang: 0.5.18`, `vllm: 0.27.1`), which is not recorded per nightly build — so the Aug 3 / Aug 2 / Jul 30 chips all show `0.5.18` even if those builds shipped different engine versions. Recording it per entry in `NIGHTLY_BUILDS` is the real fix. That list is also hand-maintained and its newest entry is Aug 3. **Kubernetes still offers only one nightly, and that is correct today.** Its command uses the floating `dynamo-planner:nightly` tag, and the operator CRD validates `runtimeVersionOverride` against `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`, so `1.4.0.dev20260802` would be rejected — all three nightlies would render an identical command. The CLI can offer three because *wheels* are published per date. ### Validation Rendered against a local `fern docs dev` server, exercised by clicking through the widget: - CLI nightly: `SGLang version` → `0.5.18 / Dynamo 1.4.0.dev20260803`, `…802`, `…730`; vLLM → `0.27.1 / …`. - Kubernetes nightly: `vLLM version` → `0.27.1 / Dynamo 1.4.0.dev20260803`. - TensorRT-LLM nightly (no Dynamo version in data) falls back to `1.3.0rc24 / latest nightly`. - Stable and source channels unchanged on both pages. - `fern check` 0 errors; `check_style_components.py` and `check_asset_paths.py` pass. ## Related Issues **🚫 This PR is NOT linked to an issue**: - [x] Confirmed — no related issue --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **Bug Fixes** - Version labels in installation and Kubernetes container selectors now consistently reflect the selected backend version, regardless of release channel. - Version metadata now prioritizes available Dynamo version information and clearly indicates source status, latest nightly builds, nightly dates, or fallback details. - Resolved inconsistent labeling that could incorrectly display “Dynamo nightly” for nightly channels.

title: fix(http): bound remote media downloads
body:
## Why

Dynamo fetches user-supplied remote media through shared HTTP clients, but response size was only known after buffering the complete body. Large or unbounded responses could therefore consume arbitrary memory before callers rejected them. Enforcing an optional limit inside both streaming clients keeps existing uncapped callers unchanged while giving media paths a reliable resource boundary, including across redirects.

## What Change

- Add opt-in response byte limits to both HTTP client implementations.
- Reject oversized headers and streaming bodies with a shared typed error.
- Revalidate limits after redirects.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    HttpClient <|-- AiohttpClient
    HttpClient <|-- HttpxClient
    AiohttpClient ..> HttpBodyTooLargeError : rejects oversized streams
    HttpxClient ..> HttpBodyTooLargeError : rejects oversized streams

    note for HttpClient "Defines the optional max-bytes contract"
    note for HttpBodyTooLargeError "Reports one backend-neutral limit failure"
```

## Test Plan

- Run focused aiohttp and httpx client tests.
- Run pre-commit on all changed files.

title: feat(video): support typed input references
body:
_Based on #13705._

## Why

The video API exposes only one untyped image reference, while vLLM-Omni pipelines can condition generation on image, video, and audio inputs. Dynamo needs a typed contract that preserves per-modality order, materializes remote media within request-level limits, and adapts singleton values to existing pipeline ABIs. Backends without this capability must reject the field instead of silently producing unconditioned video.

## What Change

- Add typed image, video, and audio references to Rust and Python protocols.
- Materialize validated references with count, byte, and cleanup boundaries.
- Scalarize generic singleton inputs and reject unsupported backend usage.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    NvCreateVideoRequest --> VideoReferenceMaterializer : supplies typed references
    VideoReferenceMaterializer --> OmniHandler : returns pipeline-ready paths
    OmniHandler --> OmniTextPrompt : attaches multimodal data

    note for VideoReferenceMaterializer "Bounds, stages, groups, and cleans request media"
    note for OmniHandler "Adapts references to the selected pipeline ABI"
```

## Test Plan

- Run Rust/Python video protocol and materializer tests.
- Run SGLang and TensorRT-LLM rejection tests.

title: feat(epp): add role-scoped worker catalogs for standalone disaggregated routing
body:
## Summary

Closes #13406 (DEP #11661, Milestone 5). With
`DYN_EPP_TOPOLOGY_MODE=disaggregated`, the standalone Rust EPP splits the pods selected by one
`InferencePool` into prefill and decode catalogs using a configurable worker-role label, and drives
two independent embedded `SelectionService` instances from them.

**Two instances, not one instance with two routing groups.** `use_kv_events` is fixed when a
`SelectionService` is built and differs per role, and the two catalogs must be disjoint so a decode
pick can never see a prefill worker. Everything else that separates the roles is *per-request*: the
decode selector carries the same `RouterConfigOverride` the Dynamo-runtime EPP applies to its decode
leg (`decode_router_config_override`, shared from `epp.rs`) and supplies it on every selection and
booking; prefill and aggregated carry none.

| | prefill | decode |
|---|---|---|
| static `use_kv_events` | base | `false` |
| static `router_predicted_ttl_secs` | base | cleared (needs events) |
| per-request `RouterConfigOverride` | none | `overlap_score_credit: 0.0`, `assume_kv_reuse: false`, `track_prefill_tokens: false` |

Prefill scores prefix overlap and does not model long-lived block occupancy; decode ignores overlap
and does model occupancy. A decode worker did not compute the prompt, so charging it prefill work
would mis-rank it, and crediting it for a prefix it never cached would be a fiction. Decode workers
therefore carry no `kv_events_endpoint` and no `replay_endpoint`, which is exactly what makes them
Schedulable under `use_kv_events=false`.

**Prefill is a selection input only.** All five reflector reads on the request path are scoped to the
serving role, and an empty decode catalog returns the new `PickError::RoleCatalogEmpty` (503)
instead of falling back to a prefill endpoint. `build_request_header_response` is the sole producer
of `x-gateway-destination-endpoint` and is reachable only through `pick()`, so scoping `pick()`
scopes the whole surface.

**Aggregated mode is unchanged.** The role label is never read, one catalog is built, and the
existing single-selector path runs byte-identically.

### Requirement-by-requirement

| # | Issue requirement | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Topology configuration + worker-role label contract | `epp_standalone_config.rs` — `EppTopologyMode`, `DYN_EPP_WORKER_ROLE_LABEL` (default `nvidia.com/dynamo-worker-role`), label-key syntax validation |
| 2 | Split eligible pool pods into prefill/decode sets | `pod_discovery.rs` — `raw_worker_from_pod` resolves the role after the existing eligibility gates |
| 3 | Role-scoped catalogs, KV-event inputs, readiness, selector config | `pod_discovery.rs` (`IndexState`/`RoleCounts`), `role_config.rs`, `selector.rs`, `topology_adapter.rs` |
| 4 | Prefill never selected as a destination | `epp_router.rs` `serving_role`, `picker.rs` `RoleCatalogEmpty`, `server.rs` 503 mapping |
| 5 | Unit + integration coverage | 18 net new test functions over `main` (table-style; 161 in the crate) across role changes, missing/invalid labels, add/remove reconciliation, and the routing invariant |

### New environment variables

`DYN_EPP_TOPOLOGY_MODE`, `DYN_EPP_WORKER_ROLE_LABEL`, and two per-role capacity overrides
(`DYN_EPP_{PREFILL,DECODE}_MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS`) that fall back to the shared value. Real P/D
fleets differ by 8–16× here, and `max_num_batched_tokens` is the denominator of
`PolicyClassConfig::worker_is_busy`. Per-role KV-block totals are deliberately not added: nothing in
this split consumes distinct totals yet.

Two configurations are rejected at startup rather than silently reinterpreted: `DYN_EPP_PEER_SERVICE`
with `disaggregated` (both instances would bind the one hardcoded `replica-agg` port; Milestone 8 /
#13418 owns multi-replica disagg), and `DYN_ROUTER_CONDITIONAL_DISAGG` (it requires decode-side KV
events and bypass orchestration `SelectionService` does not perform).
`DYN_EPP_TOPOLOGY_MODE` is standalone-only configuration like its siblings; the Dynamo-runtime mode
ignores it.

### DEP #11661 corrections this surfaced

- The two per-role `max_num_batched_tokens` env vars are missing from the Environment Contract.
- The role label key is now `nvidia.com/dynamo-worker-role`; the DEP says `nvidia.com/role` in four places.
- `DYN_EPP_KV_EVENT_PORT` / `DYN_EPP_KV_EVENT_REPLAY_PORT` apply to prefill only under disaggregated.
- Decode workers have no `kv_events_endpoints` and no `replay_endpoint`.
- `DYN_EPP_WORKER_ROLE_LABEL` is optional-with-default, not "Conditional" required.
- Conditional disaggregation is rejected by the standalone EPP; the DEP marks it "Needs design".

### Deliberately not in this change

Owned by the sibling issues: prefill/decode pair selection and reservation (#13407), the
decode-sidecar request contract (#13405), NIXL handoff (#13404), and manifests / e2e / benchmarking
(#13408). Per-role policy and queue configuration is recorded against #13407; metrics are
Milestone 9. Until #13405 and #13407 land the prefill catalog is populated but nothing selects from
it, so the EPP logs that at startup and the docs carry the same note.
## Validation

* `cargo fmt -p dynamo-ext-proc -- --check`
* `cargo clippy -p dynamo-ext-proc --all-targets -- -D warnings`
* `cargo test -p dynamo-ext-proc` — **161 passed, 0 failed**
* Focused areas: worker role (9), per-role router config (10), standalone config (18 new), pod
  discovery (14 new), topology adapter (3 new), plus the existing aggregated suite unchanged

============

## Kubernetes Validation Summary

> Revision 1 run. The revision-2 rerun (new label key, override refactor, guard removal) is in the
> follow-up comment below.

Tested on a real Kubernetes cluster — throwaway k3s v1.34.2 in Docker, Gateway API v1.5.1 + GAIE
CRDs v1.2.1 + agentgateway v1.0.0 — installed with **this repo's own documented procedure**,
`deploy/inference-gateway/scripts/install_gaie_crd_agentgateway.sh` per
[Install Gateway API Inference Extension](docs/fern/pages/kubernetes/installation/gateway-api-routing.mdx).

GPU-less setup: the workers are `traefik/whoami` echo servers carrying the `nvidia.com/role` label,
and the EPP runs off-cluster against the same API server with a stub standing in for vLLM's
`/v1/chat/completions/render`. Everything the gateway itself touches — `InferencePool`, `HTTPRoute`,
the EPP `Service` — is exactly what `deploy/inference-gateway/ext-proc/examples/onramp/agg.yaml`
ships. Echo workers are enough here because this issue is about *which* endpoint the EPP hands the
gateway, not about what the endpoint computes.

* **Role split from one InferencePool** — 2 prefill + 2 decode pods, two `SelectionService`
  instances, two policy classes, independent readiness per role.
* **KV events are prefill-only** — ZMQ listeners start for the prefill pod IPs and no others, and
  follow the label across role changes.
* **The gateway never receives a prefill endpoint** — 100/100 requests landed on decode-role pods,
  cross-checked against each pod's live label.
* **Empty decode catalog fails closed** — `503 no decode workers available` instead of falling back
  to a prefill endpoint.
* **Live role changes reconcile** — flips in both directions, label removal, and an unparseable
  label value, each with an attributable log line.
* **Aggregated mode is unchanged** — same pool, same labels, one catalog, all pods serving.

### Step 1: install the gateway with the documented script

```
$ NAMESPACE=epp-disagg AGW_NAMESPACE=agentgateway-system \
    ./deploy/inference-gateway/scripts/install_gaie_crd_agentgateway.sh
...
agentgatewayparameters.agentgateway.dev/inference-gateway-params serverside-applied
gateway.gateway.networking.k8s.io/inference-gateway created
gateway.gateway.networking.k8s.io/inference-gateway condition met

$ kubectl get gatewayclass
NAME           CONTROLLER                      ACCEPTED   AGE
agentgateway   agentgateway.dev/agentgateway   True       12s

$ kubectl get gateway inference-gateway -n agentgateway-system
NAME                CLASS          ADDRESS   PROGRAMMED   AGE
inference-gateway   agentgateway             True         10s
```

### Step 2: apply the disaggregated workload

```
$ kubectl -n epp-disagg get pods -o custom-columns='NAME:.metadata.name,IP:.status.podIP,ROLE:.metadata.labels.nvidia\.com/role,READY:...'
NAME                            IP          ROLE      READY
vllm-decode-944754ff7-f87cw     10.42.0.9   decode    True
vllm-decode-944754ff7-pnsls     10.42.0.8   decode    True
vllm-prefill-68cb66cf4d-kxwbl   10.42.0.7   prefill   True
vllm-prefill-68cb66cf4d-ljtnm   10.42.0.6   prefill   True

$ kubectl -n epp-disagg get httproute vllm-qwen-route -o jsonpath=...
agentgateway.dev/agentgateway Accepted=True ResolvedRefs=True
```

### Step 3: EPP startup — two catalogs, and ZMQ only for prefill 🔥

Prefill pods are `10.42.0.6` and `10.42.0.7`; decode pods are `10.42.0.8` and `10.42.0.9`. Only the
prefill pair gets a KV-event subscription, which is the whole point of `use_kv_events=false` and
`kv_events_endpoint: None` on the decode role.

```
INFO dynamo_ext_proc::runner: Listening for ext_proc connections (TLS) addr=0.0.0.0:9002
INFO dynamo_ext_proc::pod_discovery: Role has ready workers role="prefill" ready=2
INFO dynamo_ext_proc::pod_discovery: Role has ready workers role="decode" ready=2
INFO ...indexer::listener: ZMQ listener starting worker_id=6967477426482853 endpoint="tcp://10.42.0.6:5557"
INFO ...indexer::listener: ZMQ listener starting worker_id=1819057378898784 endpoint="tcp://10.42.0.7:5557"
WARN dynamo_ext_proc::epp_router: DYN_EPP_TOPOLOGY_MODE=disaggregated is incomplete until
     ai-dynamo/dynamo#13405 and #13407 land: the prefill catalog is populated but nothing selects
     from it yet, so decode workers still perform the whole prefill
```

### Step 4: end-to-end request through the gateway

The echo worker reflects the headers it received, so the EPP's decision is visible in the response
body itself.

```
$ curl -i http://<gateway>/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello world from the gateway"}]}'
HTTP/1.1 200 OK

Hostname: vllm-decode-944754ff7-pnsls
IP: 10.42.0.8
RemoteAddr: 10.42.0.5:54164
POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1
X-Gateway-Destination-Endpoint: 10.42.0.8:8000
```

### Step 5: 100 requests, destinations cross-checked against live role labels 🔥

Run after several role flips, so two pods carry a name from the opposite Deployment. Routing follows
the **label**, not the name — which is what the issue asks for.

```
$ kubectl -n epp-disagg get pods -o custom-columns='NAME,IP,ROLE'
vllm-prefill-68cb66cf4d-kxwbl   10.42.0.7    decode
vllm-decode-944754ff7-qv4p5     10.42.0.12   decode
vllm-decode-944754ff7-zvlzm     10.42.0.13   decode
vllm-prefill-68cb66cf4d-ljtnm   10.42.0.6    prefill
vllm-decode-944754ff7-nx6hq     10.42.0.11   prefill
vllm-prefill-68cb66cf4d-rk75z   10.42.0.10   prefill

$ # 100 requests; tally X-Gateway-Destination-Endpoint against the live label
40 requests -> 10.42.0.12 role=decode
31 requests -> 10.42.0.13 role=decode
29 requests -> 10.42.0.7 role=decode
```

**0 of 100 reached a prefill-role pod.** Same result on the earlier 60-request runs.

### Step 6: drain decode, prefill still Ready

The decode pods are confirmed gone from the API server, not merely terminating, and the pool still
holds two eligible Ready prefill pods — so this is an empty *role catalog*, not an empty pool.

```
$ kubectl -n epp-disagg scale deploy/vllm-decode --replicas=0
$ kubectl -n epp-disagg wait --for=delete pod -l nvidia.com/role=decode --timeout=90s
pod/vllm-decode-944754ff7-f87cw condition met
pod/vllm-decode-944754ff7-pnsls condition met

$ kubectl -n epp-disagg get pods
vllm-prefill-68cb66cf4d-kxwbl   prefill   Running
vllm-prefill-68cb66cf4d-ljtnm   prefill   Running

$ curl -i http://<gateway>/v1/chat/completions -d '{...}'
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
content-length: 27

no decode workers available
```

The EPP confirms the same thing independently: both decode workers are removed from the decode
selector, and the request that follows produces **no `Selected worker` and no `Request routed`
line** — `pick()` short-circuits on `has_ready_workers(Decode)` before it ever reaches the selector,
which is exactly `PickError::RoleCatalogEmpty(Decode)`.

```
06:09:34.352529 WARN ...sequences::multi_worker: Removing worker WorkerWithDpRank { worker_id: 4220446411653535 }  # 10.42.0.8
06:09:34.353019 WARN ...pod_discovery: Role has no ready workers; requests needing it will fail
                     until one appears role="decode"
06:09:34.353328 WARN ...sequences::multi_worker: Removing worker WorkerWithDpRank { worker_id: 6957111713067280 }  # 10.42.0.9

06:09:38.028162 DEBUG ...server: Received RequestHeaders from Envoy
06:09:38.028270 DEBUG ...server: Received RequestBody from Envoy body_len=83
06:09:38.028292 DEBUG ...server: Received RequestBody from Envoy eos=true
                       # no Selected worker, no Request routed -- compare Step 4
```

Deleting the pods leaves one confound: it does not separate "the decode catalog is empty" from "the
pod is not there". Step 8's label removal closes that — the pod stays Running, Ready and
pool-selected, and only its role label goes away, reaching the identical 503 through a completely
different path.

Fails closed with an attributable body, rather than falling back to a prefill endpoint.

### Step 7: live role changes

`prefill → decode`: the pod moves catalogs in place, starts serving immediately, and its KV-event
subscription is torn down.

```
$ kubectl -n epp-disagg label pod vllm-prefill-68cb66cf4d-kxwbl nvidia.com/role=decode --overwrite
Hostname: vllm-prefill-68cb66cf4d-kxwbl      # x3, it is now the only decode worker
```
```
INFO ...indexer::listener: ZMQ listener exiting after cancellation self.worker_id=1819057378898784
```

`decode → prefill`: the pod stops receiving traffic and gains a subscription.

```
$ kubectl -n epp-disagg label pod vllm-decode-944754ff7-nx6hq nvidia.com/role=prefill --overwrite
$ # 30 requests
     11 vllm-decode-944754ff7-zvlzm
     10 vllm-decode-944754ff7-qv4p5
      9 vllm-prefill-68cb66cf4d-kxwbl     # nx6hq: 0
```
```
INFO ...indexer::listener: ZMQ listener starting worker_id=8935336512433373 endpoint="tcp://10.42.0.11:5557"
```

### Step 8: missing and invalid role labels

```
$ kubectl label pod ... nvidia.com/role-                       -> 503 no decode workers available
$ kubectl label pod ... nvidia.com/role=encode --overwrite     -> 503 no decode workers available
$ kubectl label pod ... nvidia.com/role=decode --overwrite     -> 200
```
```
WARN ...pod_discovery: Pod is pool-selected and Ready but has no usable worker role; excluding it
     pod="vllm-prefill-68cb66cf4d-kxwbl" reason="role_label_missing" error=role label is missing
WARN ...pod_discovery: Pod is pool-selected and Ready but has no usable worker role; excluding it
     pod="vllm-prefill-68cb66cf4d-kxwbl" reason="role_label_invalid"
     error=role label value "encode" names no worker role
```

Startup never fails on this — a rolling update transiently produces such pods.

### Step 9: a client cannot force a prefill endpoint

In GAIE the EPP answers the gateway with an `x-gateway-destination-endpoint` header and the gateway
forwards there. So the cheapest way to defeat requirement #4 needs no bug in the catalog logic at
all: the **client** sets that header itself and names a prefill pod. `envoy_helpers.rs:54-58` argues
this cannot work — the header is deliberately kept out of `STRIPPED_REQUEST_HEADERS` because the EPP
writes it with `OverwriteIfExistsOrAdd`, which already replaces any client value, and stripping it
as well would make the outcome depend on Envoy's set-vs-remove ordering. This step checks that
argument against a real gateway.

Each row is one `curl` carrying a forged header. Pod names are unreliable after Step 7's flips, so
both role columns are the **live label**, which is what actually decides.

| forged header the client sent | role of *that* pod | endpoint the EPP returned | pod that served the request | role of *that* pod |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `10.42.0.6:8000` | `prefill` | `10.42.0.11:8000` | `vllm-decode-944754ff7-nx6hq` | `decode` |
| `10.42.0.10:8000` | `prefill` | `10.42.0.7:8000` | `vllm-prefill-68cb66cf4d-kxwbl` | `decode` |

The two role columns are the test's precondition and its assertion:

* **Column 2 must be `prefill`.** Forging a decode IP would prove nothing — override and no-override
  produce the same landing pod, so the test would have no discriminating power.
* **Column 5 must be `decode`.** That is the pass condition. Had the spoof worked, the response
  would have come from `vllm-prefill-…-ljtnm` or `vllm-prefill-…-rk75z`, the two pods actually
  labelled `prefill` at that moment.

Row 2 is why names cannot be trusted: `vllm-prefill-…-kxwbl` reads like a prefill pod but was
flipped to `decode` in Step 7, and the Deployment name never changed.

```
06:11:24.061149 INFO ...selector: Selected worker worker_id=8935336512433373
06:11:24.061409 INFO ...server: Request routed endpoint=10.42.0.11:8000
06:11:24.061449 DEBUG ...envoy_helpers: [FINAL-MUTATION] set_headers
                key=x-gateway-destination-endpoint value=10.42.0.11:8000 append_action=2

06:11:24.109389 INFO ...selector: Selected worker worker_id=1819057378898784
06:11:24.109524 INFO ...server: Request routed endpoint=10.42.0.7:8000
06:11:24.109550 DEBUG ...envoy_helpers: [FINAL-MUTATION] set_headers
                key=x-gateway-destination-endpoint value=10.42.0.7:8000 append_action=2
```

`append_action=2` is `OverwriteIfExistsOrAdd`. What this run establishes is the end-to-end property
— a client-supplied value does not change the destination. It does not distinguish whether the
forged header was dropped before ext_proc or overwritten after it, and it does not need to.

### Step 10: aggregated parity, same cluster and same labels

Restart the EPP with `DYN_EPP_TOPOLOGY_MODE` unset against the identical pool. The role label is
never read, all 6 pods form one catalog, all 6 get KV-event listeners, all 6 serve.

```
INFO dynamo_ext_proc::pod_discovery: Role has ready workers role="aggregated" ready=6
INFO ...indexer::listener: ZMQ listener starting endpoint="tcp://10.42.0.6:5557"
INFO ...indexer::listener: ZMQ listener starting endpoint="tcp://10.42.0.7:5557"
INFO ...indexer::listener: ZMQ listener starting endpoint="tcp://10.42.0.10:5557"
INFO ...indexer::listener: ZMQ listener starting endpoint="tcp://10.42.0.11:5557"
INFO ...indexer::listener: ZMQ listener starting endpoint="tcp://10.42.0.12:5557"
INFO ...indexer::listener: ZMQ listener starting endpoint="tcp://10.42.0.13:5557"
```
```
$ # 60 requests
     14 vllm-prefill-68cb66cf4d-kxwbl
     14 vllm-decode-944754ff7-zvlzm
     12 vllm-decode-944754ff7-qv4p5
      8 vllm-prefill-68cb66cf4d-ljtnm
      8 vllm-decode-944754ff7-nx6hq
      4 vllm-prefill-68cb66cf4d-rk75z
```

### Not covered by this run

Real vLLM workers, real KV-cache events (the ZMQ sockets connect but no worker publishes), NIXL
transfer, and prefill/decode pairing — pairing is #13407 and is what makes the prefill catalog do
anything, so it cannot be exercised until that lands. Multi-replica EPP under `disaggregated` is
rejected at startup and is Milestone 8 (#13418).

title: feat(epp): register shared router metrics without DRT
body:
## Summary

Expose the existing `dynamo_component_router_*` request metrics from standalone EPP without constructing a DRT. The EPP registers only the three families it can observe, reducing the work and payload of each `/metrics` scrape. The existing DRT/component constructor still registers the full set with unchanged names, labels, buckets, and observations.

The EPP records admitted selections and input tokens after `select_and_reserve`, and output tokens only when the backend reports `usage.completion_tokens` (including zero). It does not infer router TTFT, ITL, KV overlap, or completion counts from response byte chunks. Request-boundary metrics and phase timing remain in #15056.

## Details

- Add `RouterRequestMetrics::from_registry(registry, prefix, const_labels)` and a filtered `from_registry_subset` using the same metric definitions; cover schema compatibility and registry isolation.
- Register `requests_started_total`, `input_sequence_tokens`, and `output_sequence_tokens` with deployment-bound `model` and `inference_pool` labels on the EPP's existing private `/metrics` registry; test real gRPC observation paths and coexistence with `dynamo_epp_cached_tokens`.
- Document exactly which router families appear on the EPP endpoint. Families without an EPP observation source are absent rather than exporting misleading zero series.

The shared `dynamo_component_router_*` name follows the proposed reuse direction in #15058. The design discussion still has an open concern about whether an EPP-specific prefix would better distinguish observer semantics; this draft leaves that decision visible for review. Worker-state gauges, JSONL/config parity, and `picks_inflight` are outside this change.

## Validation

- `dynamo-ext-proc` full library suite: 162 passed.
- `dynamo-llm` new subset schema test passed; full workspace Rust tests passed in PR CI.
- Live-model E2E: a local ext_proc gRPC request selected a worker, invoked a CUDA TinyLlama backend through an API-compatible HTTP fixture, and recorded the backend's 19 prompt and 8 completion tokens in the private registry. Kubernetes discovery was a fixture; the model was read from an existing local cache.
- PR CI: 26 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed. Rust formatting check and `git diff --check` passed. Docs lint passed with 0 errors (8 existing warnings).

The scrape benchmark used the same model/pool labels and one observation in each populated family. It interleaved full and EPP-subset registries in eight ABBA blocks, with 50 warmups and 500 timed `Registry::gather` plus `TextEncoder::encode` samples per variant per block (4,000 timed samples each). Results on the same Linux x86_64 debug build:

| Metric | Full 12 families | EPP 3 families | Improvement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Scrape encode mean | 427.1 µs | 72.8 µs | 5.86× faster |
| Scrape encode p50 | 419.6 µs | 72.7 µs | 5.77× faster |
| Scrape encode p95 | 438.0 µs | 74.5 µs | 5.88× faster |
| Encoded response size | 21,695 B | 3,710 B | 5.85× smaller |

This measures the router families' gather/encode work, not HTTP transport or request routing. The earlier routing benchmark compared `6fad666a` (baseline) with `e073161f` (registry implementation) using the same selector and fake HTTP renderer, with 100 warmups and six timed runs per revision, 1,000 pick/completion pairs per run, interleaved ABBA. Median-of-runs results:

| Metric | Baseline | Registry implementation | Comparison |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Routing throughput | 1,029.95 requests/s | 1,032.86 requests/s | 1.003× |
| Per-request p50 | 953.59 µs | 960.05 µs | 0.993× |
| Per-request p95 | 990.03 µs | 990.31 µs | 1.000× |

Those routing differences are within run-to-run variation. The subset change targets scrape performance and does not add a request-path optimization. The routing benchmark uses a mock renderer, not live-model throughput.

## Where should the reviewer start?

`lib/llm/src/kv_router/metrics.rs` for the shared constructors, then `deploy/inference-gateway/ext-proc/src/metrics.rs` and `epp_router.rs` for EPP registration and observations.

## Related Issues

- Relates to #15058

title: fix(recipes): K-EXAONE 2.0 review follow-ups — Fern-only docs, IB component, image and resource hygiene
body:
Follow-up to the best-practices review on #14822, plus the two review comments from the launch
thread. Everything here is verified on 8x B200 — see Validation.

## Related Issues

Relates to #14822

## Fixed

**Documentation is now Fern-only** (review 23, 25)
- `recipes/k-exaone-2.0/README.md` collapsed 295 -> 20 lines: a pointer to the rendered page plus
  the variant table. The three notes that existed only in the README — the supported-features
  table, KV-aware routing scale-out behaviour, and the absence of a cache-clearing endpoint —
  were migrated into the Fern page so nothing was lost.
- Manifest headers and in-body comments trimmed to the correctness constraints a reader cannot
  infer from the flag name. The internal tuning narrative (block-size and TP sweeps, prefix-reuse
  analysis) is gone.

**InfiniBand config moved out of the base** (review 3)
- `rdma/shared_ib`, `UCX_TLS` and `NCCL_IB_DISABLE` now live in
  `kustomize/components/ib`; the base carries no fabric configuration at all. This is cluster
  networking, not model configuration.
- The rendered manifest is renamed `deploy-generic.yaml` -> **`deploy-ib.yaml`**, so it is clear
  the fabric settings are pre-injected and a reader does not layer their own on top. It also
  stops colliding with the meaning `deploy-generic.yaml` already carries elsewhere in this repo,
  where it is the render with *no* provider networking.
- No generic render is shipped for the disaggregated target: without an RDMA resource that
  configuration is untested here, and an unvalidated manifest is worse than none.

**Images pinned by digest** (review 15)
- Both images pinned to their multi-arch **index** digest, tag retained for readability. A
  `-post.N` tag is mutable and a recipe is a reproduction claim.

**Resource requests declared** (review 20, 21, 22)
- Workers: `cpu: 16`, `ephemeral-storage: 64Gi`.
- Frontend: `cpu: 8`, `memory: 16Gi`, `ephemeral-storage: 16Gi` — it previously had none, and a
  frontend pulling an image with no ephemeral-storage request is how a CPU node ran out of disk
  during this recipe's bring-up.
- `sharedMemorySize` 40Gi -> 64Gi, and the duplicate `dshm` `emptyDir` removed (the operator
  already provides `/dev/shm`; verified as a 64G tmpfs in the running container).
- The `480Gi` memory limit dropped, leaving requests only. GPU and `rdma/shared_ib` stay in
  `limits`, where extended resources are required.

**Security context** (review 4, 5)
- `runAsGroup: 0` alongside `runAsUser: 0` on all three workers.
- `SYS_PTRACE` added to the aggregated worker. The two variants disagreed — disagg had all three
  capabilities, agg had `[IPC_LOCK, SYS_RESOURCE]` — so this was a slip, not a choice.

**`imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent`** on every container (review 16).

**Benchmark doc correction** — the note claimed the shipped `perf.yaml` sends a fresh
`cache_salt` per run. It does not; its only `--extra-inputs` value is `ignore_eos:true`, so
successive concurrency points inherited the previous point's prefix cache. Now states what the
job actually does and keeps the restart requirement, matching `perf/README.md`.

## Deliberately not changed

- **`runtimeVersionOverride` is kept** (review 18). The operator cannot parse a version out of a
  digest-pinned reference, and the merged `ax-k2` recipe ships the same tag shape and keeps the
  override. Dropping it breaks the deployment.
- **The frontend stays on `dynamo-frontend:1.4.1`** rather than the worker image (review 17). It
  is CPU-only and loads no weights; the model-specific runtime is far larger, and pulling it onto
  a CPU frontend node previously exhausted ephemeral storage.
- **Frontend requests are `cpu 8 / 16Gi`, not the reviewed `16 / 128Gi`.** Two conventions exist
  in this repo — `4-8 CPU / 16Gi` (nemotron-3-ultra, gpt-oss-120b) and `16 / 128Gi`
  (solar-open2-250b). The latter assumes fat CPU nodes: on a cluster whose CPU nodes are 32 core
  / 63Gi it is unschedulable, and because the operator gang-schedules, the frontend alone holds
  the workers `Pending` too. Caught in validation.

## Deferred

The portable-contract items (`shared-model-cache` naming and mount path, frontend cache mount,
exec-form `command`, DGD naming convention) change mount paths and service names, so each needs
its own validation run. They are deliberately left for a separate PR so this one stays reviewable
and does not invalidate the validation already done on the merged recipe.

## Validation

Both variants deployed from the rendered manifests on 8x B200 and smoke-tested after every
behavioural change:

- Coherence on three prompt shapes including Korean; tool calling returns `finish_reason:
  tool_calls`; `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS` confirmed selected in the worker log.
- Disaggregated KV transfer over IB RDMA confirmed by `vllm:nixl_xfer_time_seconds` — sub-millisecond
  to low-millisecond means, cross-node.
- All environment variables read back from the **running container**, confirming the Kustomize
  component merges into `spec.env` rather than replacing it.
- Digest-pinned images, resource requests and the 64G `/dev/shm` all verified on running pods.

Depends on #15064 for the `spec.env` merge key, which is merged.

title: fix(trtllm): normalize multimodal KV events
body:
## Summary

- normalize TensorRT-LLM V2 multimodal KV events into the same routing-token representation used by requests
- consume the frontend routing identity from the additive `mm_keys[].uuid` field introduced by NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#19529 while retaining `mm_keys[].hash` as the content digest
- fail closed on missing or malformed block-local multimodal metadata, including invalid token-ID types, while allowing later events to continue
- use TensorRT-LLM's `resolve_vocab_size()` for the continuation-token offset
- pin the forward fixture to the exact TensorRT-LLM #19529 serializer contract and retain a separately labeled legacy fixture
- distinguish text-prefix-only router matches from full text-and-image matches in TensorRT-LLM end-to-end tests

## Validation

- latest commit-time pre-commit hooks passed
- latest focused TensorRT-LLM publisher, image-token-resolver, and cached-token payload tests — 86 passed
- TensorRT-LLM `resolve_vocab_size()` smoke check for Qwen3-VL — `151936`
- TensorRT-LLM V1 multimodal routing E2E — passed with a repeated-request router hit rate of `0.909`
- TensorRT-LLM V2 multimodal routing E2E against NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#19529 — passed with the strict full-match threshold (`router_kv_hit_rate > 0.5`) before the review-only follow-up

The latest follow-up could not be rerun through the model E2E because the retained validation image's compiled Dynamo core predates the checked-out frontend API; both attempts stopped before server startup. The valid event output remains covered by the focused identity and publisher-path tests above.

## Notes

This PR depends on the exact NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM#19529 event contract pinned by the fixture at `687d95a29106e642d3f38b81ae193ac5d0aa6ee2`. Dynamo intentionally decodes that fixed serialized shape without compatibility branches for hypothetical future formats. No TensorRT-LLM changes are part of this follow-up.

The request and event paths use the same frontend identity: Dynamo forwards the 16-hex routing hash as `multi_modal_uuids`; TensorRT-LLM preserves it in `mm_keys[].uuid`; Dynamo converts that UUID to the canonical multimodal pad token. The content digest remains in `mm_keys[].hash` for block-local validation. Cross-block item consistency remains TensorRT-LLM's responsibility.

`gen_multimodal_cache_key_tokens()` is intentionally not used: it generates producer-side cache-key tokens from an unexpanded multimodal item, while Dynamo consumes already-expanded serialized event tokens and must recover their block positions.

title: feat(model-protection): add protected model loading
body:
## Summary

  - Add Phase 1 protected-model loading for Dynamo/vLLM.
  - Preserve the existing plain-model path: plain Hugging Face models bypass key, license, TPM, crypto, and tmpfs handling.
  - Add protected-package verification, signed manifest/license validation, TPM-bound key recovery, AES-256-GCM shard decryption, and tmpfs-only plaintext materialization.
  - Integrate the resolved protected model path with the vLLM backend and clean up decrypted files after use.
  - Add a protected image build profile, packaging/issuance tools, deployment examples, and English operator documentation.

  ## Security properties

  - No encryption key or signing private key is committed to source, image, or runtime configuration.
  - Protected packages fail closed on invalid signatures, invalid license, machine mismatch, missing key material, integrity failure, or unsafe tmpfs/runtime policy.
  - A copied protected package cannot run on a different machine without its TPM-bound key material and valid license.
  - Plaintext model shards are materialized only in the configured tmpfs workspace.

  ## Validation

  - `components/src/dynamo/vllm/tests/test_model_protection_bootstrap.py`
    - 18 passed, 2 skipped.
    - The skipped cases require vLLM 0.29; the local environment has vLLM 0.28.
  - `git diff --check` passed.
  - Rust packager tests passed before the final main update; the current local offline cache cannot resolve a locked `aisimulate-core` dependency, so full Rust validation should run in CI.

  ## Follow-up validation before production enablement

  - Build and test the protected image with vLLM 0.29.
  - Run an end-to-end protected LFM model load through TPM → tmpfs → vLLM → GPU.
  - Validate failure paths: copied package, invalid license, TPM/machine mismatch, tampered shard, and tmpfs cleanup.

## Summary

An opted-in request now enters the normal policy queue and participates in class, deadline, priority, DRR, and worker eligibility decisions. After that admission turn drains, the router retracts the request only if it still needs to wait for worker capacity. Retraction restores global and class pending counters and disarms its lifecycle lease; the rejection reports the class load remaining after retraction. Ordinary requests continue to queue.

- Preserve `nvext.do_not_queue` and raw `RouterRequest::New.do_not_queue`, defaulting to `false`. Propagate the field through frontend, selection, standalone selection, and EPP. Advisory selection ignores it because advisory operations do not enter queue admission.
- Preserve structured raw `RouterResponse::DoNotQueue`. HTTP paths expose the distinct `router.do_not_queue` reason, `RateLimited`/429, and safe class and pending load details. Existing queue-limit, deadline, capacity, and no-worker outcomes retain their own behavior.
- Update the existing nvext documentation and all affected custom-policy example, builtin scorer, and benchmark constructors.

This option governs only the router pending queue. It does not control backend engine queues or guarantee zero end-to-end waiting. Existing high-level positional routing APIs retain their default behavior; the PR does not extend the C API.

## Validation

- macOS: `cargo test -p dynamo-kv-router --no-default-features --features standalone-selection do_not_queue --lib` (14 passed), plus all 51 scheduler queue tests without default features.
- macOS: targeted `dynamo-llm --no-default-features` tests cover semantic error mapping, raw router idle/busy behavior, and real unary and streaming HTTP 429 responses. Targeted `dynamo-ext-proc` tests cover integrated and standalone EPP mappings. The HTTP and raw router integration tests used a localhost-capable test environment.
- `cargo check` passed for `dynamo-ext-proc`, `dynamo-custom-policy-builtin`, and the two affected custom-policy examples. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` passed. Docs lint passed with 0 errors and 8 existing warnings.
- `cargo clippy` passed for `dynamo-kv-router`, `dynamo-llm`, and `dynamo-ext-proc` with `--no-default-features --all-targets -- -D warnings -A unused-variables -A clippy::derivable-impls`. The two allowances cover pre-existing macOS warnings in `dynamo-runtime` and `dynamo-mocker`.
- `policy_queue` Criterion benchmark, macOS dev profile, 20 samples, same benchmark source on main and this PR: normal `pop_once_exact/1` 869.16 ns → 879.60 ns; single rejected-tail retraction from 1024 queued requests 128.26 µs → 129.90 µs. These measurements cover queue primitives, not end-to-end router or HTTP latency; differences are small relative to run-to-run noise.

## Review entry points

1. `lib/kv-router/src/scheduling/queue.rs`: normal enqueue/drain, post-drain retraction, counter and lease cleanup.
2. `lib/kv-router/src/protocols.rs`, `lib/kv-router/src/services/selection/`, and `lib/llm/src/kv_router.rs`: wire compatibility and admission propagation.
3. Runtime semantic error, frontend HTTP, EPP, and regression tests.

Closes #10573

title: fix(metrics): remove stale worker series and expose router worker availability
body:
## Overview:

Deleted workers can reappear in frontend metrics when late request or replica updates recreate their gauge labels after discovery cleanup. Router admission can also reject workers while their discovery records remain present, including when Model Deployment Card fingerprints conflict.

- Collect `dynamo_component_router_worker_registered` from live scheduler discovery and effective availability, excluding canceled or closed owners.
- Filter the five frontend per-worker load and last-observation gauges at collection time using committed/admitted worker availability and valid DP ranks, so late writes cannot restore removed worker series.
- Account for the actual prefill and encode hop clients' local availability when reporting those workers.
- Add `dynamo_frontend_router_workers` for discovered, available, pending, and excluded physical worker counts, and `dynamo_frontend_router_worker_state` for current per-worker state and reason.
- Retain explicit zero counts for previously observed groups for the model manager lifetime, without retaining removed worker IDs. Document semantics, distinguish excluded workers from missing load telemetry in the rejection troubleshooting guides, and regenerate Python metric constants.

Worker inventory follows the frontend-local first-wins admission semantics introduced in #14632.

With one healthy incumbent and one incompatible newcomer, the expected counts are `discovered=2`, `available=1`, `pending=0`, and `excluded=1`. Only the rejected worker carries `reason="checksum_mismatch"`; the incumbent remains available.

Rejected worker additions and removals refresh metric observations without rebuilding or withdrawing the incumbent. After the incumbent fully drains, the successor transitions from excluded to pending and then available after successful commit.

Each frontend reports its own admitted workers. Different observation orders may intentionally produce different incumbents.

## Validation:

- Passed 29 targeted Rust tests after integrating #14632, covering first-wins admission, rejected membership changes, initialization/build failure, succession, final removal, independent frontend observation orders, and prefill/encode availability across same-endpoint generations.



## Where should the reviewer start?

For the latest update, start with `lib/llm/src/discovery/controller.rs`: observations now distinguish the incumbent cohort from checksum-mismatched workers, including rejected additions/removals that do not trigger incumbent reconciliation.

Then review `lib/llm/src/http/service/worker_metrics.rs` for per-worker exclusion reasons and the updated first-wins count/state regression tests.

Then review:
- `lib/llm/src/kv_router/metrics/worker_registered.rs` for registration exposition based on live scheduler discovery and availability, including cancellation and owner lifetime handling.
- `lib/llm/src/discovery/controller.rs` and `worker_inventory.rs` for observation publication and retention of empty group descriptors to expose explicit zero counts.
- `lib/llm/src/discovery/model_manager.rs` for availability checks that include the actual prefill/encode hop clients.

The nearby regression tests cover late writes after worker removal, MCD conflict and recovery, empty groups, and client-local fault inhibition. The metric contract is documented in `docs/fern/pages/reference/observability/metrics-catalog.mdx`.

title: test(runtime): stabilize early cancellation checks
body:
## Summary

Make the early-cancellation tests wait for stream closure and worker acknowledgement instead of assuming cancellation prevents every response from reaching the client.

I encountered this while running CI for #14846 (`fix(responses): preserve text instead of inferring tool calls`), at head `f41e5dcd531c3d4116b7238535b5111658104484`. That PR changes the Responses converter and its Rust coverage; the failing test uses the runtime client directly. This follow-up keeps the cancellation-test fix separate from the Responses change.

## CI failure

The [failed job](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/actions/runs/34957859227/job/104354055474) was `dynamo-runtime / test / sequential cuda13.0, amd64`. It reported:

```text
_____________ test_client_context_cancel_before_await_request[tcp] _____________
lib/bindings/python/tests/cancellation/test_cancellation.py:390:
E   AssertionError: Request should be cancelled before any responses are generated
_ = Annotated(data=0, event=None, comment=[], id=None)

1 failed, 3616 passed, 143 skipped, 1989 deselected
```

The worker log shows the ordering:

```text
11:06:27.964617Z request received
Processing iteration 0
Sending iteration 0
Processing iteration 1
11:06:28.084912Z request cancellation received
Context stopped at iteration 2
```

The cancellation reached the worker about 120 ms after the request. The mock yields every 100 ms, so a response was already in flight. `dynamo-status-check` then failed because this job failed. Rust tests, Clippy, the arm64 sequential job, and the backend tests passed. The matching job passed in the three main runs inspected, so this is not a claim that the exact CI failure was also reproduced on main.

## Why this changes the assertion

`client.generate()` schedules the Rust future immediately; awaiting the returned Python future does not start the request. `stop_generating()` signals cancellation asynchronously, and the response stream may still deliver buffered data. Requiring zero responses therefore depends on cancellation winning a scheduling race.

Both the already-cancelled and cancel-before-await tests now drain in-flight responses and require stream closure plus an explicit event from the mock worker when it observes cancellation, within a shared 5-second deadline. They retain the stopped/not-killed assertions. A 15-second pytest timeout bounds the overall test, and the event replaces the fixed 200 ms wait. Production runtime behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

- Complete cancellation module before rebasing onto current main: 14 passed, covering NATS and TCP.
- After rebasing onto current main: all four changed early-cancellation cases passed again.
- Controlled scheduling check: inserting a 150 ms event-loop delay between request creation and cancellation, still before awaiting the request, reproduced the original `Annotated(data=0)` assertion failure. This demonstrates the ordering assumption rather than reproducing the exact CI scheduling delay.
- Patched stress batch: 63 passed before an unrelated NATS `No workers available` discovery error stopped the batch. A separate delayed TCP batch passed all 10 repetitions.
- Negative control: omitting the cancellation call made both NATS and TCP tests fail at the 5-second timeout, as expected.
- Applicable repository pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed.

These checks used macOS arm64, Python 3.12.7, the existing local Dynamo extension, NATS 2.12.14, and etcd 3.5.33. The exact private ECR CI image was unavailable without registry credentials; the extension was not rebuilt from the PR.

## Related Issues

- [x] Confirmed — no related issue.
- Related PR: #14846.

title: fix(tests): resolve AISimulate from NVIDIA index in wheel smoke tests
body:
Source issue: [DYN-4508](https://linear.app/nvidia/issue/DYN-4508).

## Summary

The wheel smoke tests now take `aisimulate` as a wheel from NVIDIA's package index, removing the step that made `test_core_install_clean_room[3.13]` fail intermittently.

## Details:

`ai-dynamo` requires `aisimulate==0.12.0` on Python 3.11-3.13, and the public index serves no wheel for that version — only a 20 kB placeholder sdist whose build backend downloads the real 83.6 MB `cp311-abi3` wheel at metadata time and asserts its SHA-256. One corrupted download made `pip install` exit 1 with `metadata-generation-failed`. pip's `--retries` and `--timeout` do not govern that transfer, which runs inside the build backend.

`pip_install` in `tests/wheels/smoke_install.py` adds `--find-links https://pypi.nvidia.com/aisimulate/` only when the wheelhouse has no AISimulate wheel, and passes `--only-binary aisimulate` to avoid the placeholder build backend. The dependency consistency guard checks the smoke helper's index URL against the expected NVIDIA URL and the Dockerfile's link source. `container/templates/wheel_builder.Dockerfile` already stages the wheel this way, but only for the planner and framework runtime targets, so the framework-agnostic `dynamo-runtime` image that runs these tests is not covered. The link source is scoped to one project page. The fallback requires `pypi.nvidia.com` to be reachable, as the placeholder already did; if it is not, the install fails with a plain resolution error naming `aisimulate`.

## Where should the reviewer start?

`pip_install` in `tests/wheels/smoke_install.py`, alongside lines 635-653 of `container/templates/wheel_builder.Dockerfile`.

## Validation

Prior validation at `3590f2a7b0faba45df0e3f1f9735ea4b0906ca76`: calling `pip_install` directly on Python 3.13 against an empty wheelhouse resolves the wheel with no metadata-preparation step; the same call without the added link source exits 1. The full node needs released `ai-dynamo` wheels, so only the `dynamo-runtime / test / parallel` job exercises it end to end — this shows the fragile path is no longer executed, not that a rare corrupted download has stopped occurring.

The consistency-guard update passes the repository-pinned isort, Black, Flake8, and Ruff checks. Runtime validation uses remote CI; no local tests or builds were run for this update.

Closes https://linear.app/nvidia/issue/DYN-4508

title: fix(gms): fail-stop and broadcast TP rank failures
body:
## Purpose

- Stop all affected ranks before KV handoff.
- Fence distributed SGLang ranks before takeover.
- Defer runtime liveness deadlines until an engine is actually serving.
- Propagate a native GPU crash from rank-local GMS directly to the TP leader over a pre-connected ZMQ socket.
- Retain the shared marker and heartbeat timeout as independent fallbacks.

## Notification versus authority

The ZMQ message is only a latency hint. It is scoped to the exact writer cohort and malformed or cross-cohort messages are ignored. Receiving it starts the existing rank fence and failover callback; it does not prove CUDA quiescence or grant write ownership. The writer guard, quiescence provider, lease classification, and generation fence remain authoritative.

## Why this is separate

This is hardening step 10 of 15. #15043 defines safe quiescence/reclamation, while this PR minimizes the time required for a non-leader TP-rank crash to reach the leader. It builds on #15044; the next step is #15046.

2. `lib/gpu_memory_service/server/gpu_quiescence.py` — persistent nonblocking notifier.
3. `lib/gpu_memory_service/common/gpu_failure_marker.py` — filesystem fallback.
4. Focused rank-liveness and GMS notifier tests.

title: feat(gms): quarantine ambiguous KV until GPU quiescence
body:
## Purpose

- Classify ambiguous predecessor leases as quarantined.
- Keep quarantine-only takeover as the fail-closed default.
- Add an optional MPS-backed provider that can terminate a failed CUDA cohort and prove client retirement before reclaiming its KV.
- Catch native CUDA-worker crashes early and preserve conservative fallback behavior when quiescence cannot be proven.

## Safety model

Process death, a heartbeat timeout, traffic silence, and a fixed delay are not CUDA-quiescence proof. Ambiguous predecessor blocks remain quarantined unless the configured provider verifies that every registered CUDA client in the failed cohort has retired.

The native crash interlock is an early trigger, not takeover authority. Writer retirement, lease classification, and generation fencing remain authoritative.

title: feat(multimodal): shared encoded-image cache with session scoping
body:
Closes DIS-2912

## Summary

Combines three related multimodal image-loading changes (ported from Inferact/dynamo#261, Inferact/dynamo#264, and Inferact/dynamo#265):

**1. Shared encoded-image cache (Redis Cluster / Dragonfly)** — an opt-in shared cache for encoded multimodal image bytes (`components/src/dynamo/common/multimodal/shared_image_cache.py`), sitting in front of the existing per-worker decoded-image LRU and in-flight fetch deduplication:

- On load, check the shared cache before hitting the origin; refill it after a successful origin fetch
- Fail open to the origin on any shared-cache read/write/delete error
- Validate cached payloads; evict corrupt entries and refetch from the origin
- Split Redis connection vs I/O timeouts for large image transfers
- Expose shared-cache GET/SET latency histograms (bucketed by outcome and encoded payload size) via `register_image_loader_metrics` in `dynamo.common.utils.prometheus`

**2. Session-scoped caching** — read `x-session-affinity` at the Rust HTTP boundary and propagate it through the agent context and router session affinity into the vLLM image loader. Local decoded-image LRU entries, in-flight fetch dedup, and shared-cache entries are keyed by a hashed session identifier. Gated behind `DYN_MM_IMAGE_CACHE_SESSION_SCOPED=1` (default off); when enabled without a valid session scope, image caches are bypassed entirely.

**3. Fail open on Redis cluster errors** — also catch redis-py's `RedisClusterException` (defined directly under `Exception`, outside the `RedisError` hierarchy) so Dragonfly cluster connection timeouts fall back to origin fetching instead of failing the request.

## Porting notes

title: feat(kv-router): add Mooncake Store shared-cache routing
body:
## Overview:

### Summary

Add experimental, opt-in `--shared-cache-type mooncake-store` routing for vLLM's `MooncakeStoreConnector`. The router can credit reusable prefixes held in the shared store after GPU eviction, rather than treating every GPU miss as cold. Hints require validated worker metadata, eligible request and event provenance, and evidence that every required cache object is present.

## Details:

### Routing and residency

- Learn local request-hash to external engine-hash relationships from primary GPU `Stored` events before radix-tree insertion can reject an unknown parent. Reuse the precomputed request hashes rather than reproducing vLLM's Python hashing protocol.
- Track full SHA-256 digests, exact exported rank/group prefixes, and independent CPU/disk residency. Return a hint only when every object required at a candidate restart endpoint is present. Support validated full-attention, sliding-window, and Mamba-align layouts without assuming that every earlier endpoint is reusable.
- Bound identity and residency state. Invalidate residency on sequence gaps, malformed relevant events, and surfaced stream failures. Prevent old contract generations from changing successor state. Silent reconnects and lost final removal events remain best-effort staleness limits.
- Capture positive text-only eligibility before request and event normalization discards metadata. Missing or unsupported provenance withholds hints without rejecting ordinary GPU events. Preserve provenance through publisher coalescing and replay, including the distinction between MessagePack binary and text values.

### Worker contracts and lifecycle

- Add an explicit worker extension and bounded `dynamo_mooncake_store_descriptor` RPC. Export initialized connector facts through `ModelRuntimeConfig.set_engine_specific`, validate rank coverage and descriptor agreement, and support composition with the existing FPM worker extension.
- Pin the adapter to vLLM revision `1085b64425a9e6f5ca52876ad32e55fda5665f4e`. Require one data-parallel rank per endpoint, prefill context parallelism (`PCP`) of one, and decode context parallelism (`DCP`) of one. Tensor and pipeline parallelism use the exact exported object prefixes.
- Validate contracts against admitted workers without changing model deployment card checksum or admission rules. Keep one passive cache per router, start its background tasks only after construction succeeds, and cancel and await both tasks during shutdown.
- Replace the scheduler-owned strong request-lease observer with a weak observer. This breaks a reference cycle exposed by the failed-constructor regression while retaining live admission, progress, and completion callbacks.
- Preserve GPU overlap and cached-token accounting, scheduler semantics, and HiCache behavior. Unsupported optional contracts disable hints, not serving. Invalid feature configuration is rejected explicitly. Add configuration, deployment documentation, and generated ownership rules. Most changes outside these components initialize the new event-provenance field.

### Validation

Validation ran on the complete implementation, not on each intermediate commit.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo test -p dynamo-kv-router --lib` | 963 passed, 2 ignored |
| Targeted `dynamo-llm` router, indexer, discovery, lifecycle, scheduler, and cache tests with `--no-default-features` and `--test-threads=1` | 189 passed, 3 ignored |
| Pinned offline coordinator oracle | All 12 cases passed through both local indexers |
| Focused Python worker tests | 52 passed; 4 initialized-connector cases skipped |
| Python router configuration tests | 81 passed with a package-initializer bypass; not native-binding integration validation |
| Rust bindings and affected consumer/benchmark compilation | Passed |
| Rust formatting, targeted Clippy, scoped Python lint/compilation, oracle regeneration, and whitespace checks | Passed; existing warnings remain |
| Documentation lint | 462 files scanned, 0 errors, 8 existing warnings |

An existing recovery test timed out in the parallel run, then passed independently and in the final serial run. Its underlying timeout cause was not established.

Acceptance remains unverified for:

- The four initialized-connector cases, which require `torch` and the exact pinned vLLM installation.
- Python runtime-metadata and FPM integration suites, which could not collect because `dynamo.llm` was unavailable. Rust binding compilation passed separately.
- Live Mooncake transfer and GPU acceptance, including tensor parallelism of at least two with full-attention plus sliding-window and full-attention plus Mamba, reuse after GPU eviction, and a miss when a required parallel object is absent.

The full `pre-commit` suite and Fern CLI checks were unavailable. The whole repository test suite was not run.

### Measurements

The three-group, tensor-parallel-two debug benchmark averaged 8.42 ms for 4,096 blocks and 39.28 ms for 16,384 blocks over 32 runs per size. These are not release-profile latency results. Measured backing-map allocations at the fixed caps were approximately 98.5 MiB live and 117 MiB during growth; these figures exclude other runtime state and are not process RSS.

## Where should the reviewer start?

1. `lib/llm/src/kv_router/shared_cache/mooncake_store_contract.rs` and `lib/llm/src/kv_router/shared_cache/vllm_mooncake_store.rs` define supported layouts, contract validation, residency, and reusable-prefix lookup.
2. `components/src/dynamo/vllm/mooncake_store_runtime.py` defines the pinned worker contract and export path. `components/src/dynamo/vllm/tests/generate_mooncake_oracle.py` supplies the offline coordinator reference cases.
3. `lib/llm/src/discovery/model_manager.rs`, `lib/llm/src/kv_router/indexer/mod.rs`, and `lib/llm/src/kv_router/route_lookup.rs` integrate admitted membership, primary event observation, and request lookup.
4. `lib/kv-router/src/zmq_wire/tests.rs`, `lib/llm/src/kv_router/shared_cache/vllm_mooncake_store/tests.rs`, and `lib/llm/src/discovery/model_manager/mooncake_tests.rs` cover provenance, hybrid readiness, contract replacement, and lifetime regressions.

## Related Issues

title: fix(router): separate remote KV wait from prefill load
body:
## Overview

CPU KV offloading puts requests in vLLM's `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` state while cached KV blocks move from host storage to the GPU. The KV router currently discounts lower-tier cache hits when it scores workers, then reuses that discounted overlap as a prefill-compute estimate. This makes transfer-resident tokens look like GPU prefill work and can steer later prefix-affine requests away from the worker that already owns their KV.

This change separates remote KV transfer backlog from prefill compute load. Prefix affinity remains eligible while transfers are in flight; operators can optionally reject a worker only after its remote-KV waiting-token backlog crosses an explicit threshold.

## Summary

- Exclude all selected cached tiers, including host and disk tiers, from GPU prefill load accounting.
- Report vLLM `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` requests and tokens as dedicated forward-pass telemetry.
- Relay that telemetry to the KV router and expose per-worker Prometheus gauges.
- Add the optional `--remote-kv-waiting-tokens-threshold` / `DYN_REMOTE_KV_WAITING_TOKENS_THRESHOLD` overload check. It is disabled by default.
- Automatically enable the instrumented scheduler and relay when a vLLM KV transfer connector is configured.
- Preserve the existing queued-decode totals for planner compatibility.

## Performance

Controlled A/B on MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 used three TP4 aggregated replicas (12 GB200 GPUs), concurrency 168, the same 2,000-request Mooncake trace, CPU offloading at 100 GB/rank with `store_threshold: 2`, self-describing KV events, and the same vLLM patches. Both arms used fixed synthetic EAGLE acceptance length 2.89. The treatment changed only the Dynamo router behavior in this PR.

| Metric | Control | This change | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Output throughput | 5,548.13 tok/s | 5,716.12 tok/s | +3.03% |
| Output throughput/GPU | 462.34 tok/s | 476.34 tok/s | +3.03% |
| Benchmark duration | 883.50 s | 857.54 s | -2.94% |
| Mean TTFT | 12,306.57 ms | 11,478.36 ms | -6.73% |
| Median TTFT | 870.91 ms | 774.52 ms | -11.07% |
| Median ITL | 22.67 ms | 22.12 ms | -2.43% |
| Mean frontend queue | 26.96 requests | 23.58 requests | -12.50% |
| Mean worker waiting queue | 3.76 requests/replica | 3.15 requests/replica | -16.24% |
| Mean worker deferred queue | 3.37 requests/replica | 2.88 requests/replica | -14.52% |
| Request error rate | 0.30% | 0.30% | unchanged |

Mean ITL regressed from 35.73 ms to 47.94 ms, driven by tail outliers, and worker preemptions increased from 77 to 86. The runs used identical GB200 hardware, but Kubernetes placed the replicas on different nodes. These results therefore show the observed end-to-end effect rather than a microbenchmark of the scheduling change.

## Details

The routing policy now uses the selected worker's cumulative cached block count to compute the actual GPU prefill remainder. Lower-tier overlap weighting still affects worker selection, where transfer cost belongs, but no longer inflates active prefill compute after selection.

The worker separately publishes remote-KV waiting requests and tokens. The default policy records and exports that backlog without rejecting the worker. Setting `--remote-kv-waiting-tokens-threshold` makes the worker ineligible only when every data-parallel rank exceeds the configured backlog.

## Existing Work Check

- Current `main` contains the earlier `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` queued-decode classification used by disaggregated planner accounting, but it does not publish a remote-KV backlog signal or separate lower-tier cache transfer from router prefill load.
- #14963 adds admission control for disaggregated decode requests waiting on remote-prefill transfers. It controls request admission inside decode workers; it does not address aggregated CPU-offload worker selection or prefill-load accounting.

## Where should the reviewer start?

1. `lib/kv-router/src/scheduling/queue.rs` for the corrected prefill-compute hint.
2. `components/src/dynamo/vllm/instrumented_scheduler.py` and `lib/llm/src/fpm_publisher.rs` for the remote-KV backlog signal.
3. `lib/llm/src/discovery/worker_monitor.rs` for the optional overload policy.

- `cargo test -p dynamo-llm remote_kv`
- `PYTHONPATH=components/src python -m pytest components/src/dynamo/common/tests/configuration/test_kv_router_args.py` (70 passed)

title: fix(operator): read every vLLM flag spelling through one parser
body:
#### Overview:

vLLM accepts `--data-parallel-size 4`, `--data-parallel-size=4` and `-dp 4` as the same thing. This package did not — two readers of the same command line disagreed about which spellings count, and they are reached from different callers.

| Reader | Matches |
|---|---|
| `hasArg` (`utils.go`) | `flag value`, `flag=value`, and separate tokens — all three |
| `getFlagValue` (`backend_vllm.go`) | only an exact long flag followed by a separate token; silently returns its default of `1` otherwise |

Found by @julienmancuso while reviewing #13580. Split out because the fix reaches the multinode path too, which that PR does not otherwise touch.

#### Details:

**Consequence 1 — elastic EP renders an unsafe launch.**

`IsElasticEPRayLaunch` qualifies a launch through `hasArg`, which understands `-dpb`. The declared width is read through `getFlagValue`, which does not understand `-dp`. So this command line qualifies as elastic EP and reads as **one rank**:

```
--enable-elastic-ep -dpb ray -dp 4
```

A one-rank reading renders no extra pods, no `--data-parallel-size-local` pin and no width gate — while vLLM still places four ranks, which is exactly the abort those three exist to prevent:

```
ValueError: Not enough resources to allocate 4 DP ranks on DP master node <ip>,
            possible to fit 1 DP ranks.
```

Measured across all four spellings before the fix:

| Command line | Qualifies as elastic EP | Width read as |
|---|---|---|
| `--data-parallel-size 4` | yes | 4 |
| `--data-parallel-size=4` | yes | **1** |
| `-dpb ray -dp 4` | yes | **1** |
| `-dpb ray --data-parallel-size 4` | yes | 4 |

**Consequence 2 — multinode world size, which predates elastic EP.**

`getWorldSize` reads tensor and pipeline sizes through the same `getFlagValue`, so `-tp 4` or `--tensor-parallel-size=4` read as `1`. World size decides `dataParallelSizeLocal` and whether multinode coordination is injected at all, so a size silently read as 1 is not cosmetic.

**The fix: normalize at the tokenizer, not at each reader.**

`getExpandedCommandLine` and `getExpandedArgs` now return a canonical stream — short aliases expanded to their long form, `--flag=value` split into two tokens. Every existing helper is corrected at once, and there is no second parser left to drift from this one. A future alias is added in one place.

```go
var vllmShortFlagAliases = map[string]string{
	"-tp": tensorParallelSizeFlag, "-pp": pipelineParallelSizeFlag,
	"-dp": dataParallelSizeFlag, "-dpl": dataParallelSizeLocalFlag,
	"-dpb": dataParallelBackendFlag,
}
```

Anything unrecognized passes through untouched — this canonicalizes spelling, it does not filter.

**Verification.** Mutation-checked: dropping the `normalizeVLLMFlags` call from the two tokenizers fails **19 of the 23** new subtests. Coverage is every spelling of every size flag, the qualify-vs-size asymmetry above, `getWorldSize`, pass-through of unknown flags, and whole-token alias matching — so `-dpb` is never read as `-dp` with a stray `b`.

Full operator suite green, `gofmt` clean.

#### Where should the reviewer start?

1. `internal/dynamo/backend_vllm.go` — `normalizeVLLMFlags` and the two tokenizers that call it. The doc comment records both failure modes and why the fix sits at the tokenizer rather than at the readers.
2. `internal/dynamo/vllm_flag_normalize_test.go` — `TestNormalizeVLLMFlags_QualifyingLaunchAlsoSizes` is the elastic-EP asymmetry; `..._WorldSizeReadsShortAndEqualsForms` is the multinode one.

Note on behaviour change: flags that were previously **silently ignored** now take effect. For anyone relying on `-tp 4` having been read as `1`, this changes the rendered launch — but that reading was never intentional.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - vLLM configuration now consistently recognizes supported short and long flag aliases.
  - Both `--flag=value` and space-separated `--flag value` formats are handled equivalently.
  - Tensor, pipeline, data-parallel, and local data-parallel settings are parsed reliably across supported spellings.
  - Distributed launch sizing now correctly reflects tensor and pipeline dimensions, including elastic data-parallel configurations.
  - Unrecognized arguments remain unchanged, and partial matches no longer trigger unintended flag handling.

title: fix(ci): skip DGDR deploy tests without planner image
body:
## Summary

- Build the Planner image when DGDR files change, so DGDR-only changes still have the image they need.
- Run the DGDR deployment tests only after the Planner image copy succeeds and returns a nonempty tag. This prevents a cancelled Planner build from producing unrelated DGDR admission errors.

## Why

In [PR #14681's CI run](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/actions/runs/35692044251), the [Planner build](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/actions/runs/35692044251/job/106630989733) was cancelled at its 60-minute limit. The Planner image copy was skipped, but the DGDR job still started with an empty image tag (`dynamo-planner:`). The webhook then rejected DGDRs because `spec.image` had no parseable version tag and `spec.runtimeVersionOverride` was absent:
