title: feat(llm): add shadow tap for mirrored request and response streams
body:
## Overview:

### Summary

**Why.** Today a change to routing, scheduling, KV cache policy, or an engine version is judged on synthetic load, or on a trace that was converted after the fact. Neither method shows how the change behaves under the traffic that the deployment serves now. A shadow deployment receives a live copy of production requests and serves them on separate workers. Its results do not reach a client, so a wrong or slow result costs users nothing. The frontend had no tap that supplies this copy in the form that the workers see.

## Details:

**What.** This PR adds a shadow tap: a pipeline `Operator` in `dynamo-llm` (not the Kubernetes operator). The tap is linked immediately before `migration.forward_edge()` in `PreprocessedRouting::build_pipeline` and `build_preprocessed_pipeline`. The in-process token pipeline (`common::build_pipeline`) links it between the preprocessor and the backend operator. At this position it sees each request as a `PreprocessedRequest`, for all public APIs and for the Python chat processors. Migration retries occur below the tap, so one client request gives one record.

Two capture modes show the two uses:

| Tap in `lib/bench/shadow/taps.yaml` | Mode | Consumer need |
|---|---|---|
| `kv-history-tracker` | `capture: request`, filter `tokens-only` | Prompt tokens, when they arrive |
| `shadow-replay` | `capture: request_response`, `emit: joined` | Request, primary response, arrival time, and outcome, to replay the same load and compare |

Design points:

- `DYN_SHADOW_TAP_CONFIG` names a YAML file. If the variable is not set, the operator is not linked, and the frontend pays nothing. An invalid config stops the frontend at startup.
- Named filters run on `&PreprocessedRequest` before the copy. `project()` destructures the struct without `..`, so a new field does not compile until someone decides how the tap treats it. `strip-worker-pins` is on by default, because worker ids of the primary deployment are wrong for a shadow.
- The request id comes from the pipeline `Context`. No field is added to `PreprocessedRequest`, so the worker wire format does not change.
- Each tap has a bounded queue (default 1024 records, never unbounded) and one publisher task on the secondary runtime. The request path calls `try_send`. A full queue drops the record and increments `shadow_tap_dropped_total{reason="full"}`; a gone publisher task counts as `reason="closed"`. The tap holds the recorded output tokens of every in-flight request until its stream ends; `response.max_tokens` caps that for each choice, and the config doc states the bound when it is unset.
- The client `stream` flag does not change the tap. Inside the pipeline a response is always a stream of chunks. The tap accumulates the chunks and publishes one consolidated `ShadowResponse`. It does not forward chunks to a shadow. A request with `n > 1` gives one `ShadowChoice` for each index, with its own tokens and finish reason. The outcome is `complete` only when each requested choice finished and no choice failed. A stream that ends with no error and no cancel, but without a finish reason for each requested choice, gives `incomplete`.
- A joined record is published one time: at stream end, on an error, or when the stream is dropped. If the request context is stopped or killed, the outcome is `cancelled`. The outcomes are `complete`, `incomplete`, `cancelled`, and `error`.
- `shadow_consumer` (feature `shadow-consumer` of `dynamo-bench`) reads one topic and keeps totals. It counts records that the tap dropped and records that the transport lost.

### Validation

Unit tests (`cargo test -p dynamo-llm --lib --no-default-features shadow::`, 32 pass, and 2 in `entrypoint::input::grpc`; the full `dynamo-llm` lib suite passes, 2787 tests): filters, config, pass-through, stalled consumer under a timeout, joined record, cancel, error, engine error, shared copy, MessagePack round trip, publisher drain, and a linked pipeline with the tap above `Migration` where a retried request gives one record of each kind.

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean for `dynamo-llm`, `dynamo-runtime`, and `dynamo-bench`.

CI (`pre-merge.yml`) now compiles, lints, and runs the tests of the `shadow_consumer` binary with the `shadow-consumer` feature.

**Demo** (`lib/bench/shadow/demo.sh`): frontend with two taps, 2 mocker workers, AIPerf, one consumer per tap. File discovery, ZMQ event plane, TCP request plane. No etcd and no NATS.

| Run | Frontend metrics | `kv-history-tracker` | `shadow-replay` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200 requests, ISL 512, OSL 32 | 200 requests, 104000 input tokens, 6400 output tokens | 200 records, 104000 prompt tokens, 0 gaps | 200 records, 6400 output tokens, 200 complete, 0 gaps |
| 200 requests, non-streaming (`STREAMING=`) | 200 `unary` success, 6400 output tokens | 200 records, 0 gaps | 200 records, 6400 output tokens, 200 complete, 0 gaps |
| 200 requests, 25% cancelled by the client | 148 success, 52 cancelled, 12431 output tokens | 200 records, 0 gaps | 200 records, 12431 output tokens, 148 complete, 52 cancelled, 0 incomplete, 0 error, 0 gaps |

**Cost** (release build, 4 mocker workers at speedup 1000, AIPerf concurrency 64, 3000 requests, ISL 2048, OSL 16, two rounds). In the stalled case the two consumers are stopped with `SIGSTOP` during the measured run.

| Case | Requests/s | TTFT p50 ms | TTFT p99 ms | Frontend RSS MB |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| no tap | 1245 / 1259 | 8.09 / 7.54 | 52.2 / 50.1 | 317 / 318 |
| 2 taps, consumers read | 1196 / 1249 | 9.94 / 7.94 | 55.6 / 51.1 | 296 / 290 |
| 2 taps, consumers stalled | 1242 / 1247 | 8.26 / 8.04 | 51.9 / 52.6 | 337 / 345 |

The three cases are within the noise of the two rounds. This test does not prove that the frontend was the bottleneck, so it sets an upper limit on the cost at this load and not a precise cost. All 3300 records arrived in each tap run, with 0 gaps, after the stalled consumers continued.

**Stalled shadow.** Each tap sets the ZMQ send high-water mark of its publisher to the tap `capacity` (`EventPublisher::for_namespace_with_zmq_send_hwm`, new in this PR). The default mark is 100,000 messages for each stalled subscriber, which can hold gigabytes of long prompts in the frontend. With two consumers stopped by `SIGSTOP` and 12,300 requests of 2048 tokens, the consumers later received 4096 and 2048 records (the tap capacities are 4096 and 1024), and the frontend RSS was 22 MB more than with active consumers. ZMQ drops the other records without a count. The tap counters do not show this loss, and a consumer cannot see a loss at the end of its sequence range.

**Runtime scope.** Taps are registered for each `DistributedRuntime` and end with its shutdown token. A second runtime in the same process gets its own taps. `shadow::taps` starts the taps on first lookup, so an entry point that skips the startup call, such as a direct call of `grpc::run`, still links its taps. `grpc::run` and `prepare_engine` read the taps before they start the model watcher, so a bad config stops startup on those paths too. An in-process text engine has no `PreprocessedRequest` to mirror, so a tap config with that engine is a startup error. The registry drops the taps of a runtime when the runtime stops.

**Not done here.** The tap counters are registered on the runtime metrics registry. This PR did not examine whether the frontend `/metrics` endpoint shows them. No test or live run exercises the tap in the in-process token pipeline; it is compiled and linted only. No test builds the full `PreprocessedRouting` builders with a tap; the link order is tested on a smaller pipeline with the real `Migration` operator.

## Where should the reviewer start?

- `lib/llm/src/shadow/tap.rs`: the operator, the joined-record `Recorder`, and the tests. The outcome rules in `Recorder::emit` and the drop path are the parts that need the closest read.
- `lib/llm/src/shadow/filter.rs`: `project()`. It lists each `PreprocessedRequest` field and decides whether a shadow receives it.
- `lib/llm/src/entrypoint/input/common.rs`: the two link sites. The link chain is split so that the tap is optional.
- `lib/llm/src/entrypoint/input.rs`: `initialize_input` now returns a `Result`, so an invalid tap config stops the frontend.

## Related Issues

- Relates to #14986

#14986 is the design record for this PR. It is closed as completed, because this PR implements all of its acceptance criteria. The close comment maps each criterion to a test or a demo result.

title: fix(operator): make Ray multinode workers wait for the leader
body:
## Overview:

Ray multinode workers start `ray start --address=<leader>:6379 --block` immediately on pod start, with no gating on the leader's Ray head being ready — unlike MP (multiprocessing) workers, which already wait via an init container. This can leave a worker permanently unable to join the cluster until its pod is deleted and recreated.

## Details:

MP multinode workers already get a `wait-for-leader-mp` init container (`VLLMBackend.UpdatePodSpec`) that polls the leader's MP master port via a generic wait script/ConfigMap before the worker's main container starts. Ray workers never got an equivalent — they run `ray start --address=...` the instant the pod's containers start, racing the leader's `ray start --head`.

This reuses the same generic wait-for-leader script/ConfigMap infrastructure (already backend-agnostic) for Ray workers: it now waits on the Ray GCS port (6379) instead of the MP master port, with a `wait-for-leader-ray` init container name. Detection is based on the exact command shape `injectRayDistributedLaunchFlags` gives a plain TP/PP Ray worker (`ray start --address=...`), which is distinct from the elastic-EP Ray worker (already has its own leader health-gate) and the data-parallel-Ray path (keeps the full vLLM command) — so neither of those gets a redundant second init container.

## Where should the reviewer start?

`VLLMBackend.waitForLeaderPortAndName` and `UpdatePodSpec` in `deploy/operator/internal/dynamo/backend_vllm.go`. `TestVLLMBackend_UpdatePodSpec` in `backend_vllm_test.go` covers the new Ray-worker cases plus the elastic-EP/data-parallel exclusions.

## Validation

title: docs: Fix harmony vocab download issue
body:
## Overview:

  gpt-oss models parse reasoning and tool calls through the `gpt_oss` reasoning parser and
  the `harmony` tool call parser. Both tokenize model output with the `o200k_base.tiktoken`
  vocabulary file, which the frontend downloads on first use from
  `openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net`. In an air-gapped cluster that download never
  completes, and the failure is silent at the API surface: `tool_calls` comes back empty and
  raw Harmony channel markers pass through in `message.content`. Nothing in the docs or the
  gpt-oss recipe said so, and the file is too large for a ConfigMap, so users were left to
  discover the init-container workaround themselves.
  
  This PR documents how to serve the vocabulary from local storage. 

## Details:

 - **`docs/fern/pages/use-cases/tool-calling-and-reasoning/tool-call-parsing.mdx`** — new
    "Harmony Vocabulary for Air-Gapped Clusters" section: which parsers need the file, the
    download URL and pinned SHA256, the exact filename the parsers construct, why a
    ConfigMap will not hold it, and how to point the frontend at a staged copy with
    `TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE`. A warning notes that setting the variable disables the
    download fallback, so a wrong path fails the same silent way.
  - **`recipes/gpt-oss-120b/README.md`** — an air-gapped-only prerequisite step with a
    DynamoGraphDeployment snippet that stages the file in the existing `model-cache` PVC and
    mounts it read-only on the Frontend. Clusters with outbound access need no change.
  - **`docs/fern/pages/use-cases/tool-calling-and-reasoning/reasoning-parsing.md`** and the
    `harmony` entry in the tool-call parser table — cross-links so the requirement is
    discoverable from the parser a user is already reading about. 

  ## Where should the reviewer start?
  
  `tool-call-parsing.mdx` — it carries the explanation the other two files link to. Worth
  confirming the SHA256, the `TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE` semantics (read directory first, no
  fallback once set), and that the recipe snippet's volume and mount names match the rest of
  `recipes/gpt-oss-120b/`.
                                                                                                                                                      
  ## Related Issues
  
  - Relates to #14853


- Closes #14853 

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Documentation**
  * Added guidance for configuring Harmony tokenization in air-gapped clusters.
  * Documented the required vocabulary file, download URL, SHA256 checksum, storage location, and read-only mount configuration.
  * Added instructions for setting the `TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE` frontend variable.
  * Clarified that missing vocabulary data can prevent tool calls from being populated and reasoning from being separated.
  * Linked reasoning and tool-call parsing documentation to the new setup instructions.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: test(sglang): narrow the frontend port window in the tool-calling fixture
body:
Source issue: [DYN-4425](https://linear.app/nvidia/issue/DYN-4425).

## Overview:

The SGLang tool-calling suite fails intermittently with `Main server process exited with code 1 while waiting for health check`. The failure happens in the module-scoped `tool_calling_services` fixture, so a single failed startup marks all 11 nodes of a topology with the same message.

## Details:

`allocate_ports` checks a candidate by binding a socket and closing it again, so nothing owns the port until the service binds it. The fixture took the frontend HTTP port alongside the worker ports, leaving it unowned across the whole SGLang engine boot. A competing listener in that window makes the frontend exit 1 on `Failed to start HTTP server: port N already in use`.

The fixture now takes that port immediately before the frontend launches, allocates all three ports from the disjoint bases in `tests/utils/constants.py` (base `10000` overlaps the window `tests/router/mocker_process.py` and `tests/mm_router/test_vllm_mm_router_e2e.py` allocate from), and releases them with `deallocate_ports` in teardown.

This narrows the window to the frontend's own startup; it does not remove it. The same collision can also surface as a 240-second `TIMEOUT: Check URL ... /v1/models`, so `code 1` under-counts it.

## Where should the reviewer start?

`tool_calling_services` in `tests/frontend/test_tool_calling_sglang.py`. #15136 touches the same fixture: keep its `--nccl-port` pin, and keep one `deallocate_ports` teardown if both land. Follow-up, deliberately not done here: `_check_url` in `tests/utils/managed_process.py` gives one request the whole remaining budget, so it never re-polls a child that has already died.

## Validation

`pre-commit run --files tests/frontend/test_tool_calling_sglang.py` passes, and `pytest tests/frontend/test_tool_calling_sglang.py --collect-only -q` collects 22 tests. Taking the allocated port before the frontend binds reproduces the reported message exactly through the fixture's own process class; with the port left free the frontend comes up and stays up.

The suite was **not** run end to end. The GPU available for this work required a reset partway through, so there is no `22 passed` regression result, no negative control through the full fixture, and no repetition. That evidence has to come from the SGLang GPU job on this pull request.

## Related Issues

Source issue [DYN-4425](https://linear.app/nvidia/issue/DYN-4425) is tracked outside GitHub.

- Relates to #15136 — same fixture, pins the rendezvous port.
- Relates to #14241 — adjacent health-check diagnostics, left untouched here.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved port allocation to reduce conflicts between worker, service, and frontend processes.
  * Ensured allocated ports are released reliably after process cleanup, including when cleanup or settling encounters an error.
  * Increased reliability for environments running multiple processes or repeated test sessions by preventing stale port assignments from affecting subsequent runs.

title: feat(gms/vllm): orchestrate fenced failover activation
body:
## Overview

This PR coordinates failover ownership, bounded primary teardown, and shadow activation for the single-rank vLLM MVP. The correctness-first default locks before setup; the explicit low-latency mode initializes a standby first and keeps it undiscoverable until takeover.

## Details

- Fence decode and prefill workers before engine setup in the default mode.
- Preserve the explicit preinitialized standby (DYN_VLLM_GMS_LOCK_BEFORE_INIT=0) for the complete lease-aware integration.
- Wake and register the standby only after it owns the lock and completes the post-lock fence.
- Canonicalize both supported shadow-mode environment names before configuration validation, preventing shared writable KV from bypassing orchestration.
- Reject removed private-bootstrap/scratch options and unsupported TP, PP, DP, and headless shadow configurations.
- Bound discovery unregister, wake, and re-quiesce even when cancellation is suppressed.
- Retain ownership and terminate if activation cannot prove that the engine is quiescent.
- Arm descendant EngineCore and GPU workers to die with their parent process.

### Why it is needed

This is the user-visible handoff path. A shadow must remain healthy enough to be monitored but absent from discovery until it exclusively owns shared KV. Every failure path must either restore a known-quiescent state or retain ownership until process death. Multi-rank coordination is deliberately rejected rather than exposing a partially safe path in the TP1 MVP.

## Where should the reviewer start?

Start with components/src/dynamo/vllm/worker_factory.py, then components/src/dynamo/common/utils/graceful_shutdown.py and lib/gpu_memory_service/integrations/common/process_lifecycle.py.

## Validation

- vLLM integration suite: 235 passed.
- Common failover lifecycle suite: 32 passed.
- Focused graceful-shutdown suite: 12 passed.
- Automatic five-process GPU failover passes on the cumulative stack.
- Cumulative pinned Black/isort, whitespace, and DCO checks pass.

## Related Issues

title: refactor(gms): abstract persistent pool ownership backend
body:
Builds on #14719. Related trackers: #14704 and #12053.

## Summary

Introduce a small persistent-pool ownership interface so engine integrations do not need to know which generation of GMS allocation RPCs supplies their backing. Keep the existing v0 backend selected by default.

The interface covers claim, export, inventory, non-destructive unclaim, and explicit destruction. It owns allocation lifetime, not permission to write KV blocks: block leases and generation-fenced content metadata remain separate.

## Why the review fixes are needed

- Mapping-failure rollback needs to unclaim without destroying retained bytes. Route it through the selected backend instead of bypassing the interface with a direct v0 RPC.
- Define repeated same-session claims as idempotent, and reject changing their shared/exclusive mode without unclaim. This gives the upcoming v1 backend the same contract as v0.
- Separate permanent geometry/mode incompatibilities from temporary owner contention. Only contention is retried; bound each backoff by the remaining configured budget.
- Report allocation exhaustion as `MemoryError` through the adapter. The v0 wire shape is unchanged; the daemon uses a distinct error code for OOM.

The first two commits introduce the interface and adapter. The follow-up fix commit completes cleanup and aligns claim behavior; unlike the original extraction alone, that commit deliberately hardens daemon semantics.

## Scope

This does not select v1 in either engine, change KV write permission, or change inference-engine hooks. The next PR, #14818, implements the v1 pool capability. Full v1 engine recovery remains a separate integration step.

## Validation

- At this PR's updated tip: 65 focused contract, adapter, retry-budget, and persistent-allocation tests passed.
- Project pre-commit checks passed across both PRs' changed files.
- The stacked v1 PR adds shared v0/v1 conformance tests over real Unix sockets and a real-CUDA killed-client byte-survival test.

Earlier TP1/TP2 engine failover measurements belong to the pre-fix revision. They are historical evidence, not new failover measurements for this update.

title: fix(sglang): fence predecessor writers before crash takeover
body:
Part 8 of 14 in #14704. Builds on #14712.

## Why

The launcher lock proves one descriptor closed; it does not prove every child and outstanding CUDA writer is quiescent.

## What changes

- Give children shared writer-cohort guards tied to parent death.
- Release ownership only after the previous cohort exits.
- Retain a conservative CUDA quiescence fence after cohort exit.
- Reject cooperative handoff before unregistering or pausing.
- Make crash-triggered fencing and release exactly once.

The shadow becomes active only after process fencing, cohort drain, and the CUDA fence. Normal pause/resume does not transfer ownership.

## Scope

Data parallelism is explicitly rejected by #14709 before cache construction. This lifecycle therefore fences the supported direct scheduler-child hierarchy; it does not claim to support SGLang DP-controller topology.

## Validation

42 shared failover, writer-lifecycle, and SGLang safety tests pass at this prefix.

Next: #14714 adds focused TP1 lifecycle tests.

title: feat(sglang): orchestrate warm TP1 crash failover
body:
Part 7 of 14 in #14704. Builds on #14711.

## Why

Fast recovery needs a preinitialized shadow, but it must not serve or write shared KV until the active engine is fenced.

## What changes

- Give the primary an exclusive failover lock before activation.
- Keep lock-before-init as the conservative default: it prevents a standby from touching shared KV before it owns the lock, at the cost of cold initialization after takeover.
- Support the explicit `DYN_SGLANG_GMS_LOCK_BEFORE_INIT=0` mode used by the failover E2E: initialize the shadow, pause it outside discovery, then acquire the lock for warm takeover.
- Promote the shadow only after it acquires the released lock.
- Monitor child processes and bound discovery unregister/register work.
- Reuse the persistent allocation and content directory during promotion.

This supports crash failover. Cooperative ownership handoff is intentionally unsupported. Subsecond recovery claims apply to the explicit preinitialized-shadow mode, not the conservative default.

## Validation

The cumulative TP1 launcher-only crash E2E produces exact output, adopts six HBM pages, reuses 384 cached prompt tokens, and leaks no persistent allocation.

Next: #14713 strengthens writer fencing.

title: fix(gms/sglang): make HBM publication and adoption fail closed
body:
Part 5 of 14 in #14704. Builds on #14709.

## Why

A partial rollback after SGLang inserts a cache entry could make an in-use page allocatable again. A partial adoption could expose incomplete KV.

## What changes

- Validate hashes, pages, generations, writer epoch, and manifest before mutation.
- Separate reversible pre-insert failures from fatal post-insert failures.
- Make directory retirement and capacity reclamation transactional.
- Reject unsupported modes and layouts.
- Define the rank-consistency contract later activated by TP2.

## Safety invariant

A native-visible entry has a valid lease and complete directory record, or the engine fails closed.

## Validation

84 directory-resilience, transaction, lease, and cache tests pass at this prefix.

Next: #14711 installs the integration against current SGLang APIs.

title: test(gms/vllm): prove local persistent-KV failover
body:
## Overview

This PR proves the complete single-rank vLLM MVP with the production automatic takeover path. It starts an active primary and a preinitialized standby, kills the primary, and passes only if the standby acquires ownership, promotes metadata, hydrates vLLM's native index, and serves the preserved KV.

## Details

- Harden parent-first process teardown so the primary can run bounded cleanup while late descendants are still swept.
- Run the weights GMS daemon, KV/directory daemon, frontend/router, primary vLLM, and standby vLLM locally.
- Use numeric engine identities and the same flock, post-lock fence, directory promotion, wakeup, and discovery-registration sequence as production.
- Do not call directory_promote() or resume() from the test.
- Prove the waiting standby does not interrupt the active primary.
- Require byte-identical output, cached tokens on the first successful shadow response, persistent allocation-count equality, and positive HBM adoption and bulk-hydration counts.

### Why it is needed

Earlier coverage manually promoted metadata and resumed the shadow, so it could not detect failures in the real automatic activation path. This is the TP1 MVP acceptance boundary. TP>1, Kubernetes, continuous-stream interruption benchmarks, other engines, and storage tiers remain later work.

## Where should the reviewer start?

Start with tests/gpu_memory_service/test_shadow_failover.py, then the small harness additions in tests/gpu_memory_service/common/.

title: feat(gms): implement persistent pools for v1
body:
Stacked on #14814. Related trackers: #14704 and #12053.

## Summary

Implement the persistent-pool ownership interface using typed GMS v1 RPCs. A client disconnect drops its claims but retains daemon-owned backing for another client to attach. Reuse the existing persistent allocation store, separate from transactional weight/KV epochs.

## Review fixes

- Enforce session-mode isolation: persistent sessions cannot enumerate, export, allocate, free, commit, or abort transactional allocations.
- Preserve the legacy `ErrorResponse` wire shape. Persistent-pool error codes use a separate tagged response, with old/new decoder compatibility tests.
- Fail checkpoint preparation while persistent clients remain attached or retained persistent backing exists in either domain. Rejection preserves bytes and permits explicit cleanup; it never silently destroys KV.
- Complete non-destructive unclaim through the common interface, align claim semantics with v0, and retry only transient ownership contention.

## Validation

- Full GMS daemon suite: 366 passed.
- Broader local regression matrix: 744 passed (11 ring, 366 daemon, 45 common, 87 SGLang, 235 vLLM). TensorRT-LLM skipped because its interpreter environment is unavailable. This matrix is not a new engine-serving failover benchmark.
- Shared conformance tests exercise both real Unix-socket transports: repeated/shared/exclusive claims, size/mode rejection, FD ownership, inventory, unclaim, destruction, and OOM cleanup.
- Real-CUDA test: a separate process writes a 2 MiB pool, synchronizes, and receives SIGKILL without cleanup. A replacement client verifies the same allocation ID and every byte. Passed independently on each of the two available GPUs.
- Regression tests cover legacy error decoding, transactional-session isolation, orphaned pools in both checkpoint domains, and bounded contention retries.
- All applicable project pre-commit checks passed.

## Scope boundary

This implements v1 persistent backing, not complete v1-backed vLLM/SGLang failover. Existing v1 sleep integrations still use ephemeral KV epochs. A follow-up must explicitly select the backend and wire incarnation/GPU identity checks, block leases, content-directory adoption, index hydration, and import-failure cleanup through the engine lifecycle.

The GPU test proves allocation-byte survival across a client crash, not metadata recovery, engine output correctness, TP2 failover latency, or daemon-crash survival. Persistent-pool checkpoint/restore is deliberately rejected until implemented. Engine-level TP1/TP2 failover and baseline/primary/shadow latency trials remain required for that follow-up.

title: feat(gms): propagate and harden tensor-parallel rank liveness
body:
Part 12 of 14 in #14704. Builds on #14716.

## Why

Rank 0 can remain alive after another TP rank crashes. Waiting for a long NCCL timeout delays removal and takeover.

## What changes

- Add a lightweight heartbeat channel with startup grace and bounded detection.
- Propagate peer-rank failure to the launcher.
- Use the same fail-closed fencing path as local child death.
- Install the GMS signal hook after SGLang lazily creates native handlers, preventing first-request replacement.

## Validation

28 liveness and failure-propagation tests pass at this prefix. The cumulative TP2 E2E passes crashes of rank 0 and rank 1.

Next: #14718 tightens post-warmup collective timeouts.

title: feat(gms/sglang): persist native unified-cache pages
body:
Part 4 of 14 in #14704. Builds on #14708.

## Why

title: refactor(router): reference implementation for #14103 — KV-cache reuse metrics on RouterRequestMetrics (do not merge)
body:
## Overview

Reference implementation for the review of #14103 — **not for merge as-is**. This branch is stacked on #14103's head (`3919a0d5d`), so the diff here includes that PR; the four commits that are actually proposed are visible on the compare view: https://github.com/chanh/dynamo/compare/codex/ppc-funnel-request-trace-compat...ai-dynamo:dynamo:neelays/pr14103-kv-histograms

It keeps every definition from #14103 unchanged — per routing attempt, every pool, retries included, query-only excluded, worker-side stages only after a completed stream with a valid prompt-matched report, raw unweighted router estimates — and changes only how the values are recorded, named and labelled.

## Details

- **Where the series live.** The four stage series become histograms on the existing `RouterRequestMetrics`, registered the same way as `input_sequence_tokens`; `_sum` carries the totals the counters carried, `_count` and the buckets add the per-attempt distribution. The separate `CacheLossWorkerStageMetrics` struct and its closure registration are removed.
- **How the guard records them.** The route estimate is stored on the `RequestGuard` at construction; the worker report is kept as `enum WorkerReport { Tokens([u64; 2]), Overflowed }` and recorded once from `finish` / `abort` / `Drop`. `CacheLossTracking`, `CacheLossFinalization` and `finalize_cache_loss_state` are removed (−127 lines in `request_guard.rs`). Selector and worker-side code are unchanged.
- **Names.** `dynamo_component_router_kv_{best_eligible_cached_prefix,selected_cached_prefix,worker_lookup,worker_reused}_tokens` and `router_kv_worker_outcomes_total{result}`; no `loss` / `funnel` / `stage` in series, identifiers or the worker payload key (`engine_data.cache_loss` → `kv_cache_hit`; the values inside are vLLM's own fields, untouched).
- **Labels.** `phase = aggregated | prefill | decode` (from `tracker.phase()`, the same label the frontend exports on `stage_duration_seconds`) and `model`. Routing hosts are per model but share the process-global `RouterRequestMetrics`, so without these labels the prefill and decode attempts of a disaggregated request — and different models — land in one series.
- **Catalog** rewritten to describe pools/phases, retries, the `router_input_sequence_tokens` population change (query-only excluded), `router_kv_hit_rate` (weighted) vs the raw selected-worker estimate, and backend coverage (vLLM only for the worker-side stages).

## Verification

- Same two end-to-end scenarios run through the real `RequestGuard` on #14103's head and on this branch give identical values: complete attempt `[75, 60, 90, 85, 1, 0]`, attempt without a worker report `[75, 60, 0, 0, 0, 1]` (best, selected, lookup, reused, complete, incomplete).
- #14103's unit expectations ported with the same literals, including the overflow case; export test with #14103's inputs (96/64/80/72) gives the same totals under the new names.
- `cargo test -p dynamo-llm --lib --no-default-features kv_router`: 373 passed; targeted: 9 passed; `timing`: 32 passed; clippy clean in changed files; Python handler tests: 4 passed.
- `worker_selection` criterion bench, merge-base vs #14103 head: flat (the PR's selector work has no measurable cost). Histogram vs counter: 7.5 ns vs 1.9 ns per observation on `prometheus 0.14`.

title: feat(request-trace): match header capture entries by prefix and add a denylist
body:
## Overview:

DYN_REQUEST_TRACE_HTTP_HEADER_CAPTURE_LIST only matches header names literally, so behind a
gateway you have to list every injected header by hand, and the list rots as soon as the
gateway renames anything. Nothing tells you either, the header just stops showing up.

Items 1 and 2 of #14220. Not item 3, the capture-all sentinel, that should wait for redaction
like the issue says.

## Details:

Capture entries can end in a star now to match a prefix, and there's a new
DYN_REQUEST_TRACE_HTTP_HEADER_DENY_LIST that subtracts after the capture list matches:

```
DYN_REQUEST_TRACE_HTTP_HEADER_CAPTURE_LIST=x-someplatform-*,x-request-id

```

A lone star in the capture list is dropped at load with a warning, since capture-all should
wait for redaction. The deny list keeps it, because deny-all only subtracts.

Capture lists with no prefix entry keep the old per-entry get_all, so existing configs don't
change. Docs updated too.

Heads up that #14265 is changing the value side of the same function. This only touches name
matching, happy to rebase whichever lands first.

title: fix(request-trace): emit pre-stream cancellations
body:
## Overview

Today, Dynamo can miss the final `request_end` trace when a client cancels a request before Dynamo sends the first response item. The request is counted as cancelled by the frontend, but its trace has no ending record.

This change writes the same existing `request_end` record for that cancellation path. It does not add a new event type or change the trace schema.

## What changes

- Keep the information needed for the final trace until the request finishes or is cancelled.
- If the engine marks the request as killed before the first response item, write one `request_end` record.
- Keep the current behavior for normal stream completion and cancellation after streaming begins.
- Prevent duplicate ending records if normal completion and cleanup both run.
- Leave other early errors unchanged.

A stream that is merely cleaned up is not enough to create a trace. The engine must have marked the request as killed.

## Validation

- All 70 focused request-trace tests passed.
- `cargo fmt` and `cargo check` passed.
- We deployed the patch on ARM64 under mirrored production traffic.
- During one complete hour, all 715 trace-eligible frontend completions had exactly one `request_end` trace: **715 / 715 (100%)**.
- All four cancelled requests in that hour had exactly one matching `request_end` trace.
- A direct cancellation before the first response produced `request_payload`, then `request_end` 456 ms later.
- An unpatched control during the same period had 816 traces for 817 eligible completions (99.88%).

## Where should the reviewer start?

Start in `lib/llm/src/request_trace/integration.rs` with `RequestEndTraceState::drop`, the one-time `emit` helper, and the cancellation tests.

title: feat(router): add block-weighted KV overlap counters
body:
## Overview:

`dynamo_component_router_kv_hit_rate` is a histogram of per-request `overlap_blocks / isl_blocks`, so averaging it (`_sum / _count`) gives a mean of ratios — each request counts the same regardless of length.

Backend engines report prefix cache hits and queries as running totals, so a hit rate computed from them is a ratio of sums, weighted by blocks. The two are equal only when every request has the same ISL, and they drift apart as ISL spreads out. Two requests show it:

| | ISL | overlap |
|---|---|---|
| A | 1 block | 0 |
| B | 100 blocks | 99 |

- mean of ratios: `(0/1 + 99/100) / 2` = 0.495
- ratio of sums: `99 / 101` = 0.980

The per-request ISL weight is lost when the ratio is computed before the observation, so it cannot be recovered from the exported histogram (`_sum`, `_count`, or buckets).

The useful setup is two views of KV reuse: what the frontend predicted when it chose a worker, and what the worker actually observed. The worker view already exists — backends export it. The frontend view exists too, but only as a request-weighted histogram, so the two cannot be read side by side even though they are measuring the same thing from different vantage points.

## Details:

Adds two counters next to the existing histogram:

- `dynamo_component_router_kv_overlap_blocks_total` (counter, f64) — predicted overlap blocks summed over routed requests.
- `dynamo_component_router_kv_isl_blocks_total` (counter) — request ISL blocks summed over routed requests.

Dividing them gives the frontend view of KV reuse, aggregated the way backends aggregate theirs, so the frontend and worker numbers can finally be put on the same chart. Both are recorded in `RouterRequestMetrics::observe_kv_overlap_blocks`, following the existing `observe_non_max_overlap_selection` pattern, from the same `selection.effective_overlap_blocks` / `isl_blocks` values the histogram already uses.

The two views are not meant to be identical. The frontend records what it predicted when it made the decision; blocks can be evicted before execution, and a decision whose dispatch does not complete is still a decision the router made. That gap is informative rather than an error, which is why this is recorded with the routing decision and kept alongside `kv_hit_rate` rather than moved onto the dispatch or first-token path.

Two notes for review:

- The numerator is a float counter. `effective_overlap_blocks` is fractional under weighted overlap scoring (existing tests assert `5.75`, `3.5`), so an `IntCounter` would truncate up to one block per request.

The histogram is kept. It carries the per-request distribution, which the counters do not, so the two are complementary rather than a replacement.

No change to routing or scheduling behavior.

## Where should the reviewer start?

`lib/llm/src/kv_router/metrics.rs` — `observe_kv_overlap_blocks` plus the two unit tests beside it (aggregation difference, fractional overlap).

Then `lib/llm/src/kv_router/routing_host/kv.rs` for the single call site, next to the existing `kv_hit_rate.observe`.

`lib/bindings/python/src/dynamo/prometheus_names.py` is generated by `cargo run -p dynamo-codegen --bin gen-python-prometheus-names`, not hand-edited.

title: feat(router): expose sequence hashes to request classifiers
body:
## Summary

Request classifiers currently receive prompt counts and session metadata but cannot inspect the sequence hashes already carried by the scheduling request. Add `ClassifyRequest::sequence_hashes()` so a classifier can read those existing inputs before admission, including while its independently polled future is pending.

## Details

- Preserve missing data, present empty sequences, ordering and the host's existing public/keyed/randomized tracking semantics. The accessor does not compute hashes or interpret them as physical KV ownership or residency.
- Copy the supplied sequence into the classifier request so it cannot borrow actor-owned storage across the asynchronous boundary. This costs one sequence copy per eligible scheduling attempt, including retries that subsequently reuse cached classification overrides; requests without a classifier skip this path.
- Keep queue cost, worker selection, reservations and scheduling overrides unchanged. Shared-budget accounting is a separate change.
- Cover the projection through a classifier that yields before reading, after the original scheduling request has been changed and dropped. Keep the regression focused on sequence contents and ownership; remove redundant metadata assertions and explanatory test comments. Extend public plugin compatibility coverage and document scope, lifetime, missing data and copy cost.

## Where should the reviewer start?

- `lib/kv-router/src/plugins/request_classifier.rs`: read-only input contract and owned snapshot.
- `lib/kv-router/src/scheduling/queue.rs`: projection and asynchronous ownership regression test.

## Validation

Using the repository-pinned Rust 1.96.1:

- `cargo test -p dynamo-kv-router --lib --test plugin_api_compat`: 1,062 unit tests passed, 3 ignored (including the explicit CPU benchmark); 1 public compatibility test passed.
- `cargo clippy -p dynamo-kv-router --lib --tests --no-deps`: passed with the existing `schedule_request_with_booking` dead-code warning.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check`, and pre-commit on all four changed files: passed.
- Worker-selection `default_policy_wrapper` benchmark ran before/after, including normal 50-sample 1,024-worker direct/policy cases. These exercise the unchanged selection path; they do not quantify the new classifier snapshot-copy latency.
- Focused docs lint passed. After generating the ignored API reference pages, pinned Fern 5.80.2 `check` reported zero errors. `fern docs broken-links` reports one pre-existing link in `deepseek-v4-pro-0813.mdx` to `/dynamo/recipes/model-recipes/deepseek-v4-pro`; that page is unchanged by this PR.

## End-to-end qualification

Ran a real HTTP/GPU smoke test on head `81b7d8d78bddfab0bbc1e57bf54f0685248ef642`, using source-built Dynamo and statically linked Rust ThunderAgent `23e39302ee233f5a497cd44bc4690d203e97ca91`. A separate lab policy copy reads the public getter at classifier entry and after `await_release`, just before returning the request, and records native state; admission/accounting logic is unchanged.

Environment: one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU/worker, Qwen3-0.6B at `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`, Rust 1.96.1, Python 3.12.13, vLLM 0.29.0, torch 2.13.0; dev/BF16/eager build. Four programs share two distinct 16k-token prefix families. Each runs two turns using its actual preceding output; appending 64 tool tokens makes the continuation cross a complete tracking-block boundary. Four final requests close the sessions.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Real requests / native completions | 12/12 passed: 8 target + 4 final |
| Getter at entry and just before classifier return | 24/24 exact ordered matches to full-block hashes computed from actual prompt IDs, also checked against frontend traces |
| First turn / continuation / final | Four vectors of 256 hashes / four of 257 / four present empty sequences |
| Shared and private content | Same-family first 256 hashes match; different families differ; newly completed private continuation blocks differ |
| Native observation | 109 contiguous snapshots, one classifier instance, no observation write errors; correct registration/release/Sent/Completed ordering |
| Final state and cleanup | Native program/request tables both empty; no harness cleanup error; GPU 0 MiB, 0%, no compute processes |

The observed policy also passes 32 CPU tests against this host. Post-run checks confirm all 5,889 pinned host files, all eight observation-policy source files and the loaded extension are unchanged. Extension SHA256: `4bf9b22d1003dcba0a6b8ee994ce65ccf337b2185e4588d302f952654d48e4bb`. The archived evidence bundle contains 103 verified artifacts, SHA256 `494ca5523e1faba44d558b3d028fb12a97ec4a30ea27632b78e92ce62eb94bd0`.

Scope: one text-only/default-public-hash configuration, with read-only observation and no shared-budget feedback. This is a correctness smoke test, not a latency, physical-residency, capacity-safety or pressure/pause-resume result. Controlled shutdown emits the same channel-close, live-task and semaphore-cleanup diagnostics found in the archived unpatched run; native state and GPU cleanup checks still pass. No previously completed GPU matrix was rerun.


## Classification-input copy cost

The added copy is required by the independently polled future with the current ownership model. I measured the actual `build_classify_request` path, including classifier future construction and its first poll to Pending, against the pre-change base with the identical benchmark. Each timed batch retains all P snapshots; source preparation and cancellation are excluded. This measures CPU input preparation, not pure memcpy, full admission latency or TTFT.

Intel Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus, x86_64/WSL, CPU 0 affinity, Rust 1.96.1 release (opt-level 3, codegen-units 1, thin LTO), system allocator. Each row uses three process pairs in AB/BA/AB order, with five warmups and 40 samples per process. Deltas are medians of paired process medians; brackets give their min/max, not a confidence interval. The fixture uses block_size=16 and ISL=max(1,16*H); the prompt examples below only map hash counts to familiar sizes.

| Hashes H | Retained P | Added preparation, µs/request [pair range] | Additional hash payload |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| none | 1024 | 0.068 [0.059, 0.068] | 0 B |
| 0 | 1024 | 0.058 [0.043, 0.072] | 0 B |
| 256 | 1024 | 0.454 [0.423, 0.471] | 2,097,152 B |
| 512 | 1 | 0.064 [0.061, 0.064] | 4,096 B |
| 512 | 64 | 0.103 [0.078, 0.104] | 262,144 B |
| 512 | 1024 | 0.794 [0.771, 0.814] | 4,194,304 B |
| 8192 | 1024 | 29.793 [28.676, 40.072] | 67,108,864 B |
| 62500 | 1 | 6.625 [6.392, 6.679] | 500,000 B |
| 62500 | 64 | 295.017 [250.590, 304.459] | 32,000,000 B |

The full matrix covers absent/empty/256/512/8,192/62,500 hashes and P=1/64/1,024, with the 62,500-hash case measured only through P=64 (17 conditions). H=256/H=512 corresponds to 16k/32k routing tokens at block_size=64; H=8192 corresponds to 131,072 at block_size=16. The large retained case has meaningful cost: H=62500/P=64 adds about 0.295 ms/request, approximately 18.9 ms additional serial preparation per 64-input benchmark batch. These local measurements do not establish a production worst-case latency bound. Warmups also do not exclude allocator trimming/page faults or predict contention.

**Memory and maximum supported sizes:** each nonempty snapshot allocates/copies `8 * H` bytes; absent/empty snapshots need no hash-buffer allocation. On this build `ClassifyRequest` grows from 224 to 248 bytes. Logical added request-value/payload storage is therefore `24 * P + 8 * sum(H_i)` bytes, excluding enclosing-future layout, allocator metadata/rounding/retained pages and other request state; this is not measured RSS. Original scheduling vectors remain live separately.

There is no classifier-local pending-count cap or universal enforced prompt maximum. The copy precedes classifier-lock/terminal waits and queue admission, so downstream worker/channel limits do not bound these allocations. Frontend token-budget validation is conditional and may leave overflow rejection to the backend; actual hash-vector length is the authoritative size. With externally enforced `P_max` and `H_max` before projection, the hash payload is bounded by `8 * P_max * H_max`. For illustration, 1,024 retained 32k tokens at block size 64 inputs add 4 MiB of hash payload (+24 KiB of request layout on this build); 1,024 inputs of 1,000,000 tokens at block size 16 would add 488.28 MiB of payload. The latter P=1024 case is a calculation, not a measured timing point or a supported-limit claim.

Reproduce a row using the ignored benchmark included in this PR:

```bash
CLASSIFIER_BENCH_HASHES=512 CLASSIFIER_BENCH_PENDING=1024 \
  cargo test --release -p dynamo-kv-router --lib \
  classifier_input_projection_benchmark -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1
```

For the before/after comparison, apply the same benchmark function to base 00207840f88a89401669b258a00a1c5a43228143, rebuild each revision and run the test executable pinned to the same CPU. Use separate Cargo targets or force rebuild after switching worktrees; verify old/new type sizes 224/248 to avoid stale shared-target artifacts. JSON output retains all 40 sample values. This does not change scheduling, add concurrency limits or eliminate the semantic copy; structural shared ownership and lazy retry projection remain separate decisions.

## Related Issues

Relates to #15105.

title: fix(frontend): align DeepSeek V4.1 tool image order
body:
## Overview:

Fix image-to-placeholder mismatches in DeepSeek V4.1 conversations with out-of-order tool results.

The V4.1 prompt formatter sorts tool results into the assistant’s tool-call order, while the preprocessor collects images in message arrival order. If the assistant calls tools A then B but their results arrive B then A, the rendered prompt and collected images can disagree, associating an image with the wrong tool result.

## Details:

- Collect media from V4.1 tool results in the same order used by the prompt formatter.
- Keep each tool result’s image and UUID entries together, preserving their internal order and the positions of interleaved user images.
- Compute message indices without copying image payloads or modifying the original conversation. Apply the ordering to V4.1 requests containing tool messages, using the same normalized model-type and empty-type display-name fallback as prompt formatter selection.
- Cover reversed results, interleaved user images, separate turns, system-message boundaries, and missing or unknown tool-call IDs. Use one representative renderer-order comparison, plus selection parity and a real-preprocessor regression for empty model metadata.

Validation: all 14 V4.1 tests passed in `dynamo-llm` with `--no-default-features`, including actual media collection for the display-name fallback. The seven focused tests also pass against pinned `dynamo-protocols` 5.4.3 and `dynamo-renderer` 5.2.0, with strict Clippy and formatting checks. This change complements native V4.1 image rendering in `frontend-crates`; it does not enable image support by itself.

Start with `lib/llm/src/preprocessor/deepseek_v41.rs`, particularly `media_message_order` and the renderer-parity test. Then review the integration in `lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs`, where the media-collection loop selects the V4.1 ordering.

body:
## Summary

Expose engine-reported cached-token usage before generation finishes in the vLLM and SGLang token-streaming adapters, without repeating unchanged usage metadata on every backend chunk.

Previously, both adapters attached `completion_usage` only at completion. Continuous-usage clients could receive generated-token totals but no cache details before then, including when they disconnected early.

Closes #14850 (vLLM) and #14938 (SGLang).

## Implementation

- Both adapters emit usage on the first usable report per choice, when prompt/cache metadata changes, and at completion. Explicit zero and unavailable cache counts remain distinct.
- vLLM maintains an O(1) request-wide cumulative completion total, advancing it as each choice is emitted so snapshots do not include later, un-emitted choices.
- SGLang captures usage before metadata-upload cleanup clears engine metadata and continues treating incomplete usage as optional.
- The Rust frontend already retains prompt/cache metadata and counts generated token IDs. A regression test verifies persistence and counting across sparse reports and interleaved choices.
- The optional Python vLLM and SGLang chat processors now retain sparse usage metadata and count generated tokens locally. Intermediate usage requires both `include_usage` and `continuous_usage_stats`; existing terminal/non-streaming usage behavior is retained. Metadata survives suppressed deltas and SGLang batched flushes.

For the synthetic 1,024-chunk, stable-cache example discussed in review, additional non-final MessagePack usage payload decreases from 114,194 bytes to 110 bytes (99.9%). This is an encoded-payload calculation, not a throughput or CPU benchmark.

## Reviewer entry points

- `components/src/dynamo/vllm/handlers.py`: `BaseWorkerHandler.generate_tokens`
- `components/src/dynamo/sglang/request_handlers/llm/decode_handler.py`: `_process_token_stream`
- `components/src/dynamo/frontend/{vllm,sglang}_processor.py`: `_generate_and_stream`
- Backend delta/usage tests, Python frontend usage tests, and the Rust `delta_common.rs` metadata-persistence test.

## Validation

- 44 supplemental CPU checks passed, executing actual backend/frontend methods with engine imports bypassed. These are **not full backend-import or GPU test runs**.
- Rust regression passed: `cargo test -p dynamo-llm --no-default-features sparse_backend_usage_preserves_metadata_and_counts_interleaved_tokens --lib` (on the rebased sparse-emission commit; unchanged in the frontend follow-up).
- All commit-time pre-commit hooks, including static pytest-marker validation, and DCO checks passed.
- Pre-merge CI for current head `54a4202b1` passed: 22 checks passed, 6 skipped, none failed or pending at the final check. This includes all Rust test/Clippy jobs. Full backend/GPU CI still requires maintainer authorization.
- CodeRabbit's fresh review of `54a4202b1` reported no blocking issues. All 18 existing review threads have been addressed and resolved; maintainer approval remains required.

Coverage includes stable-report suppression, positive/zero/unavailable cache counts, late-arriving metadata, ordered per-choice totals, empty terminal chunks, metadata-upload cleanup, frontend usage-option gating, parser-suppressed chunks, and SGLang batching.

### Pending runtime validation

- [ ] Normal backend and frontend test modules with their backend dependencies installed.
- [ ] Live repeated-prompt cache-hit accounting, including continuous usage before an early disconnect.
- [ ] Live final-only streaming and non-streaming responses.
- [ ] Disaggregated prefill/decode cache accounting.

The SGLang aggregated and disaggregated decode paths share the modified stream processor. The adapters forward engine-provided counts; they do not estimate prefill hits or reinterpret transferred KV as cache hits. Separate worker text-mode implementations, dedicated multimodal handlers, and TensorRT-LLM are outside this change.

title: feat(operator): add role-specific multinode PodTemplates
body:
![Multinode role PodTemplate API and lowering overview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/911b49ba-3a4d-474a-95b5-f0734ec54688)

## Summary

A multinode engine is one Dynamo component, but it produces different leader and worker Pods. Before this change, both roles had to start from one component-level `podTemplate`.

This PR builds on the explicit `leader` and `worker` roles merged in #14419 and adds:

- a complete, independent `podTemplate` for each role;
- `experimental.flagsInjection: Automatic | Manual` from #12696; and
- role-aware lowering through defaults, backend rendering, DRA/GPU discovery, checkpoints, Grove, and LeaderWorkerSet.

The component remains the inference and lifecycle boundary: one scale target, rollout, Service, and aggregate status. Roles remain internal Pod-producing parts and do not become independently deployable DGD components.

This PR deliberately does not add role-local replica counts or new component-type restrictions. Those are tracked independently in #14477 and #14533.

## API

### Existing mode: one complete template shared by both roles

Existing manifests remain valid. The explicit role list is optional and does not change cardinality:

```yaml
spec:
  backendFramework: vllm
  components:
  - name: decode
    type: worker
    replicas: 2                 # complete engine instances
    multinode:
      nodeCount: 4              # Pods per engine instance
    podTemplate:                # complete source for leader and worker
      spec:
        containers:
        - name: main
          image: example/vllm:1.5.0
          resources:
            requests:
              nvidia.com/gpu: 8
    roles:                      # optional; implicit when omitted
    - name: leader
    - name: worker
```

This produces two complete engines. For every engine replica, role counts continue to derive from `multinode.nodeCount`: one leader and `nodeCount - 1` workers. The example therefore produces two leader Pods and six worker Pods.

### New mode: one complete template per role

The component-level `podTemplate` is omitted and every required Pod-producing role supplies its own complete template:

```yaml
spec:
  backendFramework: vllm
  components:
  - name: decode
    type: worker
    replicas: 2
    multinode:
      nodeCount: 4
    roles:
    - name: leader
      podTemplate:
        metadata:
          labels:
            example.com/engine-role: leader
        spec:
          nodeSelector:
            example.com/pool: leader
          containers:
          - name: main
            image: example/vllm-leader:1.5.0
            resources:
              requests:
                nvidia.com/gpu: 1
    - name: worker
      podTemplate:
        metadata:
          labels:
            example.com/engine-role: worker
        spec:
          nodeSelector:
            example.com/pool: worker
          containers:
          - name: main
            image: example/vllm-worker:1.5.0
            resources:
              requests:
                nvidia.com/gpu: 8
```

Role templates are complete inputs, not patches:

```text
Valid:   component.podTemplate
Valid:   every required role has role.podTemplate
Invalid: component.podTemplate + any role.podTemplate
Invalid: only some roles have role.podTemplate
```

There is no inheritance or merge from the component template into a role template.

### Backend command ownership is independent

`flagsInjection` controls backend command and topology-flag generation; it does not choose the PodTemplate source:

```yaml
components:
- name: decode
  type: worker
  multinode:
    nodeCount: 2
  roles:
  - name: leader
    podTemplate:
      spec:
        containers:
        - name: main
          image: example/vllm:1.5.0
          command: [python3, -m, dynamo.vllm]
          args: [--distributed-executor-backend=mp, --nnodes=2,
                 --node-rank=0, --master-addr=leader.example]
  - name: worker
    podTemplate:
      spec:
        containers:
        - name: main
          image: example/vllm:1.5.0
          command: [python3, -m, dynamo.vllm]
          args: [--distributed-executor-backend=mp, --nnodes=2,
                 --node-rank=1, --master-addr=leader.example]
  experimental:
    flagsInjection: Manual
```

| Mode | Ownership |
| --- | --- |
| `Automatic` or omitted | Dynamo generates the backend command and multinode topology flags. |
| `Manual` | The authored command and backend flags are preserved. |

Common operator mutations still apply in both modes, including labels, volumes, DRA integration, checkpoint metadata, and runtime wiring. Manual mode retains the established vLLM MP port and wait-for-leader behavior. Manual mode with GMS or failover remains rejected.

## Lowering and ownership

The controller selects a complete source for each semantic role and then reuses the existing Pod rendering pipeline:

```text
DGD multinode component
├── leader template ─┐
└── worker template ─┴── defaults/backend/DRA/GMS/checkpoints
                            ├── Grove: one PCSG with leader + worker cliques
                            └── non-Grove: one LeaderWorkerSet
```

- The DGD/DCD component owns desired replicas, rollout identity, Service, and aggregate readiness.
- `multinode.nodeCount` owns the role cardinality in this PR.
- Each role template owns the full Pod specification for that role.
- Dynamo owns common mutations and, in `Automatic` mode, backend command generation.
- Grove and LeaderWorkerSet remain lowering targets; no new controller ownership boundary is introduced.

## Defaulting, validation, and migration

- Omitting `roles` and all role templates keeps the existing implicit mode.
- An authored role list must contain exactly one `leader` and one `worker`.
- If any role has a `podTemplate`, every required role must have one and the component-level `podTemplate` must be absent.
- Provider overrides and role PodTemplates remain separate concerns; provider overrides are not implicit template patches.
- Switching from implicit mode to an explicit but semantically equivalent role list is allowed and hash-neutral.
- Migrating from one component template to complete role templates is allowed and creates one normal component rollout because template ownership changes.
- A real change to either role template changes the enclosing component revision and follows the existing rollout path.
- Role list order is not semantic and does not change the component hash.
- `roles[].replicas` is not part of this API; its defaulting and validation are the subject of #14477.
- Restrictions on which component types may use `multinode` are the subject of #14533.

## Independent review follow-up

A strict post-rebase review found and this revision fixes five integration gaps:

- engine GPU width now sums leader and worker role templates, including DRA-backed GPUs;
- automatic SnapshotJob ownership survives role-template selection in the LeaderWorkerSet path;
- legacy `component-type=worker` plus `sub-component-type=prefill|decode` labels survive upgrades;
- manual vLLM MP launch supports a shell program authored entirely in `command`; and
- API comments and generated references describe role-aware container lookup.

## Validation

- `make manifests`
- `make generate-api-docs`
- `uv run --no-project --with pydantic --with pyyaml --with black python3 docs/fern/scripts/gen_kubernetes_api.py`
- `go test ./api/... ./internal/dynamo ./internal/controller ./internal/webhook/validation`
- `go vet ./api/... ./internal/dynamo ./internal/controller ./internal/webhook/validation`
- `./bin/golangci-lint-v1.64.8 run`
- `uv run --no-project --with pydantic --with pyyaml --with black --with pytest --with griffe pytest -q docs/fern/scripts/tests/test_gen_kubernetes_api.py docs/fern/scripts/tests/test_api_reference_regressions.py` (75 passed)
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- pre-commit hooks

Closes the role-specific PodTemplate part of #14417 and advances #12696. Follow-ups: #14477 and #14533.

title: recipes: add DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash SGLang aggregated recipe for 4x H200
body:
## What this adds

`recipes/deepseek-v4.1-flash/sglang/agg-h200/deploy.yaml` — the Hopper counterpart to the existing `agg-gb200` recipe.

Today the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash SGLang recipes cover GB200 only (`agg-gb200`, `disagg-gb200`). Applying `agg-gb200` to 4x H200 (sm_90) does not start: the model fails at pool sizing or OOMs during CUDA graph capture, depending on which value you change first. This recipe is the working configuration, with each delta explained inline.

Validated serving `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` on 4x H200 at TP4/EP4, 512K context, KV-aware routing, aggregated.

## Deltas from `agg-gb200`, and why each one is required

| Setting | agg-gb200 | agg-h200 | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mem-fraction-static` | 0.8 | **0.92** | Weights are 119.83 GB of the ~141 GB per card; 0.8 does not hold them |
| `max-running-requests` | 256 | **64** | At 256 the SWA pool (~15.8 GB) exceeds the entire KV budget at this mem-fraction |
| `context-length` | (1M) | **524288** | 1M does not fit at TP4 on this card |
| `cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` | 64 | **32** + pinned `cuda-graph-bs` | The cap alone still captures ~20 sizes and OOMs |
| `speculative-algorithm` | DSPARK | **omitted** | Draft head + widened verify batches exceed the remaining capture workspace |
| `chunked-prefill-size` | — | **4096** | Also feeds SWA pool sizing |

Three of these are non-obvious enough to be worth stating explicitly:

**`mem-fraction-static` is inverted relative to vLLM's `--gpu-memory-utilization`.** It reserves weights + KV pool *only*; CUDA graphs are captured from what remains *outside* it. Too high OOMs in graph capture, too low fails at pool sizing — the two failure modes pull the knob in opposite directions, so it has to be tuned by reading both log lines together:

```
Memory pool end. avail mem=...
Capturing batches (bs=N avail_mem=...)
```

**`max-running-requests` must be pinned, not left to default.** Unset, `deepseek_v4_hook` forces it to 256. SWA cost is roughly `N*656 + 2*chunked_prefill_size + swa_prefix_tails*384` tokens; measured 32 → 2.30 GB, 64 → 3.57 GB, 256 → 15.78 GB. The last does not fit.

**The graph-capture OOM is transient workspace, not retained graph size.** All six retained graphs total ~0.36 GB, so raising `mem-fraction-static` to "make room" makes it worse. Pinning the captured set is what makes it fit — and each size must be its own argument, since a single space-separated string fails to parse.

## Two smaller additions

- **`PYTHONHASHSEED=0` on the worker.** Block hashes are compared across replicas; unpinned, Python salts `str` hashes per process and the KV router index becomes noise. Harmless at `replicas: 1`, required above it. This applies to the GB200 recipe too (`replicas: 2`) — happy to split it into its own PR if you'd prefer.
- **No `runAsUser: 0` and no `IPC_LOCK` / `SYS_PTRACE` / `SYS_RESOURCE`.** Aggregated serving does not need them; they're only required for disaggregated KV transfer. Dropping them lets the recipe run under restrictive pod security policies.

Resource requests reflect measured usage (103–106 GiB per worker) rather than the GB200 figures.

## Scope and honesty about validation

- The **SGLang tuning above is exactly what we run** and is the substance of this contribution.
- The surrounding pod plumbing was **normalized to this repo's conventions** (upstream's `shared-model-cache` PVC, HF model id, no node selectors or pull secrets) to match the sibling recipe, since our own deployment runs under a restrictive pod security policy. We are re-testing the manifest in this exact shape end to end and will report the result on this PR before it merges. Flagging it up front so a reviewer isn't the one to discover a volume/PVC assumption that doesn't hold.
- `replicas: 1` fills 4x H200. With one worker the KV router indexes events but has nowhere to route; scale to 2 (8x H200) for routing to do any work.
- This uses the `1.6.0-deepseek-v4.1-flash-dev.1` snapshot runtime, which upstream marks as not recommended for production. Same image as `agg-gb200`.

## Testing

Deployed and served continuously on 4x H200. Benchmarked with KV-aware routing enabled: 55% prefix-cache reuse, KV hit rate 0.624, 0 errors across the run. Cold start is dominated by weight load (~17 min from a shared RWX volume), which is why the startup probe allows up to 3h.

  * Supports up to 512K-token contexts, high-throughput request handling, reasoning and tool parsing, metrics, and KV-aware request routing.
  * Includes health monitoring and shared model/configuration storage for reliable service operation.

title: feat(profiler): bounded scalar/Pareto candidate selector
body:
## Summary
 
Implements "select bounded scalar/Pareto results" — [tracking issue #13545](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/13545), item 5. 
Given the current selection and one newly-scored `Candidate`, returns the updated selection. Maintaining state across a stream of candidates is the caller's job — same design as `compute_actions` in the DGDC reconcile-diff work (`#14931`).
 
## What's confirmed, not assumed
 
- `Candidate.objectives` is a dict keyed by `OptimizationTarget` value.
- Each objective's maximize/minimize direction is a **search-level** property (`[(t.value, t.maximize) for t in resolved_pareto_objectives]`), not a per-candidate field — callers supply it via `ObjectiveSpec`, one per objective, at the goal level.
- Scalar goals break score ties by fewer GPUs: *"rank (best score, ties → fewer GPUs) for every scalar goal."* Implemented exactly, with dedicated tests for both the tie-break firing and *not* firing when it shouldn't.
- Pareto results are *"only non-dominated candidates."*
- `ParetoGoal.max_candidates` defaults to `5`, matching the real, confirmed `RecommendationSpec.MaxCandidates` default on the `v1beta2` DGDR type (fetched directly from the `#13603` PR branch).
## Eviction policy
 
NSGA-II crowding distance when the front exceeds `max_candidates` — the standard algorithm for this exact problem, not an arbitrary rule. Boundary candidates (best on any single objective) get infinite distance by construction and are never evicted; eviction thins dense interior clusters instead of trimming the front's own extremes.
 
## Files
 
- `components/src/dynamo/profiler/sweeper/candidate_selector.py` (new)
- `components/src/dynamo/profiler/tests/unit/sweeper/test_candidate_selector.py` (new)
No existing files touched.

title: feat(profiler): DGDC reconcile-diff algorithm
body:
## Summary

Adds the reconcile-diff algorithm for DGDC lifecycle management — [tracking issue #13545](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/13545), item 5 ("materialize DGDCs, and reconcile their lifecycle"). Given a desired set of candidates and the current set of DGDCs, decides what to create, delete, and update.

## Key design decision

Identity is a **content hash** of the rendered spec + evaluation-context fields, not `Status.Rank`. Rank changes over time as better candidates are found and worse ones evicted, often with no change to the candidate's own content — using it as identity would force unnecessary delete+recreate churn. Using a content hash instead means a real content change and an identity change are the same event, which lines up naturally with `DynamoGraphDeploymentCandidate.Spec`'s real, confirmed CEL immutability rule (`"spec is immutable"`) — there's no "update spec" code path in this module at all.

Confirmed against the real `v1beta2` Go types (fetched directly from the `#13603` PR branch)


## Files

- `components/src/dynamo/profiler/sweeper/dgdc_reconcile_diff.py` (new)
- `components/src/dynamo/profiler/tests/unit/sweeper/test_dgdc_reconcile_diff.py` (new)

title: fix(local_model): keep local directory as source_path when a custom model name is set
body:
## Summary

When `LocalModelBuilder` loads a local directory with a custom served name and no explicit `source_path`, the source falls back to that name. If metadata self-hosting is disabled or unavailable, `attach()` can then publish bogus `hf://<served-name>/...` metadata URLs.

Preserve the canonical local directory before applying a different served name. Explicit local or Hugging Face sources still take precedence. Default names, including an explicitly supplied name equal to the canonical path, retain the existing absent-source representation and MDC checksum.

The change is confined to `LocalModelBuilder` and regression tests in `local_model.rs`. Metadata transport, frontend resolution, the checksum algorithm, and model-weight distribution are unchanged. Renamed local models acquire an explicit source and therefore a different MDC checksum; this PR does not introduce mixed-checksum WorkerSet admission.

## Validation

Validated on macOS after rebasing onto `8612fc179`:

- `cargo test -p dynamo-llm --no-default-features --lib metadata_publish_tests`: 3 passed. Covers actual `attach()` publication and frontend discovery with a custom name, unchanged default/same-path names, and explicit local/HF source precedence.
