title: fix(frontend): return the Anthropic error envelope on bad request bodies
body: ## Summary `/v1/messages` and `/v1/messages/count_tokens` answer every failure they produce themselves with the nested Anthropic envelope, and #13102 added the same envelope for unmatched Anthropic routes, with the note that Anthropic clients expect that shape: ```json {"type":"error","error":{"type":"not_found_error","message":"Route not found: GET /v1/messages/missing"}} ``` Requests that fail *before* reaching the handler did not get it. Both handlers used Axum's `Json` extractor, whose rejections are `text/plain`. Measured on `main` with the Anthropic endpoints enabled: ``` Content-Type: text/plain -> 415 text/plain Expected request with `Content-Type: application/json` body "{not json" -> 400 text/plain Failed to parse the request body as JSON: ... ``` So a client written against the documented envelope parses an unmatched route fine and throws on the two most common request mistakes. I checked the obvious counter-hypothesis before concluding anything: this router layers `anthropic_error_middleware`, so it looked like this might already be handled. It is not. That middleware only rewrites 422 to 400, and neither rejection is a 422. The fix reads the body explicitly and reports unsupported media type, oversized body and malformed JSON through `anthropic_error`. `handler_count_tokens` gains the `HeaderMap` it needs to see the content type. Content-type parsing reuses `is_json_content_type` from the openai module rather than reimplementing it, so this route keeps the same notion of what counts as JSON, including parameters and `+json` suffixes. **The policy is unchanged, only the envelope**: an absent `Content-Type` is still rejected, matching `ensure_json_content_type` today. ### Overlap worth flagging Two things this touches are also touched elsewhere, so whoever merges second should expect a trivial rebase rather than a surprise: - #13696 makes the identical one-line change exposing `is_json_content_type` as `pub(super)`, for the same reason on `/inference/v1/generate`. Whichever lands first, the other drops that hunk. - @chanh has #13268 open to treat an absent `Content-Type` as JSON. If that lands, this route should follow it, and reusing the shared helper is what keeps that a one-place change. This is the same class as #13685 and #13696 but a third module with a third envelope, so it is deliberately not a copy of either: Anthropic nests under `{"type":"error","error":{...}}`, `generate` uses `{"error":{...}}`, and the openai routes use a flat `{message,type,code}`. ## Validation Measured before and after by driving the route through `spawn_service(|b| b.enable_anthropic_endpoints(true))`: | input | before | after | |---|---|---| | `Content-Type: text/plain` | `415 text/plain` | **`415 application/json`**, `{"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error",...}}` | | `{not json` | `400 text/plain` | **`400 application/json`**, same envelope | Added `test_anthropic_bad_content_type_returns_anthropic_envelope` and `test_anthropic_malformed_json_returns_anthropic_envelope`, asserting the response `content-type` as well as the body, because the status codes were already correct on `main` and only the shape was wrong. **Both confirmed red first** by restoring `anthropic.rs` from `upstream/main` and re-running: ``` the 415 must use the Anthropic envelope, not Axum's text/plain rejection the 400 must use the Anthropic envelope, not Axum's text/plain rejection ``` - Full crate: **2043 tests**, which is `main`'s 2041 plus the two added, with `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean. - The one failure in those runs is `test_oversized_body_returns_json_413`, the pre-existing intermittent I reported on #13624. It is unrelated to this change and fails at the same rate on `main`. Not verified here: no GPU, so the success path of `/v1/messages` was not exercised end to end. This change only affects how the request body is read and how that read is reported when it fails. --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **Bug Fixes** - Anthropic Messages and token-count requests now provide consistent JSON-formatted error responses for unsupported content types, oversized request bodies, read failures, and malformed JSON. - Invalid requests now return the appropriate HTTP status codes, including 400 for malformed JSON and 415 for unsupported media types. - Request body size limits are enforced consistently across supported Anthropic endpoints.

title: ci: add GB300 runner validation lanes to the PR workflow
body:
## Overview:

Adds three temporary pre-merge lanes (`vllm-gb300-test`, `sglang-gb300-test`, `trtllm-gb300-test`) that exercise the `aws-gb300-tester-arm-gpu-v2` ARM64 runner pool against real test workloads, so the pool can be validated before these lanes move to `nightly-ci.yml`. Each lane carries a TODO marking it for that move.

## Details:

Supporting changes in `.github/workflows/shared-test.yml`:

- `arm_runner` is now an input (default `prod-tester-arm-v2`) rather than a hardcoded literal in `runs-on`, so a lane can target a different ARM pool.
- GPU-test gating moves from a hardcoded `matrix.platform == 'amd64'` to `contains(fromJSON(inputs.gpu_test_platforms), matrix.platform)`, defaulting to `'["amd64"]'`. This stays separate from `platform` on purpose: several existing lanes deliberately include `arm64` in `platform` for CPU coverage while running that entry on a GPU-less ARM runner, so GPU gating cannot be derived from `platform`.
- `amd_runner` becomes optional with a default, since the new arm64-only lanes never read it.
- A `models_dir` input is threaded through to the `pytest-local` action as `--models-dir`, letting a lane use a pre-populated model cache instead of downloading models online.

In `.github/actions/pytest-local/action.yml`, `--models-dir` is passed only when the mount actually holds a HuggingFace cache layout — either a `hub/` subdirectory or a `models--*` entry, the two shapes `tests/hf_cache.py` knows how to consume. The `HF_HOME` probe immediately above can create the directory empty, which would satisfy pytest's `is_dir()` check and then fail every model load under `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`. The guard falls back to online pre-download with a warning instead.

The GB300 lanes use 120 minutes per GPU stage. Both the parallel and sequential stages each receive `gpu_test_timeout_minutes`, so twice that value must stay under GitHub's 360-minute default job timeout; overrunning it cancels the job mid-stage and reports no results at all.

## Where should the reviewer start?

- `.github/workflows/shared-test.yml` — the two changed `if:` conditions and the `runs-on` expression. Worth confirming the `'["amd64"]'` and `prod-tester-arm-v2` defaults leave every existing caller on its current behavior.
- `.github/workflows/pr.yaml` — the three new lanes, and specifically that they are added to the `backend-status-check` aggregate `needs:` list.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files` passes on all three changed files.
- Audited every caller of `shared-test.yml` across `pr.yaml`, `post-merge-ci.yml`, `nightly-ci.yml`, and `dynamo-pipeline.yml`: no existing caller sets the new inputs, so the defaults reproduce today's behavior exactly.
- Exercised the `--models-dir` guard under bash against five cases — `HF_HOME` layout (`hub/`), bare cache (`models--*`), empty directory, junk directory, and missing directory. Only the two real layouts enable the flag; the rest fall back to online pre-download.
- The GB300 lanes themselves are unproven by definition — validating that runner pool is the purpose of this PR.

## Known follow-ups (deliberately not in this PR)

- The lanes select the full `(gpu_1 or gpu_2)` pool without a `pre_merge` filter and are wired into the aggregate `backend-status-check`, making them merge-blocking. Both are accepted while the lanes stay in PR stage and will be resolved when they move to nightly.
- `gpu_parallel_max_vram_gib: '280'` collapses the parallel stage to one test per GPU, since the orchestrator computes `int(budget / 280)` and clamps to 1, while the largest profiled test in the tree is 56 GiB.

title: test(bindings): remove cancellation test timing races
body:
## Summary

An already-cancelled request can return a response before its stop signal reaches the worker. The cancellation tests assume that the stop always arrives first, so they can fail under scheduling delays. In [this CI failure](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/actions/runs/35161913923/job/105024142718), the stop reached the worker after 140 ms, while the mock handler waits only 100 ms before its first response.

Use an explicit server cancellation event in all four affected tests. The two pre-cancelled request tests consume early responses and wait for stream termination plus server acknowledgement under one five-second deadline. They accept only the exact expected terminal cancellation error; request errors and other stream errors still propagate. The two mid-stream cancellation tests replace their 200 ms sleeps with bounded event waits, including the metadata case.

Preserve the tests' cancellation order and existing response, metadata, and stopped/not-killed assertions. Add a 30-second module timeout to bound fixture setup and teardown, and remove the redundant event reset. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

- Full cancellation module: **14 passed**.
- Four affected tests, TCP and NATS, repeated 50 times each with isolated services and forked processes: **400 passed**. The four groups ran in parallel.
- The module and repeat runs used the module timeout marker without a command-line timeout override.
- Seven temporary helper checks passed: early responses and expected terminal cancellation still require acknowledgement; missing acknowledgement times out; request and unrelated stream errors propagate. The temporary checks and logs are excluded from this PR.
- Black, isort, Ruff, Flake8, and `git diff --check` passed.

Tests ran outside the sandbox with an existing local `ai-dynamo-runtime` 1.5.0 wheel built from `99224822bdbbd45a520d2ec1a4c9e38ca967e8e7` with unrelated AISimulate changes. The relevant runtime cancellation and TCP code matches the inspected source.

title: feat(router): bind subagents under their parent session's group
body:
## Summary

A request that carries a parent session id now binds under an internal key derived from that parent, so the subagents of one parent land on one worker while the parent keeps its own binding. This is active whenever session affinity is enabled (`--router-session-affinity-ttl-secs`); it adds no new flags. An explicit per-request worker target stays on the request's own session, so it is neither rejected against the group nor able to move it. Under the default `hard` mode the group is pinned to its first worker and does not migrate because of load; the binding resets only when the target becomes unusable or dispatch fails.

Parent ids come from the agent headers Dynamo already recognizes (`X-Dynamo-Parent-Session-ID`, `x-claude-code-parent-agent-id`, `x-codex-parent-thread-id`, `x-parent-session-id`). The group key is `\u{1}sg:<blake3(parent)>`: the prefix cannot appear in a header value, so no client can claim it as its own session id, and the fixed length keeps long parent ids within the id limit.

**Behavior change:** clients that already send parent ids get sibling grouping automatically once session affinity is enabled.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p dynamo-llm --lib -- session_affinity::tests kv_router::routing_host::tests`: 83 passed.
- `cargo check -p dynamo-ext-proc` and `cargo check --manifest-path lib/bindings/python/Cargo.toml`: clean.
- Python router-config suite: 64 passed. `cargo fmt` and docs pre-commit hooks: clean.

## Known limitations

- Because siblings share one binding, a concurrent fan-out waits for the first sibling's dispatch to commit before the others are placed.
- With TensorRT-LLM's `attention_dp_config.kv_cache_routing_conversation_affinity` enabled, the engine re-places the attention-DP rank unless the worker runs with `--conversation-affinity-dp-rank-source dynamo`; without it the group is exact at the instance level only.

title: fix(vllm): background the aggregated multimodal worker
body:
Source issue: [DYN-4251](https://linear.app/nvidia/issue/DYN-4251).

## Summary

`examples/backends/vllm/launch/agg_multimodal.sh` backgrounded its frontend but ran the vLLM worker in the foreground, so the script sat inside the worker and never reached `wait_any_exit` during startup. `wait_any_exit` watches background jobs only. Adding the missing `&` puts this script back on the contract every other aggregated vLLM launch script already follows.

## Validation

Two branches behaved incorrectly before the change, measured by running the real script against a stand-in `python`:

- A frontend exit during startup stayed hidden until the worker finished — exit after 25 s before, 2 s after.
- `SIGTERM` to the process group during startup left status `143`, because the trap `wait_any_exit` installs was not yet in place. It is now `0`, the clean-shutdown status `examples/common/launch_utils.sh` documents.

A worker failure still surfaces as `code 1` in both arms, so nothing is relabelled into a retryable status.

`tests/serve/test_port_contract.py` gains a scan over every `examples/` script that calls `wait_any_exit` and fails, naming file and line, for any foreground `python -m dynamo.*` service, plus tests for the parser itself. The initial validation covered 107 scripts and 275 service launches. Both the scripts it selects and the launches it finds are read through the same parser, so a call with a trailing comment still puts a script in scope, a quoted command string does not hide a real launch beside it, and a service counts only where bash would run it rather than wherever it is named.

This does not show the reported flake is cured; it did not reproduce here. CI packs these tests co-resident on one card, which a single-GPU environment cannot match, and the worker-side cause of `Main server process exited with code 1` remains unidentified.

The parser regression cases also cover operator continuation newlines, grouped commands, stderr pipelines (`|&`), heredoc delimiter quoting and escapes, here-strings, and escaped quotes in ANSI-C strings.

## Where should the reviewer start?

`examples/backends/vllm/launch/agg_multimodal.sh:122`, then `_split_commands` in `tests/serve/test_port_contract.py` — launch commands span continuations, quotes, pipelines, heredoc bodies and `&&`/`||` lists, so the scan follows bash's own separator rules rather than grepping.

title: feat(sglang): publish KV hint capability for KVCR and forward request hints
body:
## Overview

Companion to the SGLang KVCR direct external linker (https://github.com/ishandhanani/sglang/pull/10, which builds on the KV-hint transport in sgl-project/sglang#38891 and on ai-dynamo/kvcr#39). The router already emits `kv.fetch@1.0` hints to workers that advertise the `router_hint` capability; the SGLang backend never advertised it and never forwarded the hint. This change does both, for both SGLang KVCR modes:

- the direct external linker: `--enable-unified-cache-external-linker --unified-cache-external-linker-backend kvcr`
- the HiCache storage backend: `--hicache-storage-backend kvcr`

## Details

`components/src/dynamo/sglang/kv_hints.py` (mirrors `dynamo/vllm/kv_hints.py`):

- Detects the KVCR mode from `server_args` and reads the KVCR extra config (`--hicache-storage-backend-extra-config`).
- When `enable_remote_hint` is set, publishes `router_hint_source_control_endpoints`, `router_hint_worker_type`, and `router_hint` (capability last, so a partially observed registration is never capability-only).
- Endpoints are keyed by global DP rank for the ranks this node runs (`local_dp_rank_bounds`). SGLang ranks bind `control_port + engine_global_attention_rank`, so DP rank `d` is published at its block's first port with stride `tp_size // dp_size`.
- Undialable configuration (port 0, wildcard/absent advertise host, a rank past 65535) raises at registration instead of registering a source no peer can reach. IPv6 hosts are bracketed.
- `disaggregation_mode` maps to the router's worker roles (`null`/None -> `aggregated`, `prefill`, `decode`). Same-role routing is preserved; prefill-to-decode KV transfer is untouched.

`_compat.py`: `kv_hints_kwargs(engine, request)` reads the preprocessor's top-level `kv_hint` (falling back to the older `extra_args.kv_transfer_params.kv_hint` nesting) and forwards it as SGLang's `kv_hints` `async_generate` kwarg, dropping it with a one-time warning when the installed engine lacks the kwarg so requests recompute instead of failing.

Handlers: the aggregated, decode, and prefill `async_generate` calls forward the hint.

## Validation

`components/src/dynamo/sglang/tests/test_sglang_kv_hints.py`, 17 cases: mode detection for both modes, publication in both modes and key order, worker type mapping, DP port striding with node-local bounds, no publication without KVCR or without remote hints, undialable endpoints raising, IPv6 bracketing, extra-config parsing, and hint kwarg extraction and engine-signature filtering. All pass locally. `isort`, `black`, `flake8`, and `ruff` pass on the changed files.

End-to-end routing through a live Dynamo frontend with two SGLang KVCR workers has not been run yet; it is tracked with the SGLang PR's GPU validation.

title: perf(mocker): streamline native block pool hot paths
body:
## Overview

Streamline native-G1 mocker block-pool hot paths while preserving physical-capacity, prefix-reuse, and eviction semantics.

## Summary

- replace the timestamp-keyed inactive `BTreeMap` with an intrusive oldest-to-newest LRU
- resolve and reserve a destination's resident prefix in one block-pool traversal
- derive inactive membership from zero references and zero pins, avoiding a separate membership discriminant
- keep constant-time invariant checks in debug builds and exhaustive structural validation in unit tests
- validate intrusive-list updates before mutation so failed invariants cannot leave a partially updated list

## Details

The native block pool now stores optional predecessor and successor IDs directly in each cached copy. Inactive membership is derived from `refs == 0 && pins == 0`; active entries carry empty links. Pinning removes an inactive entry before incrementing its pin count, and insertion/removal validates the target, neighbors, endpoints, and length before changing the list.

`reserve_resident_prefix` walks candidates until the first partial block or cache miss, pins the resident prefix, and reserves the fresh suffix atomically. Its hit vector is preallocated from the layout length.

Ordinary debug builds perform only constant-time occupancy and endpoint checks. The full LRU/hash-index sweep is compiled only for tests and runs once per logical operation rather than inside eviction loops or twice during cached allocation.

### Performance evidence

The performance run predates the review-fix commit. It compared control `329aba5d0c91c4520c5ce8a1707310fa68fccc69` with performance commit `97f68ec59d9085d18944ffd9bfe2e7c9bd9e981f`. The follow-up commit `c87c93a5a38101dca8f4e938b041ee025d54c9ac` was not rebenchmarked.

Both arms used one native-G1 mocker with 32 workers on CPUs `12-23`, frontend/AIPerf on CPUs `0-11`, 128,000 blocks per worker, block size 16, concurrency 512, all 336 Weka trace entries, a 120-second measured phase, and basic `taskset` isolation only.

| Metric | Control | Performance commit | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Mocker CPU ms/request | 23.5446 | 22.4133 | **-4.80%** |
| Mocker CPU s / 1M modeled tokens | 0.301957 | 0.286989 | **-4.96%** |
| Throughput (req/s) | 255.429 | 258.795 | **+1.32%** |
| Peak RSS (MiB) | 7107.2 | 7183.8 | +1.08% |

Both arms registered all 32 workers and completed with zero request errors or cancellations. This was intentionally one accepted run per arm; unrelated host activity remained on the mocker CPU mask.

The aggregated-worker workload exercises the intrusive LRU but not disaggregated destination reservation, so the measured CPU improvement should primarily be attributed to the LRU change. Prefix fusion is correctness-tested but not performance-qualified by this run.

The measured RSS value reflects the earlier `Option<InactiveLinks>` representation. The review follow-up removes that outer discriminant, eliminating up to 31.25 MiB of embedded cached-copy state at the benchmark's aggregate 4,096,000-block capacity, but that reduction was not measured in a new E2E run.

## Where should the reviewer start?

1. `lib/mocker/src/cache/vllm_block_pool.rs`: cached-copy state, intrusive-list validation/mutation, and invariant-check boundaries.
2. `lib/mocker/src/kv_manager/vllm_backend.rs`: destination prefix reservation and the native-manager coverage for disabled prefix caching and partial-block termination.

title: feat(runtime): multiplex TCP response streams
body:
## Summary

- hard-replace dedicated worker-to-frontend response sockets with the versioned `tcp_response_mux_v1` transport
- maintain four persistent response connections per worker-process/frontend pair while keeping request streams on their existing dedicated sockets
- multiplex logical responses by UUID with stream-local cancellation, bounded admission, per-stream byte credits, and independent slow-consumer backpressure
- batch response data for up to 1 ms by default to reduce TCP writes and per-packet operating-system overhead; interval `0` enables opportunistic batching and the maximum is 100 ms
- simplify the hot path to direct bounded writer ingress with ordered and urgent lanes, removing trait-object dispatch, per-stream writer mutexes, writer-owned stream maps, ready rings, and round-robin scheduler bookkeeping
- use a compact binary codec from the first byte of each response connection and remove the JSON handshake, connection-level credits, cumulative connection acknowledgements, and physical connection IDs
- keep operational metrics for connections, streams, writes, admission stalls, resets, reconnects, failure fanout, and opt-in Linux TCP segment diagnostics

This is a coordinated transport cutover: response connections do not fall back to the former dedicated protocol. Frontends and workers must be upgraded together.

## Design

### Protocol and batching

`MuxCodec` handles the entire connection. `ConnectionHello` contains the protocol version and frontend UUID, and the frontend returns an empty `ConnectionReady`. Subsequent frames use a 21-byte header containing payload length, frame kind, and logical-stream UUID.

Successful prologues and resets have empty payloads. Failed prologues carry UTF-8 error text. `Prologue` and `Reset` use an urgent lane; `Data` and `End` use an ordered lane. `End` is the sole completion acknowledgement and flushes preceding data for its stream.

Data flushes at the earliest of:

- `DYN_TCP_RESPONSE_BATCH_INTERVAL_MS` (default `1` ms)
- `DYN_TCP_RESPONSE_BATCH_MAX_BYTES` (default `65536`)
- `DYN_TCP_RESPONSE_BATCH_MAX_FRAMES` (default `64`)
- an urgent frame becoming ready

### Backpressure and ownership

Each stream has eight ordered-frame permits and byte credits controlled by `DYN_TCP_RESPONSE_STREAM_WINDOW_BYTES` (default `262144`). A connection-wide queued-byte semaphore bounds userspace memory. TCP supplies physical-connection backpressure; there is no additional connection credit window.

The connection writer exclusively owns batching and socket writes. Producers submit concrete frames through bounded channels without trait-object or boxed-future dispatch. Frontend `Data` routing stays in a connection-local `HashMap`, so decoded data frames do not touch the global lifecycle map.

Pending and active response entries share one lifecycle `DashMap`, with pending-to-active replacement performed atomically. Host pools live for the worker-process lifetime, and one process-wide maintenance task warms new frontend pools to four connections and repairs failed connections.

## Performance qualification

### Final simplification versus mandatory-mux baseline

Three interleaved, freshly restarted repetitions at 8 workers / concurrency 1,024, ISL 1,024, OSL 256, and mocker speedup 10:

| Metric | `06d22825e9` | Final simplification | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Request throughput | 953.5 req/s | 978.2 req/s | +2.59% |
| Output throughput | 250,185 tok/s | 256,659 tok/s | +2.59% |
| TTFT p50 | 205.66 ms | 199.41 ms | -3.04% |
| TTFT p95 | 434.38 ms | 443.16 ms | +2.02% |
| Request latency p95 | 1,066.88 ms | 1,060.93 ms | -0.56% |
| Frontend CPU/request | 2.545 ms | 2.473 ms | -2.84% |
| Worker CPU/request | 2.159 ms | 1.877 ms | -13.07% |
| Response writes/token | 0.03155 | 0.03214 | +1.88% |
| Response sockets | 32 | 32 | unchanged |

All six runs completed without request errors, cancellations, resets, or connection-failure fanout. Additional very-large-scale qualification also preserved performance after the final simplification.

### Packet reduction versus dedicated responses

Earlier 16-worker / concurrency 2,048 qualification of the 1 ms mux mode measured 0.04705 response segments/token and 0.04708 response writes/token, versus 1.04417 segments/token and an estimated 1.00762 writes/token for dedicated responses. That is 22.2x fewer response segments and 21.4x fewer response writes, with exactly 64 mux response sockets. The final simplification changed writes/token by only +1.88% relative to the mandatory-mux baseline.

For comparison, the 5 ms interval produced larger batches (35.8 frames/write versus 21.5 at 1 ms) and 37.1x fewer response segments than dedicated responses, quantifying the additional packet-reduction/latency tradeoff available through configuration.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all`
- `git diff --check`
- `cargo test -p dynamo-runtime --lib pipeline::network::tcp -- --nocapture` — 50 passed
- `cargo test -p dynamo-runtime --lib metrics::response_mux -- --nocapture` — 1 passed
- `cargo test -p dynamo-runtime --lib -- --skip transport_resolution_falls_back_when_selected_instance_disappears` — 480 passed, 2 ignored, 1 known unrelated hang skipped
- `cargo clippy -p dynamo-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: feat(router): add active sequence sparsity
body:
## Summary

- Add `--router-active-sequence-stride` / `DYN_ROUTER_ACTIVE_SEQUENCE_STRIDE` as a startup-only setting, defaulting to `1` and rejecting values below `1`.
- Retain rolling active-sequence hashes at stride endpoints while leaving KV-indexer hashes, routing-decision hashes, overlap signals, and token accounting unchanged.
- Correct externally visible active and potential decode-block estimates by scaling sparse prompt units while keeping generated-output blocks in physical units.
- Carry the stride on active-sequence add, free, and prefill-complete events; incompatible or malformed replica events are dropped before mutation and recorded through structured warnings and a Prometheus counter.

## Details

Active-sequence replica synchronization currently broadcasts the complete rolling-hash chain for every request. This makes payload size proportional to the full prompt length on every frontend.

This change computes the complete rolling chain first and then samples block positions `n, 2n, 3n, ...`. The sampled vector is used for local active-sequence tracking and is broadcast without receiver-side resampling. `BlockTracker` and `PromptMembershipTrie` remain sparsity-agnostic; outer load projection stores prompt and output components separately and converts sparse prompt units back into estimated physical blocks.

The corrected counts are estimates. Retained stride groups are fully represented, divergence inside a group can conservatively overcount overlap, and an incomplete trailing group is omitted.

`ActiveSequenceEvent.stride` is optional for wire compatibility: missing means stride `1`, while zero is malformed. A receiver drops only an incompatible event and continues processing subsequent compatible events.

Rollout must be coordinated. Deploy this binary everywhere with stride `1` first, then enable a common stride through a coordinated frontend restart. Older receivers may ignore the new field while still consuming the sparse vector.

## Where should the reviewer start?

- `lib/kv-router/src/scheduling/config.rs` for configuration and hash sampling.
- `lib/kv-router/src/sequences/prompt_registry.rs` and `multi_worker.rs` for load correction and event emission.
- `lib/kv-router/src/sequences/replica_sync.rs` and `lib/kv-router/src/protocols.rs` for compatibility enforcement.
- `lib/llm/src/kv_router/sequence.rs` and `metrics.rs` for frontend propagation and observability.

## Validation

title: fix(trtllm): install nixl in dev/local-dev images
body:
## Problem

The TRT-LLM `dev` and `local-dev` images skip `container/deps/requirements.trtllm.txt` because the install block in `trtllm_runtime.Dockerfile` was gated to non-dev targets.

That requirements file currently carries TRT-LLM-only third-party packages, including `msgspec`, `uvloop`, `imageio`, `nixl==1.0.1`, and `nixl-cu13==1.0.1`. `dev` and `local-dev` build the Dynamo wheels from source later in the shared dev stage, so those PyPI packages are never installed there. In particular, `nixl` is not pulled in by the source build, leaving the dev images without the Python NIXL package needed by KVBM.

## Fix

Install `requirements.trtllm.txt` in the stage that has the right Python environment:

- `runtime`: install the requirements in `trtllm_runtime.Dockerfile`, after the Dynamo venv is created and before the Dynamo wheels are installed.
- `dev` / `local-dev`: install the same requirements in `dev.Dockerfile`, after the shared dev stage creates `/opt/dynamo/venv`.

The install is now a plain `uv pip install --no-deps --requirement ...` in both paths. The Dynamo-built wheel installs (`ai_dynamo*`, `kvbm`, and `gpu_memory_service`) remain gated to runtime targets because dev images build those from source.

## Testing

Rendered all three targets with `container/render.py --framework trtllm --device cuda --cuda-version 13.1`:

- `dev` / `local-dev`: `requirements.trtllm.txt` is installed from the shared dev stage after `/opt/dynamo/venv` is created; the Dynamo-wheel block is omitted.
- `runtime`: `requirements.trtllm.txt` is installed into the active Dynamo venv; the Dynamo-wheel block remains present.

Also checked the rendered TRT-LLM targets for `uv pip install --system`, `uv pip install ... break-system-packages`, and `trtllm_pip_flags`; none remain in this install path.

## Follow-up

`dev.Dockerfile` still sets the TRT-LLM dev image NIXL env vars to `/opt/dynamo/nixl`, which is created by the vLLM-CUDA path. That is separate from this missing-Python-package fix and can be handled in a follow-up.

title: perf(mocker): avoid per-token replay request lookups
body:
## Overview

This PR removes the per-token UUID hash-map lookup from aggregate offline replay while keeping live and disaggregated output publication on their existing untracked path. The radix-tree optimization previously included here has moved to an independent PR.

## Summary

- Carry one private optional `ReplayRequestKey` through the existing engine request path and preserve complete backend request-ID validation.
- Store aggregate replay state in a generational `SlotMap`; retain the UUID index only for routing, admission, duplicate detection, and validated terminal removal.
- Keep `EngineOutputs` small: the original `Vec<OutputSignal>` plus private `Empty`, `Untracked`, `Tracked`, and `Mixed` bookkeeping. Appends are infallible; release builds reject mixed tracking, missing keys, stale/reused keys, UUID mismatches, and tracked outputs at live/disaggregated publication boundaries.
- Derive the first nonterminal prefill transition from runtime-owned state, including tokenless nonterminal signals. A first-and-terminal request still skips `prefill_completed`.
- Move the original output vector directly through live and disaggregated publication with no wrapper conversion or replacement allocation.
- Reject duplicate active UUIDs before observable side effects in aggregate and disaggregated replay.
- Preserve output order, speculative bursts, live suppression, attention-DP payloads, one-token completion behavior, and public replay/event formats.

The final diff is 1,025 additions and 311 deletions across 22 files. The follow-up review fix is 303 additions and 176 deletions; it replaces fallible post-mutation output appends and split validation/removal paths instead of adding another tracking abstraction. The obsolete marker-index machinery, wrapper traits, tracked-retain path, and every KV-router change remain gone.

## Details

Each aggregate output carries its request's private generational key in a sidecar aligned with the original signal vector. Nonterminal processing validates the slot and its UUID directly in O(1), without hashing the reverse UUID index. Terminal processing validates both indexes and removes the request before collector, placement, admission, or routing callbacks; index corruption is returned as an error without partially mutating either index.

Live and disaggregated paths never create replay keys. Their publication boundaries call `into_untracked()`, which rejects unexpected metadata and returns the owned `Vec<OutputSignal>` directly. vLLM also fails immediately if request state disappears while generating outputs.

No public API, configuration, event format, scheduling policy, or simulation behavior changes.

## Where should the reviewer start?

- `lib/mocker/src/scheduler/mod.rs` for `EngineRequest` and the compact `EngineOutputs` sidecar.
- `lib/mocker/src/replay/offline/agg.rs` for aggregate `SlotMap` state and output validation.
- `lib/mocker/src/scheduler/vllm/core.rs` and `lib/mocker/src/scheduler/sglang/core.rs` for backend key propagation and request-ID checks.

## Related Issues

None.

## Validation

### Source validation

- `cargo test -p dynamo-mocker replay::offline` — 192 passed
- `cargo test -p dynamo-mocker` — 721 passed
- `cargo test -p dynamo-mocker --features kvbm-offload replay::offline` — 194 passed; the exact base reproduces the same two existing failures:
  - `busy_worker_advances_offload_without_destination_admission`
  - `aggregated_canonical_evidence_covers_real_kvbm_lifecycle`
- `cargo check --manifest-path lib/bindings/python/Cargo.toml --features aic-forward-pass`
- `cargo clippy -p dynamo-mocker --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `git diff --check`

Focused coverage includes duplicate insertion and bidirectional index integrity, completed stale/reused/UUID-mismatched keys before callbacks, mixed-boundary rejection after infallible appends, propagated live-suppression errors, vLLM rejection metadata, nonzero completion-batch counters, zero-copy untracked publication, tokenless nonterminal output, first-and-terminal completion, speculative output, attention-DP propagation, and both scheduler backends.

### Canonical correctness parity

The full correctness-parity protocol passed between exact base `038c642b56a01b0afddd8c194565526faae35d26` and final head `88cefb8f710248b09fd8a10e6c827e3e6665e397`. The preserved two-process base half and a freshly run two-process final-head half cover 16 reports across aggregate/disaggregated SGLang and native-vLLM KVBM. Every report completed 5,000 requests, each final pair was byte-identical, and every final canonical report was byte-identical to its preserved base counterpart.

| Row | Canonical SHA-256 | Pressure coverage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SGLang aggregate | `84d13ec294115d63621805ceaa37e38c4069c38028ceac0b023f0c7b1a7d8a11` | KV overlap and immediate/queued placement |
| SGLang disaggregated | `ed7f2268248c118ed6b9aba7bd47f8c0d7476d4be968bda07097fab23a5a86a6` | 5,000 handoffs; 12 bounded retractions |
| vLLM KVBM aggregate | `079e11aeb65a19d0cb2dcf516e517ae88c8e4733170a2cb413d6281fcd3469c5` | 2 preemptions; nonzero G1/G2 activity |
| vLLM KVBM disaggregated | `f9e3924ad429da3ddeed49919092343f49c8c5e1426e89ddd8b7a8cb1f113cf0` | 5,000 handoffs; 1 preemption; nonzero G1/G2 activity |

### Astra vLLM point comparison

Ordinary release builds used AIConfigurator `0fa09bb7b5`, 12 aggregate vLLM workers pinned to CPU 0, B200 TP4/attention-DP1 and MoE TP1/EP4, 64-token pages, 4,096-token batching/chunking, prefix caching, KV routing/events, and the 187,906-request 2x Astra trace (`b7b2e3dccb90...`). There were no warm-ups. Preflight was 99.67–100% idle on CPU 0.

| Revision | Wall | Processed tok/s | vs. base | vs. pre-fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Base `038c642b56` | 60.149 s | 42.907 M | — | — |
| Pre-fix `de5f5c86c9` | 57.595 s | 44.810 M | +4.43% | — |
| Final `88cefb8f71` | 57.376 s | 44.981 M | **+4.83%** | +0.38% |

All three reports completed 187,906 requests with 2,401,594,588 input tokens, 179,237,676 output tokens, and 2,580,832,264 processed tokens. These are CPU-0 point comparisons, not a statistical-significance claim; routing-induced cache reuse varied from 41.829% to 42.162%.

The final extension SHA-256 is `9b1d5dcb623f8f1eb44377ac6193c409c5f8d880f9ddf024bb019a7726e008bb` (ELF build ID `aadd75e6ff872a1bf15dff7db33588c5af252e65`); the preserved base extension SHA-256 is `a0f9ab62861164069308f6388fb9e8b3c2ba2e269bf0b4c167e56712bb36b6ca`.

### Structural hot-path confirmation

- Aggregate nonterminal outputs validate `ReplayRequestKey` directly in the `SlotMap`; the UUID index is not consulted per token.
- Live and disaggregated boundaries consume the owned signal vector through `into_untracked()` and reject any sidecar, so no conversion allocation is introduced.
- The prior profile's removed per-token UUID hashing remains absent; this rewrite removes wrapper/marker scaffolding without restoring that call path.

title: perf(kv-router): reuse projections and retain fast overlap maps
body:
## Summary

Reduce per-request work in the serial KV scheduler:

- Retain `FxHashMap` overlap data instead of rebuilding it as standard `HashMap` values.
- Reuse the actor's projection-map allocation, while recomputing every request-specific load value. Keep the projection available through selection and booking, then reclaim its storage after request handling ends.
- Inline default candidate construction and scoring.
- Preserve the existing bench-only projection timing event for both allocating and reusable-map callers, with no timing work in normal builds.

Routing policy, candidate order, admission, cancellation, and wire behavior stay unchanged. The two Rust `OverlapSignals` fields and the corresponding `schedule*` and `get_potential_loads` wrapper parameters use `FxHashMap` throughout, avoiding rehashing at the wrapper boundary. This is an intentional in-process Rust source-compatibility change: direct Rust callers supplying `HashMap` must update their map type. Python and HTTP interfaces and worker/frontend wire formats are unchanged. The LLM crate directly depends on the same `rustc-hash` version already in the dependency graph; no dependency versions changed. No diagnostic instrumentation, dense-row cache, or ZMQ changes are included.

## Performance

Prior matched ARM measurements used two NUMA-local frontends, 2,048 mock workers, speedup 10, AgentX 336, concurrency 6,144, BPE threads 8, QUIC responses, replica sync, and four ZMQ I/O threads on each frontend in both arms.

| Measurement | Before | This scheduler change |
|---|---:|---:|
| Mean scheduler request processing | 231.1 us | 180.0 us |
| Mean worker selection | 157.3 us | 105.3 us |
| Steady-load frontend TTFT p99, FE0 / FE1 | 46.4 / 89.7 ms | 33.5 / 33.1 ms |

title: fix(ci): fail test jobs whose pytest stage was cut off mid-run
body:
## Overview:

### Summary

A pytest stage can be reported as a **successful step when its script never reached
the end**. When that happens the runner also drops the step's `$GITHUB_ENV` updates,
so `TEST_EXIT_CODE` is never set and the action's final `exit ${TEST_EXIT_CODE}`
expands to a bare `exit` — which returns the status of the preceding command, zero.
Real test failures are reported green.

[Job 103364334832](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/actions/runs/34534220040/job/103364334832)
(`dynamo-runtime / test / sequential cuda13.0, arm64`) is a clean example:

| | |
|---|---|
| Test result | `test_kv_router_propagates_stream_errors[100] FAILED [ 89%]` |
| Step end | cut off at 95%, mid-line, as `test_mocker_router_soak[nats-random]` started |
| Step outcome | `success`, `duration_ms=585358` |
| Next step's `env:` block | contains `STR_TEST_TYPE`, `HF_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME` — **no `TEST_EXIT_CODE`** |
| `Process Test Results` | printed `⚠️ JUnit XML file not found`, set `FAILED_TESTS=1  # Treat missing XML as failure`, **discarded it**, ran `exit ${TEST_EXIT_CODE}` → `exit` → 0 |
| Job conclusion | `success` — the PR got a green check |

**This is not a regression from #14352.** That job predates the step collapse and
runs the multi-step action, on the standard `k8s` hook rather than `k8s-novolume`,
on CPU arm64 rather than GPU. Truncation is specific to none of those. The
pre-collapse action had the identical hole, because it also read `TEST_EXIT_CODE`
from `$GITHUB_ENV` written by the long step.

### Approach

Judge each stage by a **status file** rather than by the step's exit status or an
env round trip. `pytest-local` clears `test-results/status/<test_type>.exitcode` when
the stage starts and writes the pytest exit code there as its very last action, so
absence of the file means the script did not finish. A new job-level step in
`shared-test.yml` reads one file per stage that ran and fails the job on a missing
file or a non-zero code.

The filesystem is the only channel here that a truncated step cannot corrupt: it
never crosses the container/runner boundary, unlike `$GITHUB_ENV` and the step exit
status. Both hooks keep the workspace across steps, which the existing cross-stage
`test-results/` accumulation already relies on.

Two deliberate choices:

- **Per job, not per stage** — one container-hook round trip instead of four, so
  this does not give back what #14352 bought on the critical path. The step names
  the offending stage in its output, so attribution is not lost.
- **After the JUnit upload** — results are still collected when the check fails.

It also fails when a stage writes a status file that is not in its list, so a stage
added later cannot silently opt out of the check that exists to stop silent passes.

### Scope — what this does not fix

**What truncates the script is still unknown.** The stdin-drain theory I floated on
the sibling issue does not survive this job: its hook runs the step from a *file*
(`sh -e /__w/_temp/<uuid>.sh`), not from stdin, so a child draining stdin cannot eat
the script. Candidates now point at the exec stream dropping — #14352's own
description mentions a "cluster-wide runner exec drop" — which would need the runner
administrators to confirm.

Making the truncation **visible and loud** is the prerequisite for measuring how
often it happens. Expect this step to turn some currently-green jobs red; those jobs
were already not proving what they claimed.

## Details:

`.github/actions/pytest-local/action.yml` — `mkdir -p` now creates `status/`;
`STATUS_FILE` is cleared at stage start so the value read later can only have come
from this run of this stage; the exit code is written immediately before `exit`.

`.github/workflows/shared-test.yml` — `id:` on the four stage steps, and the
`Verify test stages completed` step. Stage outcomes are passed through `env:` rather
than interpolated into the script body, matching the convention #14352 established.

## Where should the reviewer start?

The `Verify test stages completed` step at the end of `shared-test.yml`, then the
two small hunks in `action.yml` that bracket the stage with the status file.

### Validation

- `pre-commit` passes on both files, including `check yaml` and the action-pin hook.
- `bash -n` accepts both the action's `run:` script and the verification script
  extracted from the workflow.
- Replayed the verification logic against seven scenarios, all as expected:

  | scenario | expected | got |
  |---|---|---|
  | job 103364334832: stage truncated, reported success, no status file | fail | fail |
  | job 103046830380: two GPU stages truncated after two CPU stages passed | fail | fail, names both |
  | healthy four-stage amd64 job | pass | pass |
  | recorded non-zero pytest exit | fail | fail |
  | arm64 job, GPU stages skipped | pass | pass |

title: feat(recipes): add DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash vLLM performance recipes
body:
## Summary

Adds four benchmarked vLLM recipes for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash — aggregated and disaggregated, each on B200 and GB200 — alongside the existing day-0 SGLang recipes for the same model.

Every recipe is authored as Kustomize. Each deployment directory holds a `kustomize/base/`, an optional Component for provider-specific networking, and a `.kustomize-matrix.yaml`; the `deploy-*.yaml` files are generated by `scripts/kustomize-matrix.py` and are not hand-edited.

**Serving shapes**

| Target | GPUs | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| `vllm/agg-b200`, `vllm/agg-gb200` | 8 | 2 x TP4 |
| `vllm/disagg-b200`, `vllm/disagg-gb200` | 12 | 2 prefill + 1 decode, TP4 each, KV over NIXL/UCX |

The two aggregated recipes are the same serving configuration, differing only in the architecture label, the GPU product label, and the deployment name. Both pools of each disaggregated recipe carry the aggregated flag set; what differs is the prefill batch budget, the long-prefill cap, the decode CUDA-graph ceiling, and the transport.

**Venue settings are decomposed into Components**, so a base expresses requirements rather than one cluster's observed state:

- `ib-device-pin` (B200) supplies the `UCX_NET_DEVICES` HCA list. Device names are node hardware, so the Component tells you to read your own nodes with `ibstat` first.
- `gke-rdma` (GB200) supplies GKE multi-network RDMA, replaces the base's `rdma/ib` request, and sets the RoCEv2 GID index — which applies on those networks and does not apply on InfiniBand.

Dropped from the source deployments and not shipped: a scheduler priority class, registry pull secrets, a frontend anti-affinity rule that was measurement hygiene, and a hardcoded NVLink clique UUID. The clique requirement itself is real on GB200 and is preserved as the ComputeDomain mechanism.

**Benchmark.** One AIPerf trace-replay Job covers all four targets. It reuses the shared DeepSeek-V4 agentic Mooncake trace through a symlink rather than duplicating the Git LFS blob.

**Docs.** Extends the existing model card rather than adding a second page for the same model. It gains a framework axis, so it now pickers on framework, GPU, and topology; all three vocabularies already exist in `RecipeStyles`, so no style change is needed. Combinations with no recipe render an explicit panel, following the `kimi-k3` page.

## Expected performance

Each row is that target's best SLO-clearing operating point, not the peak of its throughput curve. SLO floors, both p50: per-user output >= 50 tok/s, TTFT < 5 s.

| Metric | GB200 agg | GB200 disagg | B200 agg | B200 disagg |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Output tok/s/GPU | 533.2 | **694.7** | 488.9 | 610.8 |
| Concurrency | 88 | 168 | 88 | 160 |
| TTFT p50 | **296 ms** | 3,237 ms | **210 ms** | 2,389 ms |
| ITL p99 | 128.36 ms | **36.16 ms** | 123.67 ms | **37.97 ms** |

Disaggregation gains ~30% per GPU on GB200 and ~25% on B200, on 50% more hardware, and cuts the ITL tail by more than 3x, at an order of magnitude higher TTFT. The two are not interchangeable.

## Validation

- `scripts/kustomize-matrix.py check` passes for every matrix in the repo.
- **Render-gate:** each rendered manifest round-trips to the serve argv (order-sensitive), behavioural env, and GPU/RDMA resource requests of the deployment that produced the published numbers. All four identical.
- Every rendered manifest validates against the v1beta1 `DynamoGraphDeployment` CRD schema in `deploy/operator/config/crd/bases/`.
- No duplicate environment-variable names survive Component layering, per the guidance added in #15064.
- The referenced trace resolves to sha256 `f20d3f2bc83dd1306cda659fbe34e7c4d85ca5497626c98bc0b1c4d2211379d0`, 3,541 rows — the corpus the numbers were measured on.
- `docs/fern/pages/recipes/_catalog/validate.py` passes.
- `docs_lint.py` reports no findings for the page and no errors overall; `--scan recipes` reports no findings for this recipe tree.
- All new paths are covered by existing CODEOWNERS rules.

## Why this is a draft

The container image is a placeholder pending the published NGC tag. It appears in the four `kustomize/base/deploy.yaml` files and in four catalog `runtime.image` fields, which the catalog validator keeps in sync. Ready for review on everything else.

title: fix(trtllm): resolve the model argument when the local cache reference is broken
body:
Source issue: [DYN-4426](https://linear.app/nvidia/issue/DYN-4426).

## Overview:

`tests/serve/test_trtllm.py::test_deployment[disaggregated_logprobs-2]` reports `Main server process exited with code 1 while waiting for health check`. That message appears only after the child has exited; the linked job log names the death: `Unrecognized model in /models/hub/models--Qwen--Qwen3-0.6B/snapshots`. That path has no commit component and no `config.json`.

## Details:

The worker passed `str(config.model)` to the engine, so TensorRT-LLM resolved the repository id through `huggingface_hub.snapshot_download`. When the Hub API is unreachable it falls back to the local cache and reads `refs/<revision>` without validating it; an empty ref file collapses the path to `<repo>/snapshots`, which exists, so the engine aborts and the worker exits 1.

That call site now goes through the new `resolve_model_path()`, which returns the model string unchanged when the cache reference is usable, the revision is a pinned commit, or no single complete snapshot is present — so healthy and cold machines behave as today. Only an unusable reference plus exactly one snapshot holding `config.json` yields that directory. The helper only reads the cache, never repairs it.

## Where should the reviewer start?

`components/src/dynamo/trtllm/utils/model_path.py`, then the one changed line in `components/src/dynamo/trtllm/workers/llm_worker.py`. The pinned-revision branch has no unit test.

## Validation

`pytest components/src/dynamo/trtllm/tests -m "pre_merge and trtllm and gpu_0"` passes, with one pre-existing missing-codec failure, identical at the base commit. Aggregated and disaggregated prefill/decode GPU runs both returned HTTP 200 and handed the engine the unchanged `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, no fallback. A corrupted shared cache was not reproduced on GPU hardware, so the CI flake rate is not measured here.

## Related Issues

**🔗 This PR is linked to an issue:**

- Relates to [DYN-4426](https://linear.app/nvidia/issue/DYN-4426); no GitHub issue tracks it.

title: build(llm): use HF tokenizers rc.2 for encode and decode
body:
## Summary

Switch Dynamo's default HF serving path to the official crates.io `tokenizers = "=1.0.0-rc.2"` release for both encoding and decoding. The dependency uses the `hf-tokenizers` alias, disables default features, and enables `regex`. Fastokens and Baseten retain their existing controls; their fallback-to-HF paths now use the RC too. There is no legacy serving fallback.

- Add a private `hf_runtime` adapter that owns one RC `PipelineTokenizer`. It preserves single/batch ordering and cardinality, returns Dynamo's existing encoding/decode types, and keeps the existing streaming and prefix-cache wrappers.
- Keep the startup configuration loader and `tokenizer_config.json` special-token merge. Serialize the prepared configuration in memory, run `canonicalize_str`, and construct the RC pipeline with `from_json`. Model files are not modified, and the old tokenizer is dropped after construction.
- Disable RC padding/truncation and pass through `add_special_tokens`. Embedding BOS/EOS processing still bypasses the prefix cache.
- Give conversion, construction, encode, and decode errors model/path context. Reject unsupported configurations without emulation or automatic simplification.
- Repair the empty byte-level mock vocabularies with the complete byte alphabet while preserving their declared special-token IDs. Update the root, Python-binding, and KVBM lockfiles together.

Older tokenizer dependencies remain for startup preparation and other shared-crate, benchmark, and multimodal consumers. Public request APIs, backend names, and Python Transformers dependencies are unchanged; no shared-crate release is required.

### Compatibility limits and draft status

This PR stays in draft because validation found two additional RC parity failures. Both now produce startup errors:

1. A normalized added token can decode to its normalized matching text rather than its declared content. For example, `CONTROL` with lowercase normalization decodes as `control`, while v0.21.4 returns `CONTROL`.
2. An added token above a sparse model vocabulary can receive a different ID. In the repaired Llama mock, a new token with legacy ID `128011` received RC ID `267`.

The adapter checks that each prepared added-token ID resolves to its original content in the RC vocabulary. It rejects changed IDs or stored forms. This check is conservative: normalized added tokens whose stored forms change are rejected even if a later decoder could restore the text. No legacy encode/decode call is used by the adapter.

Byte-level BPE must have a direct ByteLevel decoder, or a sequence containing only that decoder. The RC bypasses configured decoder transformations on this path, so other decoder layouts are rejected. Upstream conversion/construction errors handle other limits, including ByteLevel `add_prefix_space=true`, unsupported pre-tokenizer/Metaspace/post-processor layouts, nonzero BPE dropout, and incomplete byte alphabets.

References: [official rc.2 release](https://github.com/huggingface/tokenizers/releases/tag/v1.0.0-rc.2), [official Tokenizers v1 article](https://huggingface-tokenizers-v1.static.hf.space/index.html). The article compares against v0.23; these tests use Dynamo's current v0.21.4 as the oracle. No performance claim is made.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p dynamo-llm --test model_card --test preprocessor --test chat_template_render_errors --locked`: 60 passed (17 model-card, 40 preprocessor/embedding, 3 chat-template).
- `cargo test -p dynamo-llm --lib --locked discovery::watcher::tests::`: 25 passed.
- `cargo test -p dynamo-llm --lib --locked test_hf_rc_embedding_bos_eos_bypasses_prefix_cache`: 1 passed.
- `cargo check -p dynamo-llm --locked`.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `git diff --check`.
- `cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1` for the root, `lib/bindings/python`, and `lib/bindings/kvbm` workspaces. All resolve RC `1.0.0-rc.2` with only the `regex` umbrella feature.

Parity coverage includes byte-level BPE, byte-fallback BPE, WordPiece, Unigram, and WordLevel; single/batch and empty inputs; Unicode; special-token skipping and the first added-token ID; config-only special tokens and matching flags; cache hits/extensions; disabled serialized padding/truncation; embedding BOS/EOS; and streaming across split UTF-8 sequences with prompt context. Unsupported settings and the two added-token failures have negative tests.

All builds and test runs were outside the sandbox. Validation covers the included configurations, not universal compatibility with all HF models.

## Where should the reviewer start?

Start with `lib/llm/src/hf_runtime.rs` for the serving adapter and compatibility checks, then `lib/llm/src/model_card.rs` for construction and backend selection. Parity and rejection cases are in `lib/llm/tests/model_card.rs`.

## Related Issues

- [x] Confirmed — no related issue linked to this PR.

title: feat(router): add agentic routing preset
body: ## Summary ### Live result at a glance On the same 8x H200 NVL aggregate-serving setup, fixed-lane synthetic AgentX workload, seed, concurrency-16 soft knee, and full-restart contract, `agentic=(2,4,64)` improved over the default router cost `(1,1,0)`: | Headline metric | Default | Agentic | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Fixed-window completed-output throughput | 348.679 tok/s | 377.483 tok/s | **+8.26%** | | Drain-inclusive completed-output throughput | 268.748 tok/s | 290.882 tok/s | **+8.24%** | | Run-level p95 TTFT | 17.663 s | 10.047 s | **-43.12%** | | Run-level p95 ITL | 62.807 ms | 48.606 ms | **-22.61%** | | Paired-common trajectory E2E mean / p50 / p95 | baseline | lower | **-3.30% / -3.24% / -1.91%** | | Fully completed trajectories | 8 | 9 | **+1** | The trajectory comparison uses the eight exact complete trajectories common to both arms; 6/8 were faster with the agentic preset. The ninth agentic-only completion is counted as a system-progress outcome, not paired latency evidence. Run-level TTFT/ITL include the differing amount of work admitted by the duration-bounded workload (580 versus 629 completed requests); on the 255 exactly matched requests, p95 TTFT improved 46.9% and p95 ITL improved 6.14%. ### What this PR changes Add an experimental `--agentic` / `DYN_ROUTER_AGENTIC` KV-router preset for aggregate agentic workloads. The preset follows the existing shared `--load-aware` configuration pattern and sets the live-selected cost function: - `overlap_score_credit=2` - `prefill_load_scale=4` - `decode_active_request_weight=64` The frontend automatically selects KV routing. The same shared lowering is used by the standalone router and Squeeze-Evolve. `--agentic` fails closed when combined with `--load-aware`, clears the deprecated overlap-weight override, and leaves queueing, cache tracking, router TTL, and active-request expiry under their existing controls. The flag is explicitly experimental. The active-request term is block-based and was validated with 16-token router blocks, so other block sizes require separate validation. ## Validation ### Live aggregate serving Tested on one 8x H200 NVL system with Qwen3-32B-FP8, SGLang 0.5.16, eight TP1 aggregate workers, 16-token KV pages, and full frontend/worker restarts between arms. The fixed-lane synthetic AgentX workload used concurrency 16 at the measured soft latency knee, a 900-second send window plus full drain, and one frozen seed. | Router cost `(overlap, prefill, active)` | Fixed-window output | Drain output | Complete trajectories | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Default `(1, 1, 0)` | 348.679 tok/s | 268.748 tok/s | 8 | | Conservative nominee `(0.5, 4, 0)` | 371.564 tok/s | 283.336 tok/s | 9 | | Agentic `(2, 4, 64)` | **377.483 tok/s** | **290.882 tok/s** | 9 | Against default, the agentic preset improved fixed-window/drain completed-output throughput by **8.26% / 8.24%**. On the eight exact common complete trajectories, mean/p50/p95 trajectory E2E improved by **3.30% / 3.24% / 1.91%**, with 6/8 trajectories faster. Against `(0.5, 4, 0)`, it improved fixed-window/drain throughput by **1.59% / 2.66%** and exact nine-trajectory mean/p95 E2E by **0.13% / 0.84%**. This is a narrow Pareto win: trajectory p50 regressed 0.62% and foreground p95 regressed 0.85%, so `(0.5, 4, 0)` remains the conservative fallback. The bounded one-factor screens showed the interaction was material: `(2, 4, 64)` reached 309.533 tok/s fixed-window versus 271.744 default, 294.294 overlap-only, 297.189 prefill-only, 290.417 active64-only, and 295.172 for `(2, 4, 0)`. Adding active64 to `(2, 4, 0)` improved fixed/drain goodput by 4.87% / 7.89% with no queues, retractions, router pending/backpressure, KV mismatch, or measured-traffic severity in either short arm. All long arms completed workload/analyzer/deployment validation with rc=0. Measured frontend/worker traffic had zero warnings/errors/fatals, KV-source mismatches, retractions, router pending requests, backpressure, or non-OK KV events. At the deliberately loaded knee, the selected long arm briefly reached engine queue depth 1 in 4/643 samples; it fully drained and ended with all workers idle. Campaign caveats: this is one long seed with eight common complete trajectories, aggregate rather than P/D-disaggregated serving, and a duration-bounded synthetic AgentX workload. The benchmark used 4,200-second router TTL and active-request expiry to keep legitimate long requests alive; this preset intentionally changes only the cost function. The workload also used `cache-bust=none`, so these are controlled intra-campaign results rather than a formal AgentX submission. ### Code validation - `65 passed` in `components/src/dynamo/common/tests/configuration/test_kv_router_args.py` - Ruff format/check passed for all five touched files - Commit hooks passed, including isort, Black, flake8, codespell, Ruff, and repository consistency checks --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit - **New Features** - Added an agentic routing preset configurable through the command line or environment variables. - The preset automatically enables KV routing, KV events, and reuse with optimized cost settings. - **Validation** - Prevented load-aware and agentic presets from being enabled together. - Applied preset settings consistently across frontend, router, and SqueezeEvolve configurations. - **Tests** - Added coverage for agentic preset behavior, defaults, and invalid combinations.

title: ci: scope the token for the PR title lint workflow (OPS-8530)
body:
## Overview

`lint-pr-title.yaml` declares no `permissions:` block, so its job inherits the repository default token. It is the only `pull_request_target` workflow in the repo without one — `label-pr.yml`, `pr_full_ci_reminder.yaml` and `trigger-ci-approval-flow.yml` all scope theirs.

```yaml
permissions:
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
```

## Why these three scopes

`ytanikin/pr-conventional-commits` is a Docker action whose `token` input defaults to `${{ github.token }}`. Its `githubapi.js` calls `octokit.rest.issues.addLabels` **and** `octokit.rest.issues.createLabel` — the latter creates the repository label when it does not already exist. That create path is repository-level, so `pull-requests: write` on its own is not enough; `issues: write` is required too. Scoping this to `pull-requests: write` alone would have broken a workflow that currently works.

`contents` is deliberately left unset, which means `none`. The job has no checkout step and the action only calls the issues API, so it never reads repository contents. That matches `pr_full_ci_reminder.yaml`, the other `pull_request_target` workflow here that runs without a checkout. (An earlier revision of this PR included `contents: read`; it was dropped in 7344d6f675 after review.)

## Validation

`pre-commit run --files .github/workflows/lint-pr-title.yaml` passes, including `check yaml` and the actions SHA-pinning hook.

**This change cannot be exercised before merge, and that is worth knowing up front.** `pull_request_target` always runs the workflow definition from the base branch, so the "Lint PR" check on *this* PR executes `main`'s copy, not the version in the diff. The first real exercise is the next PR-title event after merge.

If the scopes turn out to be short, the failure is loud and immediate rather than silent — the action's README documents it as `Error: Resource not accessible by integration` — and the fix is to widen this one block.

## Where should the reviewer start?

The whole diff is the eight added lines. The judgement call worth checking is `issues: write`, explained above.

## Related Issues

Internal tracking: OPS-8530

title: fix: escape backslashes in the events table script and tighten the snapshot shard file mode (OPS-8531)
body:
## Overview

Two unrelated one-line correctness fixes, one commit each.

### 1. Escape backslashes in the community-events Markdown escaper (`b165549`)

`escapeMd` in `.github/scripts/update-events.js` escapes `[ ] | ` * _ ~` but not the backslash itself. A backslash in a calendar event title therefore passes through untouched, and the character after it ends up with only that stray backslash in front of it — which Markdown consumes as an escaped backslash, letting the next character re-open formatting in the generated README table.

Adding `\` to the character class fixes it:

```diff
-  return str.replace(/\r?\n/g, ' ').replace(/[[\]|`*_~]/g, '\\$&');
+  return str.replace(/\r?\n/g, ' ').replace(/[\\[\]|`*_~]/g, '\\$&');
```

### 2. Create snapshot shards without group or world write (`3687a1b`)

`DeviceToFileWriter` opens shard files with mode `0o666`, so their final permissions depend entirely on the umask the process happens to be running under. `0o644` keeps read access exactly as it was and only drops the group and other write bits, so no existing consumer can be affected.

It also lines the writer up with the rest of the package — `v1/server/rpc.py` sets an explicit mode for its socket rather than relying on the umask. `0o600` would be tighter still; I went with `0o644` because it cannot change behaviour for a reader running as a different user. No in-tree consumer was found either way, so if the owner knows these shards are single-user, `0o600` is the better end state and I'm happy to switch it.

## Validation

**Fix 1** — exercised in a real node 20 runtime against the before/after implementations:

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `back\slash` | `back\slash` (backslash lost) | `back\\slash` |
| `\*text*` | `\\*text\*` (asterisk can reopen) | `\\\*text\*` |
| `plain title`, `a\|b`, `[link]`, `` a`b`c ``, `x_y_z`, `~s~`, `multi\nline` | unchanged | unchanged |

Every input other than the two backslash cases is byte-identical to before.

**Fix 2** — `python3 -m pytest lib/gpu_memory_service/tests/test_v1_weight_artifact.py` passes (2 passed) in the CUDA 13 container. No test asserts the shard file mode; the only `st_mode` assertion in the package covers the RPC socket and is unrelated.

**Both** — `pre-commit run --files <changed>` passes (black, flake8, ruff, isort, codespell, actions-pinning and the rest).

## Where should the reviewer start?

Both diffs are one line each. `lib/gpu_memory_service/snapshot/disk.py` is the one worth a moment's thought — see the note above on `0o644` vs `0o600`.

title: fix(runtime): stop FileStore creating buckets after shutdown
body:
Source issue: [DYN-4415](https://linear.app/nvidia/issue/DYN-4415).

## Summary

`FileStore::shutdown` deleted the files the store owned but left the store able to create new ones. Because `Runtime::shutdown` returns before the main cancellation token is cancelled, a live actor could still call `get_or_create_bucket` and recreate `<root>/v1/<bucket>` on disk. When the caller is removing that root, the removal fails with `ENOTEMPTY` — the mechanism behind the `[Errno 39] Directory not empty: 'v1'` failure reported in DYN-4415.

## Details:

`FileStore` shares an `Arc<AtomicBool>` shutdown flag with its clones and buckets:

- Bucket creation holds `active_dirs` across the shutdown check, directory creation, and registration. Shutdown sets the flag before draining under the same lock.
- Cached buckets reject `insert`, `compare_and_replace`, and `delete` after shutdown while holding the directory mutation lock. In-flight mutations finish before shutdown cleanup takes that lock.
- `delete_owned_files` remains available for shutdown cleanup.
- The expiry thread stops on the shutdown flag or cancellation token.

The flag is per-store, not process-global. Each `DistributedRuntime` builds its own `FileStore`, so shutting one runtime down does not disable another runtime's store.

## Validation

Regression tests cover late bucket creation, writes through cached buckets, and a stale bucket attempting to delete a live store's replacement value under a shared root. The shared-root test also checks shutdown cleanup before and after the rejected delete.

Validation commands: `cargo test -p dynamo-runtime --lib storage::kv::file` and the repository's remote Pre Merge and full PR CI workflows. Rust formatting is checked with the pinned Rust 1.96.1 formatter.

The reported flake, at roughly 0.15%, did not reproduce in the original local investigation. These tests cover the directory-recreation and stale-mutation mechanisms; they do not establish that the intermittent CI symptom is eliminated.

title: fix(runtime): release endpoint registrations on rollback and shutdown
body:
## Summary

Endpoint startup published local routing and health state before request-plane and discovery registration finished. If startup failed, or an endpoint shut down, process-wide state could remain visible after the endpoint stopped serving. A restart could then inherit the earlier endpoint's engine, canary target, notifier, or readiness state.

Each endpoint start now owns a scoped registration. Rollback and shutdown release its local engine, health-check target, notifier, readiness entry, discovery record, request-plane handler, and graceful-shutdown registration. Local engines and canary targets carry registration identity, so late cleanup removes only its own state and can re-expose another outstanding registration.

Canary probes carry that identity through completion. Results from released registrations are discarded, and a replacement monitor cannot be marked ready by the outgoing handler. Configured health entries remain `NotReady` after their final target is released; unconfigured entries are removed.

Request-plane routes and cleanup include the namespace, component, endpoint name, and runtime instance ID. Same-named endpoints in different namespaces or components can coexist, and TCP and NATS remove only the requested handler. TCP discovery publishes the complete routing path; NATS retains its existing service-scoped subjects. NATS reserves an instance route before creating its subscription and owns setup through listener shutdown in one task. Unregistration waits for setup cleanup before a replacement can reuse the route. Caller cancellation cancels the owned task while retaining its reservation through cleanup. TCP serializes handler ownership and readiness changes, and keeps a shared endpoint ready until its final handler is removed.

The startup retry path also preserves timeout context when an etcd connection error arrives at the deadline, retaining the underlying error for diagnosis. This keeps deadline reporting consistent with the existing startup-timeout test.

Closes #13475

## Validation

- Rust formatting: `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the changed runtime files.
- Workflow lint: `actionlint` on `.github/workflows/dynamo-pipeline.yml`, with the repository's custom runner labels supplied.
- The Dynamo Pipeline enumerates `component::endpoint::integration_tests` with `cargo test --locked -p dynamo-runtime --features integration --lib`, then runs each test with `--exact --test-threads=1 --nocapture` in its own process against a temporary NATS server. Process isolation prevents reuse of the global TCP server after a prior test runtime shuts down; an empty test list fails the job. This covers failed-start cleanup, same-name restart after shutdown, TCP/NATS namespace and component isolation through selective shutdown, and NATS unregistration during pending or cancelled setup. A runtime unit test also covers concurrent TCP replacement and removal.
- Runtime unit tests and Clippy run in Pre Merge; the remaining integration and GPU validation runs in full CI.

No local tests, builds, or benchmarks were run during this maintenance pass. Validation results are recorded by the current-head GitHub checks.

title: fix(sglang): fail fast when an mm-router worker dies during startup
body:
Source issue: [DYN-4416](https://linear.app/nvidia/issue/DYN-4416).

## Summary

`test_sglang_deployment[mm_agg_router_qwen3.5-0.8b-4]` times out at
`Timeout (>400.0s) from pytest-timeout` when its workers die during startup, not because the
deployment is slow. Recorded failures show both workers dying at CUDA-graph capture with
`Capture cuda graph failed: CUDA error: out of memory`, while `wait_ready` polled `/health` with a
900-second default and no liveness check, so the tree was killed from outside with no engine
error.

## Details:

`wait_ready` in `examples/backends/sglang/launch/agg_multimodal_router.sh` now takes an
absolute deadline. After each unsuccessful backend or frontend readiness probe,
`check_workers_alive` checks every launched worker and reports its exit status if it has died,
ending startup with a non-zero exit. Worker and frontend waits share one `STARTUP_TIMEOUT`
(default 330s), keeping startup inside the serve tests' 400s; the same cap now bounds the other
configurations using this script. Each probe uses the remaining budget, capped at 10 seconds,
so a hung endpoint cannot block worker monitoring indefinitely.

`tests/utils/pytest_parallel_gpu.py` adds `Capture cuda graph failed` to
`_RETRYABLE_INIT_MARKERS`, so that startup-only failure reaches the existing retry path.

This makes each occurrence fast and explained, but does not reduce how often the underlying GPU
memory over-subscription happens; at the reported 0.66% rate the flake is not shown to be gone.

## Validation

On one A100-80GB, killing a worker during startup ends the test in 6.0s on this
branch (`exited with status 137 before becoming ready`), against 407s and a pytest timeout on
base; five healthy runs reached `Frontend ready` inside the cap. The target test still fails here
for a pre-existing reason: its log assertion needs the `mm-routing` bindings feature, built only
in CI.

`wait_ready` in the launch script.

Source issue: [DYN-4417](https://linear.app/nvidia/issue/DYN-4417).

## Summary

`test_slow_ray_times_out_and_still_reports_dp_tp` in the vLLM EP capacity tests failed intermittently in pre-merge CI with `caller waited 0.72s, expected to bail at 0.05s`. It measured wall-clock time around the endpoint call; this replaces that measurement with a direct check of the behaviour it stood for. Test-only — no production file changes.

## Details:

The test patched the endpoint deadline `_EP_CAPACITY_RAY_TIMEOUT_S` to `0.05`, made every stubbed Ray query sleep `0.2s`, and asserted the awaited call returned in under `0.15s`. The event loop runs on one thread, so scheduling delay on a busy runner lands in that measurement, and a shared runner makes no such promise.

`_install_ray_stub` now takes an optional `gate` (a `threading.Event`) that each query blocks on instead of sleeping, capped at 30 seconds. The `delay` path is unchanged, so the file's nine other tests behave as before. The test holds the gate shut for the whole call, so the snapshot cannot finish on its own and only the endpoint's deadline can return a result. It then asserts `handler._ep_capacity_inflight` is present and not done: the caller was released while the GCS query was still outstanding. An `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=5.0)` guard makes a regression fail instead of hang, and a `finally` opens the gate and shuts down the executor the old version leaked.

The test now pins that a bound on the caller's wait exists, not its size.

title: fix(runtime): scope endpoint routing and cleanup by full identity
body:
## Overview:

<!-- Describe your pull request here. Please read the text below the line, and make sure you follow the checklist.-->
Two components in the same `DistributedRuntime` can register an endpoint with the same name, but TCP routing does not distinguish them. The discovery address and server handler key contain only the runtime's instance ID and endpoint name. Registering the second component therefore replaces the first component's handler, and requests addressed to the first endpoint reach the second handler with a successful ACK.

This change includes the namespace and component in the TCP path and uses the full endpoint identity during cleanup. The collision requires a shared instance ID; workers with different instance IDs do not collide in this way.

## Details:

<!-- Describe the changes made in this PR. -->
### Changes and compatibility

TCP address construction and ingress registration now share the path:

```text
<instance-id>/<namespace>/<component>/<endpoint>
```

Both discovery-registration rollback and normal shutdown pass the full `EndpointId` to unregister the matching handler. The NATS implementation uses `(EndpointId, instance_id)` for its task map as well, so the shared cleanup interface does not discard component identity. NATS subjects are unchanged.

Existing TCP clients already retain everything after the address's first slash and forward it as the request path, so no client parser change is required for the new address format. Mixed-version deployments were not tested.

The existing TCP regression test now varies one identity field at a time: instance ID, namespace, component, or endpoint name. It checks delivery to the first handler after both registrations, delivery to the surviving handler after removal, and an unavailable ACK for the removed endpoint. This extends the existing test without adding a test file.

### Reproduction

The local reproduction used in-memory discovery and real loopback TCP connections, with two endpoints started through `endpoint_builder().handler(...).start_with_registration()`:

1. Start `audit/first/generate` and send a request to its advertised address. The first handler receives it.
2. Start `audit/second/generate` in the same runtime.
3. Send another request to the first endpoint's address. The ACK succeeds, but the second handler receives the payload.

Both endpoints had the same `host:port/<instance-id>/generate` address. The handler observations produced this assertion failure:

```text
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: Some("second")
 right: Some("first")
```

Changing only the second endpoint's name to `other` made the control case pass. No model inference was involved; the reproduction checked which handler actually received the request.

With the fix, a separate check using the public startup API verified distinct advertised addresses and delivery to the first handler after both endpoints were registered. Shutting down the first endpoint also left the second endpoint callable.

### Validation

- Public startup API check over loopback TCP: passed.
- Runtime library unit suite, run serially using the compiled test executable: **745 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored**.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p dynamo-runtime --lib --tests -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check`: passed.

The regression included in this PR can be run with:

```bash
cargo test --locked -p dynamo-runtime --lib \
  unregister_endpoint_removes_only_the_matching_endpoint_instance
```

NATS task bookkeeping was reviewed and compiled, but was not tested against a live broker.

## Where should the reviewer start?

<!-- call out specific files that should be looked at closely -->
- `lib/runtime/src/transports/tcp.rs` and `lib/runtime/src/component/endpoint.rs`: shared TCP path construction and cleanup call sites.
- `lib/runtime/src/pipeline/network/ingress/shared_tcp_endpoint.rs`: handler registration, removal, and the expanded regression test.
- `lib/runtime/src/pipeline/network/ingress/unified_server.rs` and `lib/runtime/src/pipeline/network/ingress/nats_server.rs`: full-identity cleanup interface and NATS task lookup.
