title: fix(frontend): render the chat template off the async runtime
body:
## Overview:

`OpenAIPreprocessor::apply_template` renders the chat template synchronously on the tokio worker thread that runs the request. Tokenization was moved to the blocking pool for this reason (see the comment on `encode_with_timing`), but the render was not. In internal testing with a burst of a few thousand long conversations, the renders saturate the runtime's worker threads and hyper's I/O tasks stop being scheduled: request bodies stay unread in kernel receive buffers (we measured up to ~74 MB across ~600 sockets), the receive windows close, and clients with a TCP user timeout abort the upload before the frontend ever reads it.

## Details:

- New `off_runtime()` helper: on the multi-thread runtime it wraps the closure in `tokio::task::block_in_place`, which hands the current worker to the blocking pool and lets tokio start a replacement worker for the async tasks; on the current-thread runtime (unit tests) it runs inline, since `block_in_place` is not available there.
- `preprocess_request_with_options` renders the template through it. Nothing else changes; `TEMPLATE_SECONDS` still measures the render.
- `block_in_place` is used rather than `spawn_blocking` because `apply_template` borrows the request generically (`&R`), so there is no `'static` value to move into a spawned closure.

## Where should the reviewer start?

- `lib/llm/src/preprocessor.rs`: `off_runtime` and its single call site in `preprocess_request_with_options`.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p dynamo-llm --lib -- preprocessor`: 211 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p dynamo-llm --no-deps --lib -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

title: fix(frontend): make the HTTP listen backlog configurable, default 4096
body:
## Overview:

The frontend HTTP listener is created with `tokio::net::TcpListener::bind`, which listens with a backlog of 128 (tokio copies the Rust standard library default). When a few thousand clients open connections within a few seconds, the accept queue overflows before the accept loop drains it. On hosts with `net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies=1` and `tcp_abort_on_overflow=0`, an overflowed handshake is not retried: the final ACK is dropped and the client's first data segment is answered with a RST, which the client sees as `Connection reset by peer`. We found this in internal testing with a load client that opens one connection per session.

## Details:

- `bind_listener()` in `service_v2.rs` builds the socket with `tokio::net::TcpSocket`, sets `SO_REUSEADDR` (what `TcpListener::bind` also does), binds, and listens with a configurable backlog.
- New environment variable `DYN_HTTP_LISTEN_BACKLOG`, default 4096. The kernel caps the effective value at `net.core.somaxconn`. Zero, negative or unparseable values fall back to the default.
- Only the main HTTP listener changes. Callers that pass a pre-bound listener (`run_with_listener` / `spawn_with_listener`) are unaffected.
- Docs: one `ParamField` in `frontend-configuration.mdx`; constant registered in `environment_names.rs`.

## Where should the reviewer start?

- `lib/llm/src/http/service/service_v2.rs`: `bind_listener`, `parse_listen_backlog`, and the call site in `run_inner`.
- `lib/runtime/src/config/environment_names.rs`: `DYN_HTTP_LISTEN_BACKLOG`.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p dynamo-llm --lib -- listen_backlog bind_listener`: `test_listen_backlog_env_var` (default, zero, invalid, whitespace-padded value) and `test_bind_listener_accepts_connections` (bind on an ephemeral port, connect, accept) pass.
- Internal testing, single frontend, a load client ramping 2,542 new TCP connections over 10 s on a host with `tcp_syncookies=1`: before this change 12-29 connections per run failed with `Connection reset by peer`; with it, 0 resets across the same ramp.
- `cargo clippy -p dynamo-llm -p dynamo-runtime --no-deps --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

title: fix(frontend): observe audit metrics before non-streaming fold
body:
## Overview

With request-payload capture enabled, non-streaming chat responses are folded into one chunk, dropping the per-chunk metrics needed by the frontend collector. Recovering only the final annotation cannot restore TTFT/ITL: those measurements depend on when chunks are observed.

This fix forwards metrics as chunks arrive while buffering response content, and places the observer before the backend-error preflight.

## Details

- `fold_aggregate_with_future` moves typed metrics with `take()` into metric-only carriers, avoiding cloning and JSON round-trips. Legacy `llm_metrics` / `payload_usage` annotations pass through as data-less shells, separately from their payload data.
- Each source chunk yields at most one observable metrics frame. A chunk carrying both typed `llm_metrics` and a `payload_usage` annotation (the tool-call jail produces this shape) forwards the typed frame only, the precedence the streaming path already applies. On such a chunk the annotation's `cached_tokens` is not observed; the unfolded stream behaves the same, which the test's control leg pins.
- Non-streaming chat and non-streaming `/v1/responses` both use fold → observe metrics → `check_for_backend_error` → aggregate, so preflight buffering cannot delay metric observation.
- The folded response carries no `llm_metrics`, preventing replay of observations. Response content, usage and `id`/`model`/`created` remain available to HTTP aggregation and request-payload capture.

The issue's former `audit/stream.rs` path is now `lib/llm/src/request_trace/payload_stream.rs`.

## Validation

- Fold tests cover typed and event-tagged metrics under both tags, frame order, a zero-token `payload_usage` tail carrying its production tag, a dual-carrier chunk (one observable frame), response aggregation, identity fields and the no-metrics case.
- Collector tests (`http::service::metrics::tests::fold_regression`) drive fold → observe → preflight → aggregate and assert output-token totals, ISL/OSL/cached counts and sums, TTFT/ITL sample counts, and response `id`/`model`/`created`; the dual-carrier chunk is observed once (OSL 5, not the annotation's 3); plain, scan and fold paths produce identical metric signatures on the same chunk vector.
- `tests/http_metrics.rs::test_non_streaming_observes_metrics_before_backend_error_preflight` drives the real handler: the engine holds its first data chunk behind a gate, and TTFT must be exposed on `/metrics` while the leading metrics frame is still held by the preflight.
- Mutation matrix at 25f8628 (each mutation reverted afterwards):
  - two independent `if`s restored in the fold → `test_fold_dual_carrier_chunk_yields_one_metrics_frame`, `test_non_streaming_fold_observes_dual_carrier_chunk_once` fail
  - `ANNOTATION_PAYLOAD_USAGE` arm removed → `test_fold_forwards_metric_frames_before_folded_chunk`, `test_non_streaming_fold_preserves_chunk_metrics` (`cached_tokens` n=0), `test_metrics_parity_across_payload_capture_modes` fail
  - `openai.rs` handler order reverted to check → observe → `test_non_streaming_observes_metrics_before_backend_error_preflight` times out
- Local gate: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --lib --tests`, `cargo clippy --lib --tests -D warnings`; test groups: `request_trace::payload_stream` 10 passed, `fold_regression` 3 passed, `http_metrics` handler test 1 passed.
- Recorded mocker smoke check with payload capture enabled (from 2b8a915, unchanged code path): a 32-token non-streaming response produced output tokens +32, TTFT samples +1, ITL samples +31, and a complete payload record.

## Where should the reviewer start?

Round 3 is the single commit 25f8628 on top of the rebase: the `else if` in `fold_aggregate_with_future`, the `/v1/responses` reorder in `openai.rs`, `mod fold_regression` in `metrics.rs`, and the gated-engine test in `tests/http_metrics.rs`.

For the full fix, start with `fold_aggregate_with_future` in `payload_stream.rs`, then the non-streaming handler in `openai.rs` and `test_non_streaming_fold_preserves_chunk_metrics` in `metrics.rs`.

## Related Issues

Closes #11349

---

## Commit message (already on the branch as 25f8628, for reference)

```
fix(frontend): observe dual-carrier audit chunks once and pin the handler order

fold_aggregate_with_future forwarded both the typed llm_metrics and the event
annotation of a chunk that carries both, so the collector observed that chunk
twice and the zero-token payload_usage annotation overwrote the final OSL. Typed
metrics now take precedence over the annotation on the same chunk, the
precedence the streaming path already applies. /v1/responses non-streaming
observes metrics ahead of the backend-error preflight, matching non-streaming
chat.

Tests: fold boundary (production payload_usage tag, legacy llm_metrics frame,
dual-carrier chunk yields one observable frame); collector (dual-carrier
observed once with OSL 5, id/model/created through the fold, plain/scan/fold
parity); real handler in tests/http_metrics.rs (TTFT observed while the leading
frame sits in the preflight buffer). Verified with fmt/check/clippy -D warnings,
the three test groups, and mutations (independent ifs, dropped payload_usage
arm, reverted handler order) each failing the tests that pin them.
```

title: ci(release): push GA Helm charts to NGC OCI as well as ChartMuseum
body: The nightly helm step dual-pushes to ChartMuseum and to oci://nvcr.io//ai-dynamo. The GA step never did, it only cm-pushes, so every released chart through 1.4.0 exists in ChartMuseum but not in OCI, and consumers on OCI-only registries such as ACR, ECR and Harbor cannot mirror them. Push the same packaged tarball to the OCI mirror after the ChartMuseum push succeeds. helm does not read docker's credentials for OCI, so this needs its own registry login. Fail-soft on purpose: ChartMuseum is the primary distribution channel and has already succeeded by that point, so an OCI hiccup must not fail the release. It cannot ship silently either, since the GitLab publish:helm-oci:ondemand job probes for the OCI copy and refuses to file the publishing MR without it. Closes #OPS-8338 --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Helm charts are now published to both ChartMuseum and the NGC OCI repository during GA releases. * NGC publishing issues generate warnings without blocking the overall release.

title: ci: mirror CI images to us-east-1 ECR
body:
## Summary

- mirror pushed Dynamo CI runtime and test images from the primary ECR registry to `us-east-1`
- copy the already-built OCI image and its tags instead of rebuilding in each region
- verify source and destination ECR digests match before mirrored images are considered ready

This draft is the east-local image phase of the production-east rollout. The initial `prod-tester-amd-gpu-4-v2` canary in Velonix #655 will continue pulling from west so runner validation is not blocked on regional image publishing.

## Iterative rollout plan

### Phase 1: runner canary using west images

1. Merge and reconcile Velonix #655 with only `prod-tester-amd-gpu-4-v2` present and suspended.
2. Confirm the east cluster can pull the existing coordinator and workflow images from `us-west-2`.
3. Resume the east runner Kustomization and validate one four-GPU smoke job.
4. Validate burst, queueing, and capacity-failure behavior without changing west.

Cross-region pulls prove the east runner path, but do not establish regional image resilience.

### Phase 2: canary east-local publishing

1. Provision the `ai-dynamo/dynamo` ECR repository in `us-east-1` through Velonix Terraform.
2. Grant the existing builder role push access and east runner nodes pull access.
3. Mirror one on-demand GPU test image and require matching west/east digests.
4. Pull the east image from a fresh east pod or node to avoid a cached-image false positive.
5. Keep this PR in draft until the live copy and pull validation succeeds.

### Phase 3: expand and cut over

1. Enable mirroring incrementally for the required PR, post-merge, and nightly image builds.
2. Switch the east runner/workflow image references to the east ECR hostname.
3. Repeat smoke, burst, queueing, capacity-failure, and regional-failover tests.
4. Expand to other runner families only after the four-GPU path is stable.

## Dependencies

- Velonix Terraform must provision the east ECR repository and IAM permissions.
- Velonix #655 remains west-image-first for the initial runner canary.
- The final east cutover must update the cluster image references only after digest and pull validation.

body:
## Overview

SGLang HiCache stores one logical page as several per-pool Mooncake objects, keyed as `{key_prefix}_{page_hash}{suffix}` (for DeepSeek V4 these are `__deepseek_v4_c4`, `__deepseek_v4_c4_indexer`, `__deepseek_v4_c4_state`, `__deepseek_v4_c128`, `__deepseek_v4_c4_indexer_state`, `__swa`). The router previously guessed a TP/PP/MLA `_k`/`_v` layout and required every pool on every page, so for hybrid / multi-subpool models the shared-cache (L3) query keys never matched the keys the worker actually stored, and lookups always missed — independent of whether the event stream was healthy. This PR lets the worker advertise its concrete per-pool layout so the router reconstructs the real keys and applies each pool's own hit policy; it is backward compatible and a no-op for models that don't advertise one.

The SGLang-side producer that emits this layout is sgl-project/sglang#40467 (`GET /get_hicache_l3_cache_layout`); the two changes are independent and can land in either order.

## Details

- Add an optional `hicache_object_layout` to the SGLang HiCache Mooncake runtime config (`#[serde(default)]`, so older workers that don't send it are unaffected). Each pool advertises its key `suffixes`, a `hit_policy` (`all_pages` / `trailing_pages`), and for trailing pools the `trailing_pages` window size, following SGLang's `PoolHitPolicy` semantics. The layout also carries `key_prefix`, the prefix Mooncake actually tags every object with (backend tag plus model name) — `extra_backend_tag` alone omits the model name, so keys built from it never matched.
- When the layout is advertised, `required_page_keys` builds the query keys for a given page from the pools that cover it: `all_pages` pools on every page, `trailing_pages` pools only on the last N pages. This fixes the previous all-or-nothing `.all()` check, which scored every leading page of a hybrid sequence as a miss because the sliding-window state pools never store leading pages.
- When no layout is advertised, the existing `_k`/`_v` derived behavior is unchanged.
- Include the layout in `has_same_layout` so a layout change re-clears cached hits.


## Where should the reviewer start?

- `lib/llm/src/kv_router/shared_cache.rs`: `HicacheObjectLayout` / `HicacheObjectPool` / `covers_page` (trailing-page scoping), and `required_page_keys` (key reconstruction per page).
- Tests: `test_required_page_keys_uses_advertised_key_prefix` (prefix precedence over `extra_backend_tag`), `test_required_page_keys_scopes_trailing_pool_to_trailing_pages`, and `test_check_blocks_does_not_require_trailing_pool_on_leading_pages` (end-to-end: events in, hits out).


## Validation

- `cargo test -p dynamo-llm --lib shared_cache` — 27 passed (5 new tests). `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- Cross-checked the page-hash reconstruction against SGLang's `SHA256(prior_digest ‖ u32-LE tokens)` scheme (independent recompute matches the test vectors), and the generated keys match SGLang's `_get_hybrid_page_component_keys` output for the single-PP DeepSeek V4 case.
- Not yet validated end-to-end (needs a live DeepSeek V4 + Mooncake deployment); the SGLang-side producer is being prepared as a companion change.


## Related Issues

**🚫 This PR is NOT linked to an issue**:
- [x] Confirmed — no related issue. Companion change: sgl-project/sglang#40467 (the SGLang-side producer of this layout).

## Note

Prepared with AI assistance; I reviewed every line and ran the tests listed above. I searched the tracker (`pool_key_suffixes`, `expand_actual_query_keys`, `shared_cache mooncake`, etc.) and found no existing PR for multi-subpool key reconstruction. This builds directly on the now-merged #11239 ("feat(kv-router): index Mooncake KV events"), which introduced the Mooncake KV-event index and `expand_actual_query_keys` with the `_k`/`_v` layout; this PR extends that path to multi-subpool models. Happy to link or close as duplicate if I missed something.

title: fix(router): account for all output blocks in response chunks
body:
## Overview:

<!-- Describe your pull request here. Please read the text below the line, and make sure you follow the checklist.-->

With `--router-track-output-blocks` enabled, the router undercounts output blocks when a response chunk crosses more than one block boundary. 
This makes its local decode-load estimate depend on how the backend groups tokens into responses.

`OutputBlockTracker` advances its total to include all newly crossed blocks, but `RequestGuard` sends only one `AddOutputBlock` update. Later chunks cannot recover the missing blocks because the tracker has already advanced.

The fix carries the number of new blocks in `OutputBlockUpdate` and enqueues an update for each through the existing booking-checked scheduler path. 
It leaves the decay formula, cleanup, and local-only load updates unchanged. Output-block tracking remains disabled by default; no backend or wire-format changes are needed.


## Details:

<!-- Describe the changes made in this PR. -->

The regression uses the actual request guard and scheduler, without GPU inference. 
For a 16-token prompt, 48 output tokens, and block size 16, single-token chunks count 4 blocks before and after the fix. Grouping the same tokens as `[1, 32, 15]` exposes the bug. 
SGLang's real output accumulator also produces this layout with `stream_interval=32` in the CPU producer probe.

Recorded output for the grouped case:

**Before** — the regression fails:

```text
track_output_blocks=true prompt_tokens=16 output_tokens=48 block_size=16 chunks=[1, 32, 15] initial_blocks=1 observed_blocks=3 expected_blocks=4
```

**After** — the same regression passes:

```text
track_output_blocks=true prompt_tokens=16 output_tokens=48 block_size=16 chunks=[1, 32, 15] initial_blocks=1 observed_blocks=4 expected_blocks=4
```

title: perf(mocker): parallelize conservative replay windows
body:
## Summary

This draft adds an opt-in conservative parallel runtime for aggregated offline replay. Logical workers execute independently on persistent CPU lanes between known trace-arrival boundaries. The coordinator keeps routing, admission, collector updates, sequence allocation, and output publication serial and deterministic.

Enable the prototype with:

```shell
DYN_MOCKER_OFFLINE_AGG_PARALLEL_THREADS=12
```

Unset or `0` keeps the existing serial runtime unchanged. The parallel path does not use snapshots, journals, speculative state, or rollback. It stops every worker at a known causality boundary and falls back to exact serial stepping while the router backlog is non-empty.

On the Astra DeepSeek-V4-Flash point workload, 12 lanes improved replay throughput by **2.210x for SGLang** and **2.199x for vLLM**.

## Overview

The existing offline runtime processes the global event heap serially even when logical workers have no shared state before the next trace arrival. This change isolates worker-owned epoch execution, then uses conservative safe windows to run those independent epochs in parallel.

The feature is intentionally private and opt-in while the implementation is reviewed. It supports static aggregated replay with native vLLM or SGLang KV state, DP1 or attention DP, and round-robin or KV routing. Unsupported modes fail early when the environment variable is enabled.

## Details

- Isolate each logical worker and all its DP ranks behind a raw epoch boundary.
- Keep attention-DP ranks for one logical worker together and retain the existing shared slowest-rank boundary.
- Use persistent worker lanes with stable worker assignment.
- Stream bounded, recycled 64-epoch chunks through per-lane `ArrayQueue`s.
- Merge worker actions in the coordinator using the existing timestamp, sequence, worker, and rank ordering.
- Apply completions before arrivals at the same horizon.
- Keep the serial runtime as the exact disabled path.
- Record counters for safe windows, chunks, epochs, coordinator wait/merge time, lane work, and queue stalls.

## Performance

These are single point measurements. They are not statistical claims. The host was idle during each accepted preflight, but CPUs were not kernel-isolated. There were no warm-ups or repeated rounds.

Baseline was Dynamo `5c950bf90fcfd15209f9501c8bd0652e5a21bda8`. The measured candidate was `d3e7d40cc2c4ac127be91a049f91c45d3dbcd8c8`; the two commits in this PR have the same tracked source tree. Every Astra cell used AIC `ed13cfc2c8e8892d2a039dfa8eceed1885012e05`.

Configuration: 12 aggregated workers, 12 parallel lanes, DeepSeek-V4-Flash on B200, TP4/attention-DP1, MoE TP1/EP4, native KV state, KV routing/events, and CPUs 0-13. SGLang used HYBRID AIC and vLLM used SILICON AIC. Every cell completed 93,953 requests and processed 1,290,416,132 tokens.

| Backend | Serial wall time | 12-lane wall time | Serial tokens/s | 12-lane tokens/s | Speedup | Wall-time reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SGLang | 25.9995 s | 11.7659 s | 49,632,289 | 109,673,793 | **2.210x** | **54.75%** |
| vLLM | 25.5513 s | 11.6213 s | 50,502,925 | 111,038,936 | **2.199x** | **54.52%** |

The final SGLang profile kept the coordinator to 12.46% of sampled P-core cycles. `ArrayQueue::pop` was 0.10% of total P-core cycles. The remaining main limit is the global arrival barrier: 91,674 safe windows yielded only about 2.3 epochs per worker per window.

## Validation

The exact candidate source tree passed:

- `cargo test -p dynamo-mocker replay::offline` — 200 passed
- `cargo test -p dynamo-mocker` — 731 passed
- `cargo check --manifest-path lib/bindings/python/Cargo.toml --features aic-forward-pass`
- `cargo clippy -p dynamo-mocker --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `git diff --check`

Aggregate correctness used 24 independent processes: baseline serial, candidate one-lane, and candidate four-lane runs, each repeated twice across vLLM/SGLang and KV/round-robin routing. Every report completed 5,000 requests. All six reports in each backend/router row were byte-identical after removing only wall-clock-derived fields.

KVBM was not tested because this opt-in path rejects KVBM/offload. Disaggregated replay continues to use the unchanged serial runtime and was outside this aggregate-only parity matrix.

## Where should the reviewer start?

Start with `lib/mocker/src/replay/offline/conservative.rs`, then review the worker-epoch boundary in `lib/mocker/src/replay/offline/components/engine.rs` and the opt-in dispatch in `lib/mocker/src/replay/offline/agg.rs`.

title: fix(runtime): scope shared TCP server to Tokio runtime
body:
## Overview

Scope the shared TCP request-plane server to the Tokio runtime that owns its background tasks. This prevents a later runtime in the same process from inheriting a cached server whose executor has already stopped, while preserving server sharing between network managers on the same runtime.

## Details

- Store the shared server, actual bound port, and lifetime token in a per-Tokio-runtime scope.
- Prune dead weak scope entries when creating a replacement, so repeated runtime creation cannot grow the registry without bound.
- Always initialize the TCP server and publish the actual port reported by the same `NetworkManager`; endpoint discovery no longer re-reads `DYN_TCP_RPC_PORT` after configuration was captured.
- Keep the scope token independent of any individual manager token. Multiple distributed runtimes can share one Tokio runtime, so shutting down one manager must not stop the listener used by its siblings.
- Isolate the TCP lifecycle tests from an externally configured `DYN_TCP_RPC_PORT` and cover same-runtime sharing, runtime teardown/recreation, stale-entry pruning, and sibling survival after one manager token is cancelled.

Each live Tokio runtime owns a distinct listener. Concurrent runtimes in one process must therefore use OS-assigned or otherwise distinct ports; restoring cross-runtime listener sharing would reintroduce stale executor ownership.

## Where should the reviewer start?

- `lib/runtime/src/pipeline/network/manager.rs`: runtime scope ownership, registry pruning, and lifecycle regressions.
- `lib/runtime/src/component/endpoint.rs`: actual bound-port publication.

title: fix(runtime): stop discovery daemon reflector tasks on every exit path
body:
Overview:
Fixes a task/resource leak in the Kubernetes discovery daemon: two long-lived reflector tasks were spawned and never stopped, so they (and the Kubernetes watch connections they held) outlived the daemon itself.

Details:
DiscoverySource::new spawns the readiness reflector (an EndpointSlice watcher in pod mode, or a Pod watcher in container mode) and discards its JoinHandle. DiscoveryDaemon::run separately spawns the DynamoWorkerMetadata CR reflector and discards that handle too. Neither task ever observes the daemon's cancellation token, so every exit path from run() — cancellation, or either reflector channel closing — left both tasks running detached, each still holding its Kubernetes watch stream, reflector writer, and client state.

DiscoverySource::new now returns its reflector's JoinHandle instead of discarding it; the CR reflector's handle is captured the same way.
run()'s main loop is restructured to yield its outcome via break rather than bailing out directly from inside the loop, so every exit path (cancellation or either channel closing) reaches a single cleanup point instead of skipping it.
A new stop_reflector_tasks helper aborts both handles and awaits them, so returning from run() means both watches have actually stopped, not just that the loop did.
Added a regression test that exercises stop_reflector_tasks directly against two tasks that would otherwise run forever, standing in for the reflector loops — it hangs instead of returning if abort is only requested and never awaited, or a handle is dropped instead of joined.
Note on the issue's suggested regression coverage: the issue asked for a test using synthetic Kubernetes watch streams, but this crate has no existing mock-kube::Client test infrastructure to build that on safely. Rather than introduce untested mocking machinery for it, the added test covers the actual mechanism (stop_reflector_tasks) directly.

Where should the reviewer start?
stop_reflector_tasks and the loop restructuring in DiscoveryDaemon::run, both in lib/runtime/src/discovery/kube/daemon.rs. The DiscoverySource::new signature change is mechanical (returns the handle alongside Self).

Related Issues

Closes #13874
